1.15.s:
sūta uvāca
prajāḥ sṛjeti vyādiṣṭaḥ pūrvaṃ dakṣaḥ svayaṃbhuvā /
sasarja devān gandharvān ṛṣīṃścaivāsuroragān //
1.15.d:
सूत उवाच
प्रजाः सृजेति व्यादिष्टः पूर्वं दक्षः स्वयंभुवा ।
ससर्ज देवान् गन्धर्वान् ऋषींश्चैवासुरोरगान् ॥
1.15.m: Sūta said: / Formerly directed by the Self-born One, "Create living beings!" / Dakṣa created the gods, Gandharvas, seers, asuras, and serpents.

1.15.s:
yadāsya sṛjamānasya na vyavardhanta tāḥ prajāḥ /
tadā sasarja bhūtāni maithunenaiva dharmataḥ //
1.15.d:
यदास्य सृजमानस्य न व्यवर्धन्त ताः प्रजाः ।
तदा ससर्ज भूतानि मैथुनेनैव धर्मतः ॥
1.15.m: When those creatures he was creating did not multiply, / then, in accordance with righteousness, he created living beings through sexual union alone.

1.15.s:
asiknyāṃ janayāmāsa vīraṇasya prajāpateḥ /
sutāyāṃ dharmayuktāyāṃ putrāṇāṃ tu sahastrakam //
1.15.d:
असिक्न्यां जनयामास वीरणस्य प्रजापतेः ।
सुतायां धर्मयुक्तायां पुत्राणां तु सहस्त्रकम् ॥
1.15.m: Upon Asiknī, the virtuous daughter of the progenitor Vīraṇa, / he fathered a thousand sons.

1.15.s:
teṣu putreṣu naṣṭeṣu māyayā nāradasya saḥ /
ṣaṣṭiṃ dakṣo 'sṛjat kanyā vairaṇyāṃ vai prajāpatiḥ //
1.15.d:
तेषु पुत्रेषु नष्टेषु मायया नारदस्य सः ।
षष्टिं दक्षो ऽसृजत् कन्या वैरण्यां वै प्रजापतिः ॥
1.15.m: When those sons perished through the illusory power of Nārada, / Dakṣa, the progenitor, created sixty daughters upon the daughter of Vīraṇa.

1.15.s:
dadau sa daśa dharmāya kaśyapāya trayodaśa /
viṃśat sapta ca somāya catastro 'riṣṭanemine //
1.15.d:
ददौ स दश धर्माय कश्यपाय त्रयोदश ।
विंशत् सप्त च सोमाय चतस्त्रो ऽरिष्टनेमिने ॥
1.15.m: He gave ten to Dharma, thirteen to Kaśyapa, / twenty-seven to Soma, and four to Ariṣṭanemi,

1.15.s:
dve caiva bahuputrāya dve kṛśāśvāya dhīmate /
dve caivāṅgirase tadvat tāsāṃ vakṣye 'tha nistaram //
1.15.d:
द्वे चैव बहुपुत्राय द्वे कृशाश्वाय धीमते ।
द्वे चैवाङ्गिरसे तद्वत् तासां वक्ष्ये ऽथ निस्तरम् ॥
1.15.m: two to Bahuputra, two to the wise Kṛśāśva, / and likewise two to Aṅgiras; I shall now relate them in full detail.

1.15.s:
arundhatī vasurjāmī lambā bhānurmarutvatī /
saṃkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvā ca bhāminī //
1.15.d:
अरुन्धती वसुर्जामी लम्बा भानुर्मरुत्वती ।
संकल्पा च मुहूर्ता च साध्या विश्वा च भामिनी ॥
1.15.m: Arundhatī, Vasu, Jāmī, Lambā, Bhānu, Marutvatī, / Saṃkalpā, Muhūrtā, Sādhyā, and the beautiful Viśvā—

1.15.s:
dharmapatnyo daśa tvetāstāsāṃ putrān nibodhata /
viśvāyā viśvadevāstu sādhyā sādhyānajījanat //
1.15.d:
धर्मपत्न्यो दश त्वेतास्तासां पुत्रान् निबोधत ।
विश्वाया विश्वदेवास्तु साध्या साध्यानजीजनत् ॥
1.15.m: these were the ten wives of Dharma; hear about their sons: / Viśvā gave birth to the Viśvedevas, and Sādhyā to the Sādhyas.

1.15.s:
marutvanto marutvatyāṃ vasavo 'ṣṭau vasoḥ sutāḥ /
bhānostu bhānavaścaiva muhūrtā vai muhūrtajāḥ //
1.15.d:
मरुत्वन्तो मरुत्वत्यां वसवो ऽष्टौ वसोः सुताः ।
भानोस्तु भानवश्चैव मुहूर्ता वै मुहूर्तजाः ॥
1.15.m: The Marutvants were born of Marutvatī, and the eight Vasus were the sons of Vasu; / the Bhānus were the sons of Bhānu, and the Muhūrtas were born of Muhūrtā.

1.15.s:
lambāyāścātha ghoṣo vai nāgavīthī tu jāmijā /
pṛthivīviṣayaṃ sarvamarundatyāmajāyata /
saṃkalpāyāstu saṃkalpo dharmaputrā daśa smṛtāḥ //
1.15.d:
लम्बायाश्चाथ घोषो वै नागवीथी तु जामिजा ।
पृथिवीविषयं सर्वमरुन्दत्यामजायत ।
संकल्पायास्तु संकल्पो धर्मपुत्रा दश स्मृताः ॥
1.15.m: Ghoṣa was the son of Lambā, and the Nāgavīthī was born of Jāmī; / everything pertaining to the earth was born of Arundhatī, / and Saṃkalpa was born of Saṃkalpā; these are recorded as the ten sons of Dharma.

1.15.s:
āpo dhruvaśca somaśca dharaścaivānilo 'nalaḥ /
pratyūṣaśca prabhāsaśca vasavo 'ṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ //
1.15.d:
आपो ध्रुवश्च सोमश्च धरश्चैवानिलो ऽनलः ।
प्रत्यूषश्च प्रभासश्च वसवो ऽष्टौ प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
1.15.m: Āpa, Dhruva, Soma, Dhara, Anila, Anala, / Pratyūṣa, and Prabhāsa are celebrated as the eight Vasus.

1.15.s:
āpasya putro vaitaṇḍyaḥ śramaḥ śrānto dhunistathā /
dhruvasya putro bhagavān kālo lokaprakālanaḥ //
1.15.d:
आपस्य पुत्रो वैतण्ड्यः श्रमः श्रान्तो धुनिस्तथा ।
ध्रुवस्य पुत्रो भगवान् कालो लोकप्रकालनः ॥
1.15.m: The sons of Āpa were Vaitaṇḍya, Śrama, Śrānta, and Dhuni; / the son of Dhruva was the lord Kāla, who drives the worlds along.

1.15.s:
somasya bhagavān varcā dharasya draviṇaḥ sutaḥ /
purojavo 'nilasya syādavijñātagatistathā //
1.15.d:
सोमस्य भगवान् वर्चा धरस्य द्रविणः सुतः ।
पुरोजवो ऽनिलस्य स्यादविज्ञातगतिस्तथा ॥
1.15.m: The son of Soma was the glorious Varcas, and Draviṇa was the son of Dhara; / Purojava and Avijñātagati were the sons of Anila.

1.15.s:
kumāro hyanalasyāsīt senāpatiriti smṛtaḥ /
devalo bhagavān yogī pratyūṣasyābhavat sutaḥ /
viśvakarmā prabhāsasya śilpakartā prajāpatiḥ //
1.15.d:
कुमारो ह्यनलस्यासीत् सेनापतिरिति स्मृतः ।
देवलो भगवान् योगी प्रत्यूषस्याभवत् सुतः ।
विश्वकर्मा प्रभासस्य शिल्पकर्ता प्रजापतिः ॥
1.15.m: Kumāra, renowned as the commander of the army, was the son of Anala; / the lord and yogin Devala was the son of Pratyūṣa; / and Viśvakarman, the creator of arts and progenitor, was the son of Prabhāsa.

1.15.s:
aditirditirdanustadvadariṣṭā surasā tathā /
surabhirvinatā caiva tāmra krodhavaśā irā /
kadrurmuniśca dharmajñā tatputrān vai nibodhata //
1.15.d:
अदितिर्दितिर्दनुस्तद्वदरिष्टा सुरसा तथा ।
सुरभिर्विनता चैव ताम्र क्रोधवशा इरा ।
कद्रुर्मुनिश्च धर्मज्ञा तत्पुत्रान् वै निबोधत ॥
1.15.m: Aditi, Diti, Danu, likewise Ariṣṭā, and Surasā, / Surabhī, Vinatā, Tāmrā, Krodhavaśā, Irā, / Kadru, and Muni who knew righteousness; hear now of their sons.

1.15.s:
aṃśo dhātā bhagastvaṣṭā mitro 'tha varuṇor'yamā /
vivasvān savitā pūṣā hyaṃśumān viṣṇureva ca //
1.15.d:
अंशो धाता भगस्त्वष्टा मित्रो ऽथ वरुणोर्ऽयमा ।
विवस्वान् सविता पूषा ह्यंशुमान् विष्णुरेव च ॥
1.15.m: Aṃśa, Dhātṛ, Bhaga, Tvaṣṭṛ, Mitra, Varuṇa, Aryaman, / Vivasvant, Savitṛ, Pūṣan, Aṃśumant, and Viṣṇu.

1.15.s:
tuṣitā nāma te pūrvaṃ cākṣuṣasyāntare manoḥ /
vaivasvate 'ntare proktā ādityāścāditeḥ sutāḥ //
1.15.d:
तुषिता नाम ते पूर्वं चाक्षुषस्यान्तरे मनोः ।
वैवस्वते ऽन्तरे प्रोक्ता आदित्याश्चादितेः सुताः ॥
1.15.m: Formerly, in the era of the Cākṣuṣa Manu, they were called the Tuṣitas; / in the era of Vaivasvata, they are proclaimed as the Ādityas, the sons of Aditi.

1.15.s:
ditiḥ putradvayaṃ lebhe kaśyapād balasaṃyutam /
hiraṇyakaśipuṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ hiraṇyākṣaṃ tathāparam //
1.15.d:
दितिः पुत्रद्वयं लेभे कश्यपाद् बलसंयुतम् ।
हिरण्यकशिपुं ज्येष्ठं हिरण्याक्षं तथापरम् ॥
1.15.m: Diti obtained two powerful sons from Kaśyapa: / Hiraṇyakaśipu, the elder, and Hiraṇyākṣa, the other.

1.15.s:
hiraṇyakaśipurdaityo mahābalaparākramaḥ /
ārādhya tapasā devaṃ brahmāṇaṃ parameṣṭhinam /
dṛṣṭvālebhevarān divyān stutvāsau vividhaiḥ stavai //
1.15.d:
हिरण्यकशिपुर्दैत्यो महाबलपराक्रमः ।
आराध्य तपसा देवं ब्रह्माणं परमेष्ठिनम् ।
दृष्ट्वालेभेवरान् दिव्यान् स्तुत्वासौ विविधैः स्तवै ॥
1.15.m: The Daitya Hiraṇyakaśipu, endowed with great strength and valor, / propitiated through austerity the god Brahmā, the supreme lord, / and having seen him and praised him with diverse hymns, obtained divine boons.

1.15.s:
atha tasya balād devāḥ sarva eva surarṣayaḥ /
bādhitāstāḍitā jagmurdevadevaṃ pitāmaham //
1.15.d:
अथ तस्य बलाद् देवाः सर्व एव सुरर्षयः ।
बाधितास्ताडिता जग्मुर्देवदेवं पितामहम् ॥
1.15.m: Then, tormented and struck down by his power, / all the gods and celestial seers went to the Grandfather, the god of gods,

1.15.s:
śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ devaṃ śaṃbhuṃ sarvajaganmayam /
brahmāṇaṃ lokakartāraṃ trātāraṃ puruṣaṃ param /
kūṭasthaṃ jagatāmekaṃ purāṇaṃ puruṣottamam //
1.15.d:
शरण्यं शरणं देवं शंभुं सर्वजगन्मयम् ।
ब्रह्माणं लोककर्तारं त्रातारं पुरुषं परम् ।
कूटस्थं जगतामेकं पुराणं पुरुषोत्तमम् ॥
1.15.m: the refuge worthy of refuge, the god Śambhu who comprises the whole universe, / Brahmā, the creator of the world, the protector, the supreme Person, / the immutable, the one of the worlds, the ancient Supreme Spirit.

1.15.s:
sa yācito devavarairmunibhiśca munīśvarāḥ /
sarvadevahitārthāya jagāma kamalāsanaḥ //
1.15.d:
स याचितो देववरैर्मुनिभिश्च मुनीश्वराः ।
सर्वदेवहितार्थाय जगाम कमलासनः ॥
1.15.m: Entreated by the foremost of the gods and the seers, O best of sages, / he who sits upon the lotus went for the welfare of all the gods,

1.15.s:
saṃstūyamānaḥ praṇatairmunīndrairamarairapi /
kṣīrodasyottaraṃ kūlaṃ yatrāste harirīśvaraḥ //
1.15.d:
संस्तूयमानः प्रणतैर्मुनीन्द्रैरमरैरपि ।
क्षीरोदस्योत्तरं कूलं यत्रास्ते हरिरीश्वरः ॥
1.15.m: praised by the eminent seers and the immortals who bowed before him, / to the northern shore of the Ocean of Milk, where Lord Hari resides.

1.15.s:
dṛṣṭvā devaṃ jagadyoniṃ viṣṇuṃ viśvaguruṃ śivam /
vavande caraṇau mūrdhnā kṛtāñjalirabhāṣata //
1.15.d:
दृष्ट्वा देवं जगद्योनिं विष्णुं विश्वगुरुं शिवम् ।
ववन्दे चरणौ मूर्ध्ना कृताञ्जलिरभाषत ॥
1.15.m: Beholding the god, the source of the universe, Viṣṇu, the preceptor of the universe, auspicious, / he bowed to his feet with his head and, with palms joined in reverence, spoke.

1.15.s:
brahmovāca
tvaṃ gatiḥ sarvabhūtānāmananto 'syakhilātmakaḥ /
vyāpī sarvāmaravapurmahāyogī sanātanaḥ //
1.15.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच
त्वं गतिः सर्वभूतानामनन्तो ऽस्यखिलात्मकः ।
व्यापी सर्वामरवपुर्महायोगी सनातनः ॥
1.15.m: Brahmā said: / You are the refuge of all beings, infinite, the self of all, / all-pervading, having the form of all the immortals, the eternal great yogin.

1.15.s:
tvamātmā sarvabhūtānāṃ pradhānaṃ prakṛtiḥ parā /
vairāgyaiśvaryanirato rāgātīto nirañjanaḥ //
1.15.d:
त्वमात्मा सर्वभूतानां प्रधानं प्रकृतिः परा ।
वैराग्यैश्वर्यनिरतो रागातीतो निरञ्जनः ॥
1.15.m: You are the self of all beings, the unmanifest source, the supreme primordial matter, / devoted to dispassion and sovereignty, beyond passion, free from taint.

1.15.s:
tvaṃ kartā caiva bhartā ca nihantā suravidviṣām /
trātumarhasyananteśa trātā hi parameśvaraḥ //
1.15.d:
त्वं कर्ता चैव भर्ता च निहन्ता सुरविद्विषाम् ।
त्रातुमर्हस्यनन्तेश त्राता हि परमेश्वरः ॥
1.15.m: You are the creator, the sustainer, and the slayer of the enemies of the gods; / you ought to protect us, O infinite Lord, for the Supreme Lord is the protector.

1.15.s:
itthaṃ sa viṣṇurbhagavān brahmaṇā saṃprabodhitaḥ /
provāconnidrapadmākṣaḥ pītavāsāsuradviṣaḥ //
1.15.d:
इत्थं स विष्णुर्भगवान् ब्रह्मणा संप्रबोधितः ।
प्रोवाचोन्निद्रपद्माक्षः पीतवासासुरद्विषः ॥
1.15.m: Thus awakened by Brahmā, the blessed Viṣṇu, / whose eyes were like blossoming lotuses, clad in yellow garments, spoke to the foes of the asuras:

1.15.s:
kimarthaṃ sumahāvīryāḥ saprajāpatikāḥ surāḥ /
imaṃ deśamanuprāptāḥ kiṃ vā kāryaṃ karomi vaḥ //
1.15.d:
किमर्थं सुमहावीर्याः सप्रजापतिकाः सुराः ।
इमं देशमनुप्राप्ताः किं वा कार्यं करोमि वः ॥
1.15.m: "For what purpose have you, gods of exceedingly great valor, together with the progenitors, / arrived at this place? Or what task may I perform for you?"

1.15.s:
devā ūcuḥ
hiraṇyakaśipurnāma brahmaṇo varadarpitaḥ /
bādhate bhagavan daityo devān sarvān saharṣibhiḥ //
1.15.d:
देवा ऊचुः
हिरण्यकशिपुर्नाम ब्रह्मणो वरदर्पितः ।
बाधते भगवन् दैत्यो देवान् सर्वान् सहर्षिभिः ॥
1.15.m: The gods said: / "O Blessed One, the Daitya named Hiraṇyakaśipu, arrogant with boons from Brahmā, / torments all the gods along with the seers.

1.15.s:
avadhyaḥ sarvabhūtānāṃ tvāmṛte puruṣottama /
hantumarhasi sarveṣāṃ tvaṃ trātāsi jaganmaya //
1.15.d:
अवध्यः सर्वभूतानां त्वामृते पुरुषोत्तम ।
हन्तुमर्हसि सर्वेषां त्वं त्रातासि जगन्मय ॥
1.15.m: He cannot be slain by any living being except you, O Supreme Spirit; / you ought to slay him, for you are the protector of all, O you who comprise the universe!"

1.15.s:
śrutvā taddaivatairuktaṃ sa viṣṇurlokabhāvanaḥ /
vadhāya daityamukhyasya so 'sṛjat puruṣaṃ svayam //
1.15.d:
श्रुत्वा तद्दैवतैरुक्तं स विष्णुर्लोकभावनः ।
वधाय दैत्यमुख्यस्य सो ऽसृजत् पुरुषं स्वयम् ॥
1.15.m: Hearing that which was spoken by the deities, that Viṣṇu, creator of the world, / himself created a person for the slaying of that foremost of Daityas.

1.15.s:
meruparvatavarṣmāṇaṃ ghorarūpaṃ bhayānakam /
śaṅkhacakragadāpāṇiṃ taṃ prāha garuḍadhvajaḥ //
1.15.d:
मेरुपर्वतवर्ष्माणं घोररूपं भयानकम् ।
शङ्खचक्रगदापाणिं तं प्राह गरुडध्वजः ॥
1.15.m: To him whose body was like Mount Meru, of terrible form, frightening, / holding a conch, discus, and mace in his hands, he whose banner is Garuḍa said:

1.15.s:
hatvā taṃ daityarājaṃ tvaṃ hiraṇyakaśipuṃ punaḥ /
imaṃ deśaṃ samāgantuṃ kṣipramarhasi pauruṣāt //
1.15.d:
हत्वा तं दैत्यराजं त्वं हिरण्यकशिपुं पुनः ।
इमं देशं समागन्तुं क्षिप्रमर्हसि पौरुषात् ॥
1.15.m: "Having slain that king of the Daityas, Hiraṇyakaśipu, / you should quickly return to this place by your prowess."

1.15.s:
niśamya vaiṣṇavaṃ vākyaṃ praṇamya puruṣottamam /
mahāpuruṣamavyaktaṃ yayau daityamahāpuram //
1.15.d:
निशम्य वैष्णवं वाक्यं प्रणम्य पुरुषोत्तमम् ।
महापुरुषमव्यक्तं ययौ दैत्यमहापुरम् ॥
1.15.m: Hearing the words of Viṣṇu and bowing to the Supreme Spirit, / that great, unmanifest Person went to the great city of the Daitya.

1.15.s:
vimuñcan bhairavaṃ nādaṃ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ /
āruhya garuḍaṃ devo mahāmerurivāparaḥ //
1.15.d:
विमुञ्चन् भैरवं नादं शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः ।
आरुह्य गरुडं देवो महामेरुरिवापरः ॥
1.15.m: Uttering a terrifying roar, bearing conch, discus, and mace, / the god, having mounted Garuḍa, was like another Great Meru.

1.15.s:
ākarṇya daityapravarā mahāmegharavopamam /
samācacakṣire nādaṃ tadā daityapaterbhayāt //
1.15.d:
आकर्ण्य दैत्यप्रवरा महामेघरवोपमम् ।
समाचचक्षिरे नादं तदा दैत्यपतेर्भयात् ॥
1.15.m: Hearing that roar resembling the rumbling of a great cloud, / the foremost Daityas then reported it out of fear to the lord of the Daityas.

1.15.s:
asurā ūcuḥ
kaścidāgacchati mahān puruṣo devacoditaḥ /
vimuñcan bhairavaṃ nādaṃ taṃ jānīmo 'marārdana //
1.15.d:
असुरा ऊचुः
कश्चिदागच्छति महान् पुरुषो देवचोदितः ।
विमुञ्चन् भैरवं नादं तं जानीमो ऽमरार्दन ॥
1.15.m: The asuras said: / "Some great person is approaching, impelled by the gods, / uttering a terrifying roar; recognize him, O tormentor of the immortals!"

1.15.s:
tataḥ sahāsuravarairhiraṇyakaśipuḥ svayam /
saṃnaddhaiḥ sāyudhaiḥ putraiḥ prahrādādyaistadā yayau //
1.15.d:
ततः सहासुरवरैर्हिरण्यकशिपुः स्वयम् ।
संनद्धैः सायुधैः पुत्रैः प्रह्रादाद्यैस्तदा ययौ ॥
1.15.m: Then Hiraṇyakaśipu himself set forth along with the foremost asuras, / and with his sons, Prahrāda and the rest, who were armored and equipped with weapons.

1.15.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ garuḍāsīnaṃ sūryakoṭisamaprabham /
puruṣaṃ parvatākāraṃ nārāyaṇamivāparam //
1.15.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं गरुडासीनं सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभम् ।
पुरुषं पर्वताकारं नारायणमिवापरम् ॥
1.15.m: Seeing that person seated upon Garuḍa, radiant as ten million suns, / shaped like a mountain, like another Nārāyaṇa,

1.15.s:
dudruvuḥ kecidanyonmamūcuḥ saṃbhrāntalocanāḥ /
ayaṃ sa devo devānāṃ goptā nārāyaṇo ripuḥ //
1.15.d:
दुद्रुवुः केचिदन्योन्ममूचुः संभ्रान्तलोचनाः ।
अयं स देवो देवानां गोप्ता नारायणो रिपुः ॥
1.15.m: some fled, while others spoke among themselves with bewildered eyes: / “This is that god, the protector of the gods, our enemy Nārāyaṇa,

1.15.s:
asmākamavyayo nūnaṃ tatsuto vā samāgataḥ /
ityuktvā śastravarṣāṇi sasṛjuḥ puruṣāya te /
tāni cāśeṣato devo nāśayāmāsa līlayā //
1.15.d:
अस्माकमव्ययो नूनं तत्सुतो वा समागतः ।
इत्युक्त्वा शस्त्रवर्षाणि ससृजुः पुरुषाय ते ।
तानि चाशेषतो देवो नाशयामास लीलया ॥
1.15.m: imperishable to us, who has surely arrived, or else his son.” / Having said this, they unleashed showers of weapons upon that person, / and the god effortlessly destroyed them entirely in sport.

1.15.s:
tadā hiraṇyakaśipoścatvāraḥ prathitaujasaḥ /
putrā nārāyaṇodbhūtaṃ yuyudhurmeghaniḥ svanāḥ /
prahrādaścāpyanuhrādaḥ saṃhrādo hrāda eva ca //
1.15.d:
तदा हिरण्यकशिपोश्चत्वारः प्रथितौजसः ।
पुत्रा नारायणोद्भूतं युयुधुर्मेघनिः स्वनाः ।
प्रह्रादश्चाप्यनुह्रादः संह्रादो ह्राद एव च ॥
1.15.m: Then Hiraṇyakaśipu's four sons of celebrated might, / thundering like clouds, fought against him who had arisen from Nārāyaṇa: / Prahrāda, Anuhrāda, Saṃhrāda, and Hrāda.

1.15.s:
prahrādaḥ prāhiṇod brāhmamanuhrādo 'tha vaiṣṇavam /
saṃhrādaścāpi kaumāramāgneyaṃ hrāda eva ca //
1.15.d:
प्रह्रादः प्राहिणोद् ब्राह्ममनुह्रादो ऽथ वैष्णवम् ।
संह्रादश्चापि कौमारमाग्नेयं ह्राद एव च ॥
1.15.m: Prahrāda discharged the weapon of Brahmā, Anuhrāda then that of Viṣṇu, / Saṃhrāda that of Kumāra, and Hrāda that of Agni.

1.15.s:
tāni taṃ puruṣaṃ prāpya catvāryastrāṇi vaiṣṇavam /
na śekurbādhituṃ viṣṇuṃ vāsudevaṃ yathā tathā //
1.15.d:
तानि तं पुरुषं प्राप्य चत्वार्यस्त्राणि वैष्णवम् ।
न शेकुर्बाधितुं विष्णुं वासुदेवं यथा तथा ॥
1.15.m: Those four weapons, reaching that Vaiṣṇava person, / were unable to harm him, just as [they could not harm] Viṣṇu Vāsudeva.

1.15.s:
athāsau caturaḥ putrān mahābāhurmahābalaḥ /
pragṛhya pādeṣu karaiḥ saṃcikṣepa nanāda ca //
1.15.d:
अथासौ चतुरः पुत्रान् महाबाहुर्महाबलः ।
प्रगृह्य पादेषु करैः संचिक्षेप ननाद च ॥
1.15.m: Then that mighty-armed one of great strength seized the four sons / by their feet with his hands, hurled them away, and roared.

1.15.s:
vimukteṣvatha putreṣu hiraṇyakaśipuḥ svayam /
pādena tāḍayāmāsa vegenorasi taṃ balī //
1.15.d:
विमुक्तेष्वथ पुत्रेषु हिरण्यकशिपुः स्वयम् ।
पादेन ताडयामास वेगेनोरसि तं बली ॥
1.15.m: When his sons had been cast off, the powerful Hiraṇyakaśipu himself / struck him violently upon the chest with his foot.

1.15.s:
sa tena pīḍito 'tyarthaṃ garuḍena tathā'śugaḥ /
adṛśyaḥ prayayau tūrṇaṃ yatra nārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ /
gatvā vijñāpayāmāsa pravṛttamakhilaṃ tathā //
1.15.d:
स तेन पीडितो ऽत्यर्थं गरुडेन तथाऽशुगः ।
अदृश्यः प्रययौ तूर्णं यत्र नारायणः प्रभुः ।
गत्वा विज्ञापयामास प्रवृत्तमखिलं तथा ॥
1.15.m: Deeply afflicted by him and by Garuḍa, the swift-moving one / quickly went, invisible, to where Lord Nārāyaṇa was; / and having gone, he reported everything that had happened in that manner.

1.15.s:
saṃcintya manasā devaḥ sarvajñānamayo 'malaḥ /
narasyārdhatanuṃ kṛtvā siṃhasyārdhatanuṃ tathā //
1.15.d:
संचिन्त्य मनसा देवः सर्वज्ञानमयो ऽमलः ।
नरस्यार्धतनुं कृत्वा सिंहस्यार्धतनुं तथा ॥
1.15.m: Having reflected in his mind, the spotless god, consisting of all knowledge, / made half his body that of a man and half that of a lion.

1.15.s:
nṛsiṃhavapuravyakto hiraṇyakaśipoḥ pure /
āvirbabhūva sahasā mohayan daityapuṅgavān //
1.15.d:
नृसिंहवपुरव्यक्तो हिरण्यकशिपोः पुरे ।
आविर्बभूव सहसा मोहयन् दैत्यपुङ्गवान् ॥
1.15.m: The unmanifest one, assuming the form of the Man-Lion, / suddenly appeared in the city of Hiraṇyakaśipu, bewildering the bull-like daityas.

1.15.s:
daṃṣṭrākarālo yogātmā yugāntadahanopamaḥ /
samāruhyātmanaḥ śaktiṃ sarvasaṃhārakārikām /
bhāti nārāyaṇo 'nanto yathā madhyandine raviḥ //
1.15.d:
दंष्ट्राकरालो योगात्मा युगान्तदहनोपमः ।
समारुह्यात्मनः शक्तिं सर्वसंहारकारिकाम् ।
भाति नारायणो ऽनन्तो यथा मध्यन्दिने रविः ॥
1.15.m: Fierce with fangs, the embodiment of yoga, resembling the fire at the end of an aeon, / having mounted his own power that effects universal destruction, / the infinite Nārāyaṇa shone like the midday sun.

1.15.s:
dṛṣṭvā nṛsiṃhavapuṣaṃ prahrādaṃ jyeṣṭhaputrakam /
vadhāya prerayāmāsa narasihasya so 'suraḥ //
1.15.d:
दृष्ट्वा नृसिंहवपुषं प्रह्रादं ज्येष्ठपुत्रकम् ।
वधाय प्रेरयामास नरसिहस्य सो ऽसुरः ॥
1.15.m: Seeing that form of the Man-Lion, that asura / urged his eldest son Prahrāda to slay the Man-Lion:

1.15.s:
imaṃ nṛsiṃhavapuṣaṃ pūrvasmād bahuśaktikam /
sahaiva tvanujaiḥ sarvairnāśayāśu mayeritaḥ //
1.15.d:
इमं नृसिंहवपुषं पूर्वस्माद् बहुशक्तिकम् ।
सहैव त्वनुजैः सर्वैर्नाशयाशु मयेरितः ॥
1.15.m: “This one possessing the form of a Man-Lion has far greater power than the former one; / together with all your younger brothers, commanded by me, destroy him quickly!”

1.15.s:
tatsaṃniyogādasuraḥ prahrādo viṣṇumavyayam /
yuyudhe sarvayatnena narasiṃhena nirjitaḥ //
1.15.d:
तत्संनियोगादसुरः प्रह्रादो विष्णुमव्ययम् ।
युयुधे सर्वयत्नेन नरसिंहेन निर्जितः ॥
1.15.m: At his command, the asura Prahrāda fought against the imperishable Viṣṇu / with every effort, [yet] was overcome by the Man-Lion.

1.15.s:
tataḥ saṃcodito daityo hiraṇyākṣastadānujaḥ /
dhyātvā paśupaterastraṃ sasarja ca nanāda ca //
1.15.d:
ततः संचोदितो दैत्यो हिरण्याक्षस्तदानुजः ।
ध्यात्वा पशुपतेरस्त्रं ससर्ज च ननाद च ॥
1.15.m: Then incited, the daitya Hiraṇyākṣa, his younger brother, / meditated upon the weapon of the Lord of Beasts, discharged it, and roared.

1.15.s:
tasya devādidevasya viṣṇoramitatejasaḥ /
na hānimakarodastraṃ yathā devasya śūlinaḥ //
1.15.d:
तस्य देवादिदेवस्य विष्णोरमिततेजसः ।
न हानिमकरोदस्त्रं यथा देवस्य शूलिनः ॥
1.15.m: Against that primal god of gods, Viṣṇu of boundless splendor, / the weapon did no harm, just as [it would do none] against the trident-bearing god.

1.15.s:
dṛṣṭvā parāhataṃ tvastraṃ prahrādo bhāgyagauravāt /
mene sarvātmakaṃ devaṃ vāsudevaṃ sanātanam //
1.15.d:
दृष्ट्वा पराहतं त्वस्त्रं प्रह्रादो भाग्यगौरवात् ।
मेने सर्वात्मकं देवं वासुदेवं सनातनम् ॥
1.15.m: Seeing the weapon repelled, Prahrāda, by the weight of good fortune, / recognized that god as eternal Vāsudeva, the self of all.

1.15.s:
saṃtyajya sarvaśastrāṇi sattvayuktena cetasā /
nanāma śirasā devaṃ yogināṃ hṛdayeśayam //
1.15.d:
संत्यज्य सर्वशस्त्राणि सत्त्वयुक्तेन चेतसा ।
ननाम शिरसा देवं योगिनां हृदयेशयम् ॥
1.15.m: Abandoning all weapons, with a mind full of clarity, / he bowed with his head to the god who rests in the hearts of yogins.

1.15.s:
stutvā nārāyaṇaiḥ stotraiḥ ṛgyajuḥ sāmasaṃbhavaiḥ /
nivārya pitaraṃ bhrātṛn hiraṇyākṣaṃ tadābravīt //
1.15.d:
स्तुत्वा नारायणैः स्तोत्रैः ऋग्यजुः सामसंभवैः ।
निवार्य पितरं भ्रातृन् हिरण्याक्षं तदाब्रवीत् ॥
1.15.m: Having praised him with hymns to Nārāyaṇa born of the Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāma Vedas, / and holding back his father and brothers, he then spoke to Hiraṇyākṣa:

1.15.s:
ayaṃ nārāyaṇo 'nantaḥ śāśvato bhagavānajaḥ /
purāṇapuruṣo devo mahāyogī jaganmayaḥ //
1.15.d:
अयं नारायणो ऽनन्तः शाश्वतो भगवानजः ।
पुराणपुरुषो देवो महायोगी जगन्मयः ॥
1.15.m: “This is the infinite Nārāyaṇa, the eternal, unborn Lord, / the ancient Person, the god, the great yogin composed of the universe.

1.15.s:
ayaṃ dhātā vidhātā ca svayañjyotirnirañjanaḥ /
pradhānapuruṣastattvaṃ mūlaprakṛtiravyayaḥ //
1.15.d:
अयं धाता विधाता च स्वयञ्ज्योतिर्निरञ्जनः ।
प्रधानपुरुषस्तत्त्वं मूलप्रकृतिरव्ययः ॥
1.15.m: He is the supporter and the creator, self-luminous and taintless, / the primary matter and the conscious spirit, reality itself, the imperishable root primordial matter.

1.15.s:
īśvaraḥ sarvabhūtānāmantaryāmī guṇātigaḥ /
gacchadhvamenaṃ śaraṇaṃ viṣṇumavyaktamavyayam //
1.15.d:
ईश्वरः सर्वभूतानामन्तर्यामी गुणातिगः ।
गच्छध्वमेनं शरणं विष्णुमव्यक्तमव्ययम् ॥
1.15.m: He is the Lord of all beings, the inner controller, beyond the qualities. / Seek refuge in him, in the unmanifest, imperishable Viṣṇu!”

1.15.s:
evamukte sudurbuddhirhiraṇyakaśipuḥ svayam /
provāca putramatyarthaṃ mohito viṣṇumāyayā //
1.15.d:
एवमुक्ते सुदुर्बुद्धिर्हिरण्यकशिपुः स्वयम् ।
प्रोवाच पुत्रमत्यर्थं मोहितो विष्णुमायया ॥
1.15.m: When this was spoken, the utterly wicked-minded Hiraṇyakaśipu himself, / deluded by Viṣṇu's illusory creative power, spoke harsh words to his son:

1.15.s:
ayaṃ sarvātmanā vadhyo nṛsiṃho 'lpaparākramaḥ /
samāgato 'smadbhavanamidānīṃ kālacoditaḥ //
1.15.d:
अयं सर्वात्मना वध्यो नृसिंहो ऽल्पपराक्रमः ।
समागतो ऽस्मद्भवनमिदानीं कालचोदितः ॥
1.15.m: “This Man-Lion of little prowess must be killed by every means; / impelled by time, he has now arrived at our dwelling!”

1.15.s:
vihasya pitaraṃ putro vacaḥ prāha mahāmatiḥ /
mā nindasvainamīśānaṃ bhūtānāmekamavyayam //
1.15.d:
विहस्य पितरं पुत्रो वचः प्राह महामतिः ।
मा निन्दस्वैनमीशानं भूतानामेकमव्ययम् ॥
1.15.m: Laughing at his father, the highly intelligent son spoke these words: / “Do not revile this one Lord, the imperishable ruler of all beings!

1.15.s:
kathaṃ devo mahādevaḥ śāśvataḥ kālavarjitaḥ /
kālena hanyate viṣṇuḥ kālātmā kālarūpadhṛk //
1.15.d:
कथं देवो महादेवः शाश्वतः कालवर्जितः ।
कालेन हन्यते विष्णुः कालात्मा कालरूपधृक् ॥
1.15.m: How could the god, the great god, eternal and devoid of time, / Viṣṇu, whose essence is time and who bears the form of time, be slain by time?”

1.15.s:
tataḥ suvarṇakaśipurdurātmā vidhicoditaḥ /
nivārito 'pi putreṇa yuyodha harimavyayam //
1.15.d:
ततः सुवर्णकशिपुर्दुरात्मा विधिचोदितः ।
निवारितो ऽपि पुत्रेण युयोध हरिमव्ययम् ॥
1.15.m: Then Suvarṇakaśipu, evil-minded and driven by fate, / though held back by his son, fought against the imperishable Hari.

1.15.s:
saṃraktanayano 'nto hiraṇyanayanāgrajam /
nakhairvidārayāmāsa prahrādasyaiva paśyataḥ //
1.15.d:
संरक्तनयनो ऽन्तो हिरण्यनयनाग्रजम् ।
नखैर्विदारयामास प्रह्रादस्यैव पश्यतः ॥
1.15.m: With blood-red eyes, the Infinite One tore open the elder brother of Hiraṇyākṣa / with his claws, while Prahrāda was actually watching.

1.15.s:
hate hiraṇyakaśipau hiraṇyākṣo mahābalaḥ /
visṛjya putraṃ prahrādaṃ dudruve bhayavihvalaḥ //
1.15.d:
हते हिरण्यकशिपौ हिरण्याक्षो महाबलः ।
विसृज्य पुत्रं प्रह्रादं दुद्रुवे भयविह्वलः ॥
1.15.m: When Hiraṇyakaśipu was slain, the mighty Hiraṇyākṣa, / abandoning his nephew Prahrāda, fled, overwhelmed by fear.

1.15.s:
anuhrādādayaḥ putrā anye ca śataśo 'surāḥ /
nṛsiṃhadehasaṃbhūtaiḥ siṃhairnotā yamālayam //
1.15.d:
अनुह्रादादयः पुत्रा अन्ये च शतशो ऽसुराः ।
नृसिंहदेहसंभूतैः सिंहैर्नोता यमालयम् ॥
1.15.m: The sons, Anuhrāda and the rest, and hundreds of other asuras, / were led to the abode of Yama by lions born from the body of the Man-Lion.

1.15.s:
tataḥ saṃhṛtya tadrūpaṃ harirnārāyaṇaḥ prabhuḥ /
svameva paramaṃ rūpaṃ yayau nārāyaṇāhvayam //
1.15.d:
ततः संहृत्य तद्रूपं हरिर्नारायणः प्रभुः ।
स्वमेव परमं रूपं ययौ नारायणाह्वयम् ॥
1.15.m: Then, withdrawing that form, Lord Hari Nārāyaṇa / returned to his own supreme form called Nārāyaṇa.

1.15.s:
gate nārāyaṇe daityaḥ prahrādo 'surasattamaḥ /
abhiṣekeṇa yuktena hiraṇyākṣamayojayat //
1.15.d:
गते नारायणे दैत्यः प्रह्रादो ऽसुरसत्तमः ।
अभिषेकेण युक्तेन हिरण्याक्षमयोजयत् ॥
1.15.m: When Nārāyaṇa had departed, the daitya Prahrāda, the best among asuras, / invested Hiraṇyākṣa with the proper consecration.

1.15.s:
sa bādhayāmāsa surān raṇe jitvā munīnapi /
labdhvāndhakaṃ mahāputraṃ tapasārādhya śaṅkaram //
1.15.d:
स बाधयामास सुरान् रणे जित्वा मुनीनपि ।
लब्ध्वान्धकं महापुत्रं तपसाराध्य शङ्करम् ॥
1.15.m: Having conquered the gods in battle, and also the sages, he oppressed them, / having obtained a great son, Andhaka, by worshipping Śaṅkara with asceticism.

1.15.s:
devāñjitvā sadevendrān badhvāca dharaṇīmimām /
nītvā rasātalaṃ cakre vandīmindīvaraprabhām //
1.15.d:
देवाञ्जित्वा सदेवेन्द्रान् बध्वाच धरणीमिमाम् ।
नीत्वा रसातलं चक्रे वन्दीमिन्दीवरप्रभाम् ॥
1.15.m: Having conquered the gods along with the lords of gods, and binding this earth, / he carried her to Rasātala and made her a captive, she who shines like a blue lotus.

1.15.s:
tataḥ sabrahmakā devāḥ parimlānamukhaśriyaḥ /
gatvā vijñāpayāmāsurviṣṇave harimandiram //
1.15.d:
ततः सब्रह्मका देवाः परिम्लानमुखश्रियः ।
गत्वा विज्ञापयामासुर्विष्णवे हरिमन्दिरम् ॥
1.15.m: Then the gods, accompanied by Brahmā, the splendor of their faces withered, / went to Hari's abode and reported [this] to Viṣṇu.

1.15.s:
sa cintayitvā viśvātmā tadvadhopāyamavyayaḥ /
sarvedevamayaṃ śubhraṃ vārāhaṃ vapurādadhe //
1.15.d:
स चिन्तयित्वा विश्वात्मा तद्वधोपायमव्ययः ।
सर्वेदेवमयं शुभ्रं वाराहं वपुरादधे ॥
1.15.m: Having reflected on the means of slaying him, the imperishable Self of all / assumed the radiant form of a boar, comprising all the gods.

1.15.s:
gatvā hiraṇyanayanaṃ hatvā taṃ puruṣottamaḥ /
daṃṣṭrayoddhārayāmāsa kalpādau dharaṇīmimām //
1.15.d:
गत्वा हिरण्यनयनं हत्वा तं पुरुषोत्तमः ।
दंष्ट्रयोद्धारयामास कल्पादौ धरणीमिमाम् ॥
1.15.m: Going there and slaying Hiraṇyanayana, the Supreme Spirit / lifted up this earth with his tusk at the beginning of the aeon.

1.15.s:
tyaktvā varāhasaṃsthānaṃ saṃsthāpya ca suradvijān
svāmeva prakṛtiṃ divyāṃ yayau viṣṇuḥ paraṃ padam //
1.15.d:
त्यक्त्वा वराहसंस्थानं संस्थाप्य च सुरद्विजान्
स्वामेव प्रकृतिं दिव्यां ययौ विष्णुः परं पदम् ॥
1.15.m: Renouncing the form of the boar and re-establishing the gods and the twice-born, / Viṣṇu departed to his own divine primordial state, the supreme abode.

1.15.s:
tasmin hate 'mararipau prahrādau viṣṇutatparaḥ /
apālayat svakaṃrājyaṃ bhāvaṃ tyaktvā tadā'suram //
1.15.d:
तस्मिन् हते ऽमररिपौ प्रह्रादौ विष्णुतत्परः ।
अपालयत् स्वकंराज्यं भावं त्यक्त्वा तदाऽसुरम् ॥
1.15.m: When that enemy of the immortals was slain, Prahrāda, devoted to Viṣṇu, / ruled his own kingdom, having then abandoned his demonic nature.

1.15.s:
iyāja vidhivad devān viṣṇorārādhane rataḥ /
niḥ sapatnaṃ tadā rājyaṃ tasyāsīd viṣṇuvaibhavāt //
1.15.d:
इयाज विधिवद् देवान् विष्णोराराधने रतः ।
निः सपत्नं तदा राज्यं तस्यासीद् विष्णुवैभवात् ॥
1.15.m: He sacrificed to the gods according to the rule, intent on the worship of Viṣṇu; / then his kingdom was free of rivals through the majesty of Viṣṇu.

1.15.s:
tataḥ kadācidasuro brāhmaṇaṃ gṛhamāgatam /
tāpasaṃ nārcayāmāsa devānāṃ caiva māyayā //
1.15.d:
ततः कदाचिदसुरो ब्राह्मणं गृहमागतम् ।
तापसं नार्चयामास देवानां चैव मायया ॥
1.15.m: Then once, through the illusory creative power of the gods, the asura / failed to show honor to an ascetic brāhmaṇa who had arrived at his house.

1.15.s:
sa tena tāpaso 'tyarthaṃ mohitenāvamānitaḥ /
śaśāpāsurarājānaṃ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ //
1.15.d:
स तेन तापसो ऽत्यर्थं मोहितेनावमानितः ।
शशापासुरराजानं क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः ॥
1.15.m: Treated with deep disrespect by him who was thus deluded, the ascetic, / his eyes blood-red with anger, cursed the king of the asuras:

1.15.s:
yattadvalaṃ samāśritya brāhmaṇānavamanyase /
sā bhaktirvaiṣṇavī divyā vināśaṃ te gamiṣyati //
1.15.d:
यत्तद्वलं समाश्रित्य ब्राह्मणानवमन्यसे ।
सा भक्तिर्वैष्णवी दिव्या विनाशं ते गमिष्यति ॥
1.15.m: “That power by relying on which you show disrespect to brāhmaṇas, / that divine devotion to Viṣṇu of yours shall go to destruction!”

1.15.s:
ityuktvā prayayau tūrṇaṃ prahrādasya gṛhād dvijaḥ /
mumoha rājyasaṃsaktaḥ so 'pi śāpabalāt tataḥ //
1.15.d:
इत्युक्त्वा प्रययौ तूर्णं प्रह्रादस्य गृहाद् द्विजः ।
मुमोह राज्यसंसक्तः सो ऽपि शापबलात् ततः ॥
1.15.m: Having said this, the twice-born quickly departed from Prahrāda's house; / and Prahrāda too, attached to his kingdom, became bewildered from the power of that curse.

1.15.s:
bādhayāmāsa viprendrān na viveda janārdanam /
piturvadhamanusmṛtya krodhaṃ cakre hariṃ prati //
1.15.d:
बाधयामास विप्रेन्द्रान् न विवेद जनार्दनम् ।
पितुर्वधमनुस्मृत्य क्रोधं चक्रे हरिं प्रति ॥
1.15.m: He oppressed the eminent vipras and did not know Janārdana; / remembering the slaying of his father, he conceived hatred toward Hari.

1.15.s:
tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ sughoraṃ romaharṣaṇam /
nārāyaṇasya devasya prahrādasyāmaradviṣaḥ //
1.15.d:
तयोः समभवद् युद्धं सुघोरं रोमहर्षणम् ।
नारायणस्य देवस्य प्रह्रादस्यामरद्विषः ॥
1.15.m: Between the two there took place a battle, exceedingly dreadful and hair-raising, / between the god Nārāyaṇa and Prahrāda, the enemy of the immortals.

1.15.s:
kṛtvā tu sumahad yuddhaṃ viṣṇunā tena nirjitaḥ /
purvasaṃskāramāhātmyāt parasmin puruṣe harau /
saṃjātaṃ tasya vijñānaṃ śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau //
1.15.d:
कृत्वा तु सुमहद् युद्धं विष्णुना तेन निर्जितः ।
पुर्वसंस्कारमाहात्म्यात् परस्मिन् पुरुषे हरौ ।
संजातं तस्य विज्ञानं शरण्यं शरणं ययौ ॥
1.15.m: Having fought a very great battle, he was defeated by Viṣṇu. / Through the power of his former impressions, regarding Hari, the supreme person, / spiritual knowledge arose in him, and he took refuge in the refuge of all.

1.15.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti daityendro hyananyāṃ bhaktimudvahan /
nārāyaṇe mahāyogamavāpa puruṣottame //
1.15.d:
ततः प्रभृति दैत्येन्द्रो ह्यनन्यां भक्तिमुद्वहन् ।
नारायणे महायोगमवाप पुरुषोत्तमे ॥
1.15.m: From then on, the lord of Daityas, bearing unswerving devotion / toward Nārāyaṇa, the Supreme Spirit, attained great yoga.

1.15.s:
hiraṇyakaśipoḥ putre yogasaṃsaktacetasi /
avāpa tanmahad rājyamandhako 'surapuṅgavaḥ //
1.15.d:
हिरण्यकशिपोः पुत्रे योगसंसक्तचेतसि ।
अवाप तन्महद् राज्यमन्धको ऽसुरपुङ्गवः ॥
1.15.m: When the son of Hiraṇyakaśipu had his mind absorbed in yoga, / Andhaka, the foremost of the Asuras, obtained that great kingdom.

1.15.s:
hiraṇyanetratanayaḥ śaṃbhordehasamudbhavaḥ /
mandarasthāmumāṃ devīṃ cakame parvatātmajām //
1.15.d:
हिरण्यनेत्रतनयः शंभोर्देहसमुद्भवः ।
मन्दरस्थामुमां देवीं चकमे पर्वतात्मजाम् ॥
1.15.m: The son of Hiraṇyanetra, born from the body of Śaṃbhu, / lusted after goddess Umā, the daughter of the mountain, who was dwelling on Mount Mandara.

1.15.s:
purā dāruvane puṇye munayo gṛhamedhinaḥ /
īśvarārādhanārthāya tapaśceruḥ sahastraśaḥ //
1.15.d:
पुरा दारुवने पुण्ये मुनयो गृहमेधिनः ।
ईश्वराराधनार्थाय तपश्चेरुः सहस्त्रशः ॥
1.15.m: Formerly, in the holy Dāru forest, householder sages / practiced austerities by the thousands for the sake of worshiping the Lord.

1.15.s:
tataḥ kadācinmahati kālayogena dustarā /
anāvṛṣṭiratīvogrā hyāsīd bhūtavināśinī //
1.15.d:
ततः कदाचिन्महति कालयोगेन दुस्तरा ।
अनावृष्टिरतीवोग्रा ह्यासीद् भूतविनाशिनी ॥
1.15.m: Then at one time, through the juncture of time, there occurred an insurmountable / and exceedingly severe drought, which destroyed living beings.

1.15.s:
sametya sarve munayo gautamaṃ tapasāṃ nidhim /
ayācanta kṣudhāviṣṭā āhāraṃ prāṇadhāraṇam //
1.15.d:
समेत्य सर्वे मुनयो गौतमं तपसां निधिम् ।
अयाचन्त क्षुधाविष्टा आहारं प्राणधारणम् ॥
1.15.m: All the sages assembled and, seized with hunger, / begged Gautama, a treasury of austerities, for food to sustain life.

1.15.s:
sa tebhyaḥ pradadāvannaṃ mṛṣṭaṃ bahutaraṃ budhaḥ /
sarve bubujire viprā nirviśaṅkena cetasā //
1.15.d:
स तेभ्यः प्रददावन्नं मृष्टं बहुतरं बुधः ।
सर्वे बुबुजिरे विप्रा निर्विशङ्केन चेतसा ॥
1.15.m: The wise sage gave them abundant, purified food; / all the brāhmaṇas ate with minds free from doubt.

1.15.s:
gate tu dvādaśe varṣe kalpānta iva śaṅkarī /
babhūva vṛṣṭirmahatī yathāpūrvamabhūjjagat //
1.15.d:
गते तु द्वादशे वर्षे कल्पान्त इव शङ्करी ।
बभूव वृष्टिर्महती यथापूर्वमभूज्जगत् ॥
1.15.m: When twelve years had passed, there came a great, beneficent rain, / like that at the end of a cosmic age, and the world became as before.

1.15.s:
tataḥ sarve munivarāḥ samāmantrya parasparam /
maharṣi gautamaṃ procurgacchāma iti vegataḥ //
1.15.d:
ततः सर्वे मुनिवराः समामन्त्र्य परस्परम् ।
महर्षि गौतमं प्रोचुर्गच्छाम इति वेगतः ॥
1.15.m: Then all the excellent sages took counsel with one another / and said hastily to the great sage Gautama, “We are departing.”

1.15.s:
nivārayāmāsa ca tān kañcit kālaṃ yathāsukham /
uṣitvā madgṛhe 'vaśyaṃ gacchadhvamiti paṇḍitāḥ //
1.15.d:
निवारयामास च तान् कञ्चित् कालं यथासुखम् ।
उषित्वा मद्गृहे ऽवश्यं गच्छध्वमिति पण्डिताः ॥
1.15.m: He checked them, saying, “Learned sages, / after staying comfortably in my house for some time, you must certainly go.”

1.15.s:
tato māyāmayīṃ sṛṣṭvā kṛśāṃ gāṃ sarva eva te /
samīpaṃ prāpayāmāsugautamasya mahātmanaḥ //
1.15.d:
ततो मायामयीं सृष्ट्वा कृशां गां सर्व एव ते ।
समीपं प्रापयामासुगौतमस्य महात्मनः ॥
1.15.m: Then they all created an illusory, emaciated cow / and brought it near the great-souled Gautama.

1.15.s:
so 'nuvīkṣya kṛpāviṣṭastasyāḥ saṃrakṣaṇotsukaḥ /
goṣṭhe tāṃ bandhayāmāsa spṛṣṭamātrā mamāra sā //
1.15.d:
सो ऽनुवीक्ष्य कृपाविष्टस्तस्याः संरक्षणोत्सुकः ।
गोष्ठे तां बन्धयामास स्पृष्टमात्रा ममार सा ॥
1.15.m: Looking upon her, filled with compassion and eager to protect her, / he tied her in the cowpen; the moment she was touched, she died.

1.15.s:
sa śokenābhisaṃtaptaḥ kāryākāryaṃ mahāmuniḥ /
na paśyati sma sahasā tādṛśaṃ munayo 'bruvan //
1.15.d:
स शोकेनाभिसंतप्तः कार्याकार्यं महामुनिः ।
न पश्यति स्म सहसा तादृशं मुनयो ऽब्रुवन् ॥
1.15.m: Tormented by grief, the great sage suddenly / could not distinguish what was to be done from what was not to be done; and the sages said to him:

1.15.s:
govadhyeyaṃ dvijaśreṣṭha yāvat tava śarīragā /
tāvat te 'nnaṃ na bhoktavyaṃ gacchāmo vayameva hi //
1.15.d:
गोवध्येयं द्विजश्रेष्ठ यावत् तव शरीरगा ।
तावत् ते ऽन्नं न भोक्तव्यं गच्छामो वयमेव हि ॥
1.15.m: “O best of the twice-born, as long as this cow-slaughter attaches to your body, / so long must your food not be eaten; we are indeed departing.”

1.15.s:
tena te muditāḥ santo devadāruvanaṃ śubham /
jagmuḥ pāpavaśaṃ nītāstapaścartuṃ yathā purā //
1.15.d:
तेन ते मुदिताः सन्तो देवदारुवनं शुभम् ।
जग्मुः पापवशं नीतास्तपश्चर्तुं यथा पुरा ॥
1.15.m: Rejoicing at this, led under the sway of sin, / they went to the auspicious Devadāru forest to practice austerities as before.

1.15.s:
sa teṣāṃ māyayā jātāṃ govadhyāṃ gautamo muniḥ /
kenāpi hetunā jñātvā śaśāpātīvakopanaḥ //
1.15.d:
स तेषां मायया जातां गोवध्यां गौतमो मुनिः ।
केनापि हेतुना ज्ञात्वा शशापातीवकोपनः ॥
1.15.m: The sage Gautama, discovering by some means / that the cow-slaughter was produced by their deceit, was extremely angered and cursed them:

1.15.s:
bhaviṣyanti trayībāhyā mahāpātakibhiḥ samāḥ /
babhūvuste tathā śāpājjāyamānāḥ punaḥ punaḥ //
1.15.d:
भविष्यन्ति त्रयीबाह्या महापातकिभिः समाः ।
बभूवुस्ते तथा शापाज्जायमानाः पुनः पुनः ॥
1.15.m: “They shall be outside the three Vedas, equal to perpetrators of great sins.” / And through the curse, being born again and again, they became so.

1.15.s:
sarve saṃprāpya deveśaṃ śaṅkaraṃ viṣṇumavyayam /
astuvan laukikaiḥ stotrairucchiṣṭā iva sarvagau //
1.15.d:
सर्वे संप्राप्य देवेशं शङ्करं विष्णुमव्ययम् ।
अस्तुवन् लौकिकैः स्तोत्रैरुच्छिष्टा इव सर्वगौ ॥
1.15.m: They all approached the lord of the gods, Śaṅkara, and the imperishable Viṣṇu, / and, as if impure, praised the two omnipresent gods with worldly hymns:

1.15.s:
devadevau mahādevau bhaktānāmārtināśanau /
kāmavṛttyā mahāyogau pāpānnastrātumarhathaḥ //
1.15.d:
देवदेवौ महादेवौ भक्तानामार्तिनाशनौ ।
कामवृत्त्या महायोगौ पापान्नस्त्रातुमर्हथः ॥
1.15.m: “O two gods of gods, two Mahādevas, destroyers of the distress of devotees, / you who act at your own will and possess great yoga, you ought to deliver us from sin.”

1.15.s:
tadā pārśvasthitaṃ viṣṇuṃ saṃprekṣya vṛṣabhadhvajaḥ /
kimeteṣāṃ bhavet kāryaṃ prāha puṇyaiṣiṇāmiti //
1.15.d:
तदा पार्श्वस्थितं विष्णुं संप्रेक्ष्य वृषभध्वजः ।
किमेतेषां भवेत् कार्यं प्राह पुण्यैषिणामिति ॥
1.15.m: Then the bull-bannered [Śiva], looking at Viṣṇu standing at his side, / said, “What should be done for these who seek merit?”

1.15.s:
tataḥ sa bhagavān viṣṇuḥ śaraṇyo bhaktavatsalaḥ /
gopatiṃ prāha viprendrānālokya praṇatān hariḥ //
1.15.d:
ततः स भगवान् विष्णुः शरण्यो भक्तवत्सलः ।
गोपतिं प्राह विप्रेन्द्रानालोक्य प्रणतान् हरिः ॥
1.15.m: Then the blessed lord Viṣṇu, the refuge of all and affectionate to devotees, / beholding the bowed leaders of the brāhmaṇas, said to the lord of cattle:

1.15.s:
na vedabāhye puruṣe puṇyaleśo 'pi śaṅkara /
saṃgacchate mahādeva dharmo vedād vinirbabhau //
1.15.d:
न वेदबाह्ये पुरुषे पुण्यलेशो ऽपि शङ्कर ।
संगच्छते महादेव धर्मो वेदाद् विनिर्बभौ ॥
1.15.m: “O Śaṅkara, not even a fraction of merit belongs to a man outside the Veda; / O Mahādeva, righteousness has shone forth from the Veda.

1.15.s:
tathāpi bhaktavātsalyād rakṣitavyā maheśvara /
asmābhiḥ sarva eveme gantāro narakānapi //
1.15.d:
तथापि भक्तवात्सल्याद् रक्षितव्या महेश्वर ।
अस्माभिः सर्व एवेमे गन्तारो नरकानपि ॥
1.15.m: Even so, out of affection for devotees, O Maheśvara, / we must protect all these, even though they will go to the hells.

1.15.s:
tasmād vai vedabāhyānāṃ rakṣaṇārthāya pāpinām /
vimohanāya śāstrāṇi kariṣyāmo vṛṣadhvaja //
1.15.d:
तस्माद् वै वेदबाह्यानां रक्षणार्थाय पापिनाम् ।
विमोहनाय शास्त्राणि करिष्यामो वृषध्वज ॥
1.15.m: Therefore, O bull-bannered lord, for the sake of protecting the sinners / who are outside the Veda, we will compose treatises to delude them.”

1.15.s:
evaṃ saṃbodhito rudro mādhavena murāriṇā /
cakāra mohaśāstrāṇi keśavo 'pi śiveritaḥ //
1.15.d:
एवं संबोधितो रुद्रो माधवेन मुरारिणा ।
चकार मोहशास्त्राणि केशवो ऽपि शिवेरितः ॥
1.15.m: Thus addressed by Mādhava, the enemy of Mura, Rudra / composed delusive treatises, and Keśava too, impelled by Śiva, [composed treatises]:

1.15.s:
kāpālaṃ nākulaṃ vāmaṃ bhairavaṃ pūrvapaścimam /
pañcarātraṃ pāśupataṃ tathānyāni sahastraśaḥ //
1.15.d:
कापालं नाकुलं वामं भैरवं पूर्वपश्चिमम् ।
पञ्चरात्रं पाशुपतं तथान्यानि सहस्त्रशः ॥
1.15.m: Kāpāla, Nākula, Vāma, Bhairava, the Eastern and the Western, / Pañcarātra, Pāśupata, and thousands of others like them.

1.15.s:
sṛṣṭvā tānūcaturdevau kurvāṇāḥ śāstracoditam /
patanto niraye ghore bahūn kalpān punaḥ punaḥ //
1.15.d:
सृष्ट्वा तानूचतुर्देवौ कुर्वाणाः शास्त्रचोदितम् ।
पतन्तो निरये घोरे बहून् कल्पान् पुनः पुनः ॥
1.15.m: Having created them, the two gods said to them: “Performing what is enjoined in these treatises, / falling into a dreadful hell again and again for many cosmic ages,

1.15.s:
jāyanto mānuṣe loke kṣīṇapāpacayāstataḥ /
īśvarārādhanabalād gacchadhvaṃ sukṛtāṃ gatim /
vartadhvaṃ matprasādena nānyathā niṣkṛtirhi vaḥ //
1.15.d:
जायन्तो मानुषे लोके क्षीणपापचयास्ततः ।
ईश्वराराधनबलाद् गच्छध्वं सुकृतां गतिम् ।
वर्तध्वं मत्प्रसादेन नान्यथा निष्कृतिर्हि वः ॥
1.15.m: then being born in the mortal world with your accumulated sins diminished, / you shall attain the state of the virtuous through the power of worshiping the Lord. / Live by my grace; for you have no other expiation.”

1.15.s:
evamīśvaraviṣṇubhyāṃ coditāste maharṣayaḥ /
ādeśaṃ pratyapadyanta śirasāsuravidviṣoḥ //
1.15.d:
एवमीश्वरविष्णुभ्यां चोदितास्ते महर्षयः ।
आदेशं प्रत्यपद्यन्त शिरसासुरविद्विषोः ॥
1.15.m: Thus commanded by the Lord and Viṣṇu, those great sages / accepted the command of the two enemies of the Asuras with their heads.

1.15.s:
cakruste 'nyāni śāstrāṇi tatra tatra ratāḥ punaḥ /
śiṣyānadhyāpayāmāsurdarśayitvā phalāni tu //
1.15.d:
चक्रुस्ते ऽन्यानि शास्त्राणि तत्र तत्र रताः पुनः ।
शिष्यानध्यापयामासुर्दर्शयित्वा फलानि तु ॥
1.15.m: Devoted to those various systems, they composed other treatises; / and showing the fruits [of them], they taught them to their disciples.

1.15.s:
mohayanta imaṃ lokamavatīrya mahītale /
cakāra śaṅkaro bhikṣāṃ hitāyaiṣāṃ dvijaiḥ saha //
1.15.d:
मोहयन्त इमं लोकमवतीर्य महीतले ।
चकार शङ्करो भिक्षां हितायैषां द्विजैः सह ॥
1.15.m: Deluding this world, having descended onto the earth, / Śaṅkara wandered for alms together with the twice-born for their benefit,

1.15.s:
kapālamālābharaṇaḥ pretabhasmāvaguṇṭhitaḥ /
vimohayaṃllokamimaṃ jaṭāmaṇḍalamaṇḍitaḥ //
1.15.d:
कपालमालाभरणः प्रेतभस्मावगुण्ठितः ।
विमोहयंल्लोकमिमं जटामण्डलमण्डितः ॥
1.15.m: adorned with a garland of skulls, smeared with the ashes of corpses, / deluding this world, adorned with a mass of matted hair.

1.15.s:
nikṣipya pārvatīṃ devīṃ viṣṇāvamitatejasi /
niyojyāṅgabhavaṃ rudraṃ bhairavaṃ duṣṭanigrahe //
1.15.d:
निक्षिप्य पार्वतीं देवीं विष्णावमिततेजसि ।
नियोज्याङ्गभवं रुद्रं भैरवं दुष्टनिग्रहे ॥
1.15.m: Entrusting the goddess Pārvatī to Viṣṇu of immeasurable splendor, / and appointing the body-born Rudra, Bhairava, to subdue the wicked,

1.15.s:
dattvā nārāyaṇe devīṃ nandinaṃ kulanandinam /
saṃsthāpya tatra gaṇapān devānindrapurogamān //
1.15.d:
दत्त्वा नारायणे देवीं नन्दिनं कुलनन्दिनम् ।
संस्थाप्य तत्र गणपान् देवानिन्द्रपुरोगमान् ॥
1.15.m: having given the goddess to Nārāyaṇa, and stationing Nandin, the delight of his family, / the leaders of the Gaṇas there, and the gods headed by Indra,

1.15.s:
prasthite 'tha mahādeve viṣṇurviśvatanuḥ svayam /
strīrūpadhārī niyataṃ sevate sma maheśvarīm //
1.15.d:
प्रस्थिते ऽथ महादेवे विष्णुर्विश्वतनुः स्वयम् ।
स्त्रीरूपधारी नियतं सेवते स्म महेश्वरीम् ॥
1.15.m: when Mahādeva had departed, Viṣṇu, who is universal in form, / constantly attended upon Maheśvarī, having himself assumed a female form.

1.15.s:
brahmā hutāśanaḥ śakro yamo 'nye surapuṅgavāḥ /
siṣevire mahādevīṃ strīveśaṃ śobhanaṃ gatāḥ //
1.15.d:
ब्रह्मा हुताशनः शक्रो यमो ऽन्ये सुरपुङ्गवाः ।
सिषेविरे महादेवीं स्त्रीवेशं शोभनं गताः ॥
1.15.m: Brahmā, Fire, Indra, Yama, and the other foremost gods, / having assumed beautiful female attire, served the great goddess.

1.15.s:
nandīśvaraśca bhagavān śaṃbhoratyantavallabhaḥ /
dvāradeśe gaṇādhyakṣo yathāpūrvamatiṣṭhata //
1.15.d:
नन्दीश्वरश्च भगवान् शंभोरत्यन्तवल्लभः ।
द्वारदेशे गणाध्यक्षो यथापूर्वमतिष्ठत ॥
1.15.m: And the blessed Nandīśvara, exceedingly dear to Śaṃbhu, / the commander of the Gaṇas, stood at the doorway as before.

1.15.s:
etasminnantare daityo hyandhako nāma durmatiḥ /
āhartukāmo girijāmājagāmātha mandaram //
1.15.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे दैत्यो ह्यन्धको नाम दुर्मतिः ।
आहर्तुकामो गिरिजामाजगामाथ मन्दरम् ॥
1.15.m: In the meantime, the evil-minded Daitya named Andhaka, / desiring to abduct the daughter of the mountain, came to Mount Mandara.

1.15.s:
saṃprāptamandhakaṃ dṛṣṭvā śaṅkaraḥ kālabhairavaḥ /
nyaṣedhayadameyātmā kālarūpadharo haraḥ //
1.15.d:
संप्राप्तमन्धकं दृष्ट्वा शङ्करः कालभैरवः ।
न्यषेधयदमेयात्मा कालरूपधरो हरः ॥
1.15.m: Seeing Andhaka arrived, Śaṅkara, [present as] Kālabhairava, / Hara of immeasurable nature, wearing the form of Time, barred his way.

1.15.s:
tayoḥ samabhavad yuddhaṃ sughoraṃ romaharṣaṇam /
śūlenorasi taṃ daityamājaghāna vṛṣadhvajaḥ //
1.15.d:
तयोः समभवद् युद्धं सुघोरं रोमहर्षणम् ।
शूलेनोरसि तं दैत्यमाजघान वृषध्वजः ॥
1.15.m: Between the two of them arose a battle, exceedingly dreadful and hair-raising; / the bull-bannered lord struck that Daitya in the chest with a trident.

1.15.s:
tataḥ sahastraśo daityaḥ sasarjāndhakasaṃjñitān /
nandiṣeṇādayo daityairandhakairabhinirjitāḥ //
1.15.d:
ततः सहस्त्रशो दैत्यः ससर्जान्धकसंज्ञितान् ।
नन्दिषेणादयो दैत्यैरन्धकैरभिनिर्जिताः ॥
1.15.m: Then by the thousands the Daitya produced [forms] named Andhaka; / Nandiṣeṇa and the others were utterly overcome by the Daityas, the Andhakas.

1.15.s:
ghaṇṭākarṇo meghanādaścaṇḍeśaścaṇḍatāpanaḥ /
vināyako meghavāhaḥ somanandī ca vaidyutaḥ //
1.15.d:
घण्टाकर्णो मेघनादश्चण्डेशश्चण्डतापनः ।
विनायको मेघवाहः सोमनन्दी च वैद्युतः ॥
1.15.m: Ghaṇṭākarṇa, Meghanāda, Caṇḍeśa, Caṇḍatāpana, / Vināyaka, Meghavāha, Somanandin, and Vaidyuta,

1.15.s:
sarve 'ndhakaṃ daityavaraṃ saṃprāpyātibalānvitāḥ /
yuyudhuḥ śūlaśaktyṛṣṭigirikūṭaparaśvadhaiḥ //
1.15.d:
सर्वे ऽन्धकं दैत्यवरं संप्राप्यातिबलान्विताः ।
युयुधुः शूलशक्त्यृष्टिगिरिकूटपरश्वधैः ॥
1.15.m: all reaching the excellent Daitya Andhaka and endowed with immense might, / fought with tridents, javelins, spears, mountain peaks, and battle-axes.

1.15.s:
bhrāmayitvātha hastābhyāṃ gṛhītacaraṇadvayāḥ /
daityendreṇātibalinā kṣiptāste śatayojanam //
1.15.d:
भ्रामयित्वाथ हस्ताभ्यां गृहीतचरणद्वयाः ।
दैत्येन्द्रेणातिबलिना क्षिप्तास्ते शतयोजनम् ॥
1.15.m: Whirling them around with his hands, seized by their two feet, / they were hurled a hundred yojanas by the immensely strong lord of the Daityas.

1.15.s:
tato 'ndhakanisṛṣṭāste śataśo 'tha sahastraśaḥ /
kālasūryapratīkāśā bhairavaṃ tvabhidudruvuḥ //
1.15.d:
ततो ऽन्धकनिसृष्टास्ते शतशो ऽथ सहस्त्रशः ।
कालसूर्यप्रतीकाशा भैरवं त्वभिदुद्रुवुः ॥
1.15.m: Then those created by Andhaka in hundreds and thousands, / resembling the sun of destruction, rushed against Bhairava.

1.15.s:
hā heti śabdaḥ sumahān babhūvātibhayaṅkaraḥ /
yuyodha bhairavo rudraḥ śūlamādāya bhīṣaṇam //
1.15.d:
हा हेति शब्दः सुमहान् बभूवातिभयङ्करः ।
युयोध भैरवो रुद्रः शूलमादाय भीषणम् ॥
1.15.m: A very great, terrifying cry arose, "Alas! Alas!" / Rudra, as Bhairava, fought, taking up his dreadful trident.

1.15.s:
dṛṣṭvāndhakānāṃ subalaṃ durjayaṃ tarjito haraḥ /
jagāma śaraṇaṃ devaṃ vāsudevamajaṃ vibhum //
1.15.d:
दृष्ट्वान्धकानां सुबलं दुर्जयं तर्जितो हरः ।
जगाम शरणं देवं वासुदेवमजं विभुम् ॥
1.15.m: Seeing the immense and invincible army of the Andhakas, Hara was challenged; / he went for refuge to the lord, the unborn and all-pervading god Vāsudeva.

1.15.s:
so 'sṛjad bhagavān viṣṇurdevīnāṃ śatamuttamam /
devīpārśvasthito devo vināśāyāmaradviṣām //
1.15.d:
सो ऽसृजद् भगवान् विष्णुर्देवीनां शतमुत्तमम् ।
देवीपार्श्वस्थितो देवो विनाशायामरद्विषाम् ॥
1.15.m: That lord Viṣṇu created an excellent hundred goddesses; / stationed beside the Goddess, the god [acted] for the destruction of the enemies of the immortals.

1.15.s:
tathāndhakasahastraṃ tu devībhiryamasādanam /
nītaṃ keśavamāhātmyāllīlayaiva raṇājire //
1.15.d:
तथान्धकसहस्त्रं तु देवीभिर्यमसादनम् ।
नीतं केशवमाहात्म्याल्लीलयैव रणाजिरे ॥
1.15.m: And in that way, a thousand Andhakas were dispatched to Yama's abode / by the goddesses simply in sport on the field of battle, through Keśava's majesty.

1.15.s:
dṛṣṭvā parāhataṃ sainyamandhako 'pi mahāsuraḥ /
parāṅmukhoraṇāt tasmāt palāyata mahājavaḥ //
1.15.d:
दृष्ट्वा पराहतं सैन्यमन्धको ऽपि महासुरः ।
पराङ्मुखोरणात् तस्मात् पलायत महाजवः ॥
1.15.m: Seeing his army stricken down, the great Asura Andhaka also / turned away from that battle and fled with great speed.

1.15.s:
tataḥ krīḍāṃ mahādevaḥ kṛtvā dvādaśavārṣikīm /
hitāya loke bhaktānāmājagāmātha mandaram //
1.15.d:
ततः क्रीडां महादेवः कृत्वा द्वादशवार्षिकीम् ।
हिताय लोके भक्तानामाजगामाथ मन्दरम् ॥
1.15.m: Then Mahādeva, having engaged in sport for twelve years / for the welfare of his devotees in the world, came to Mount Mandara.

1.15.s:
saṃprāptamīśvaraṃ jñātvā sarva eva gaṇeśvarāḥ /
samāgamyopatasthustaṃ bhānumantamiva dvijāḥ //
1.15.d:
संप्राप्तमीश्वरं ज्ञात्वा सर्व एव गणेश्वराः ।
समागम्योपतस्थुस्तं भानुमन्तमिव द्विजाः ॥
1.15.m: Knowing the Lord had arrived, all the leaders of the Gaṇas / assembled and waited upon him, just as the twice-born attend the sun.

1.15.s:
praviśya bhavanaṃ puṇyamayuktānāṃ durāsadam /
dadarśa nandinaṃ devaṃ bhairavaṃ keśavaṃ śivaḥ //
1.15.d:
प्रविश्य भवनं पुण्यमयुक्तानां दुरासदम् ।
ददर्श नन्दिनं देवं भैरवं केशवं शिवः ॥
1.15.m: Entering the sacred dwelling, inaccessible to those not united [in yoga], / Śiva beheld the divine Nandin, Bhairava, and Keśava.

1.15.s:
praṇāmapravaṇaṃ devaṃ so 'nugṛhyātha nandinam /
āghrāya mūrdhanīśānaḥ keśavaṃ pariṣasvaje //
1.15.d:
प्रणामप्रवणं देवं सो ऽनुगृह्याथ नन्दिनम् ।
आघ्राय मूर्धनीशानः केशवं परिषस्वजे ॥
1.15.m: Having shown favor to the divine Nandin, who was devoted to bowing, / Īśāna smelled Keśava on the crown of his head and embraced him.

1.15.s:
dṛṣṭvā devī mahādevaṃ prītivisphāritekṣaṇā /
nanāma śirasā tasya pādayorīśvarasya sā //
1.15.d:
दृष्ट्वा देवी महादेवं प्रीतिविस्फारितेक्षणा ।
ननाम शिरसा तस्य पादयोरीश्वरस्य सा ॥
1.15.m: Seeing Mahādeva, the Goddess, her eyes widened with joy, / bowed with her head at the feet of the Lord.

1.15.s:
nivedya vijayaṃ tasmai śaṅkarāyātha śaṅkarī /
bhairavo viṣṇumāhātmyaṃ praṇataḥ pārśvago 'vadat //
1.15.d:
निवेद्य विजयं तस्मै शङ्करायाथ शङ्करी ।
भैरवो विष्णुमाहात्म्यं प्रणतः पार्श्वगो ऽवदत् ॥
1.15.m: Then Śaṅkarī reported victory to that Śaṅkara; / bowing and standing beside him, Bhairava spoke of Viṣṇu's majesty.

1.15.s:
śrutvā tadvijayaṃ śaṃbhurvikramaṃ keśavasya ca /
samāste bhagavānīśo devyā saha varāsane //
1.15.d:
श्रुत्वा तद्विजयं शंभुर्विक्रमं केशवस्य च ।
समास्ते भगवानीशो देव्या सह वरासने ॥
1.15.m: Hearing of that victory and the valor of Keśava, / the lord Īśa sat together with the Goddess on an excellent throne.

1.15.s:
tato devagaṇāḥ sarve marīcipramukhā dvijāḥ /
ājagmurmandaraṃ druṣṭaṃ devadevaṃ trilocanam //
1.15.d:
ततो देवगणाः सर्वे मरीचिप्रमुखा द्विजाः ।
आजग्मुर्मन्दरं द्रुष्टं देवदेवं त्रिलोचनम् ॥
1.15.m: Then all the hosts of gods and the twice-born led by Marīci / came to Mount Mandara to behold the three-eyed god of gods.

1.15.s:
yena tad vijitaṃ pūrvaṃ devīnāṃ śatamuttamam /
samāgataṃ daityasainyamīśdarśanavāñchayā //
1.15.d:
येन तद् विजितं पूर्वं देवीनां शतमुत्तमम् ।
समागतं दैत्यसैन्यमीश्दर्शनवाञ्छया ॥
1.15.m: By whom that excellent hundred goddesses had previously conquered / the gathered Daitya army, desiring the sight of the Lord.

1.15.s:
dṛṣṭvā varāsanāsīnaṃ devyā candravibhūṣaṇam /
praṇemurādarād devyo gāyanti smātilālasāḥ //
1.15.d:
दृष्ट्वा वरासनासीनं देव्या चन्द्रविभूषणम् ।
प्रणेमुरादराद् देव्यो गायन्ति स्मातिलालसाः ॥
1.15.m: Seeing him adorned with the moon seated with the Goddess on an excellent throne, / the goddesses bowed with respect and, filled with intense longing, sang.

1.15.s:
praṇemurgirijāṃ devīṃ vāmapārśve pinākinaḥ /
devāsanagataṃ devaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayam //
1.15.d:
प्रणेमुर्गिरिजां देवीं वामपार्श्वे पिनाकिनः ।
देवासनगतं देवं नारायणमनामयम् ॥
1.15.m: They bowed to the goddess Girijā on the left side of the wielder of the Pināka, / and to the divine, flawless Nārāyaṇa seated on the divine throne.

1.15.s:
dṛṣṭvā siṃhāsanāsīnaṃ devyā nārāyaṇena ca /
praṇamya devamīśānaṃ pṛṣṭavatyo varāṅganāḥ //
1.15.d:
दृष्ट्वा सिंहासनासीनं देव्या नारायणेन च ।
प्रणम्य देवमीशानं पृष्टवत्यो वराङ्गनाः ॥
1.15.m: Seeing [Īśāna] seated on the lion-throne with the Goddess and Nārāyaṇa, / the excellent women bowed to the divine Īśāna and asked:

1.15.s:
kanyā ūcuḥ
kastvaṃ vibhrājase kāntyā keyaṃ bālaraviprabhā /
ko 'nvayaṃ bhti vapuṣā paṅkajāyatalocanaḥ //
1.15.d:
कन्या ऊचुः
कस्त्वं विभ्राजसे कान्त्या केयं बालरविप्रभा ।
को ऽन्वयं भ्ति वपुषा पङ्कजायतलोचनः ॥
1.15.m: The maidens said: / "Who are you that shine with splendor? Who is this woman radiant as the morning sun? / And who is this one who shines with his body, possessing eyes long as lotuses?"

1.15.s:
niśamya tāsāṃ vacanaṃ vṛṣendravaravāhanaḥ /
vyājahāra mahāyogī bhūtādhipatiravyayaḥ //
1.15.d:
निशम्य तासां वचनं वृषेन्द्रवरवाहनः ।
व्याजहार महायोगी भूताधिपतिरव्ययः ॥
1.15.m: Hearing their words, he whose mount is the best of bulls, / the great yogin, the imperishable lord of beings, spoke:

1.15.s:
ahaṃ nārāyaṇo gaurī jaganmātā sanātanī /
vibhajya saṃsthito devaḥ svātmānaṃ bahudheśvaraḥ //
1.15.d:
अहं नारायणो गौरी जगन्माता सनातनी ।
विभज्य संस्थितो देवः स्वात्मानं बहुधेश्वरः ॥
1.15.m: "I, Nārāyaṇa, and Gaurī, the eternal mother of the world— / having divided his own self manifold, the divine Lord abides.

1.15.s:
na me viduḥ paraṃ tattvaṃ devādyā na maharṣayaḥ /
eko 'yaṃ veda viśvātmā bhavānī viṣṇureva ca //
1.15.d:
न मे विदुः परं तत्त्वं देवाद्या न महर्षयः ।
एको ऽयं वेद विश्वात्मा भवानी विष्णुरेव च ॥
1.15.m: Neither the gods and others nor the great sages know my supreme truth; / only this one who is the self of the universe, Bhavānī, and Viṣṇu knows it.

1.15.s:
ahaṃ hi niṣkriyaḥ śāntaḥ kevalo niṣparigrahaḥ /
māmeva keśavaṃ devamāhurdevīmathāmbikām //
1.15.d:
अहं हि निष्क्रियः शान्तः केवलो निष्परिग्रहः ।
मामेव केशवं देवमाहुर्देवीमथाम्बिकाम् ॥
1.15.m: For I am actionless, tranquil, solitary, and free from possessions; / me alone they call the divine Keśava, and also the Goddess Ambikā.

1.15.s:
eṣa dhātā vidhātā ca kāraṇaṃ kāryameva ca /
kartā kārayitā viṣṇurbhuktimuktiphalapradaḥ //
1.15.d:
एष धाता विधाता च कारणं कार्यमेव च ।
कर्ता कारयिता विष्णुर्भुक्तिमुक्तिफलप्रदः ॥
1.15.m: He is the creator and the ordainer, the cause and the effect, / the doer and the instigator—Viṣṇu, who bestows the fruit of enjoyment and liberation.

1.15.s:
bhoktā pumānaprameyaḥ saṃhartā kālarūpadhṛk /
straṣṭā pātā vāsudevo viśvātmā viśvatomukhaḥ //
1.15.d:
भोक्ता पुमानप्रमेयः संहर्ता कालरूपधृक् ।
स्त्रष्टा पाता वासुदेवो विश्वात्मा विश्वतोमुखः ॥
1.15.m: He is the experiencer, the immeasurable Spirit, the destroyer bearing the form of Time, / the creator, the protector, Vāsudeva, the self of the universe, facing in all directions.

1.15.s:
kṛṭastho hyakṣaro vyāpī yogī nārāyaṇaḥ svayam /
tārakaḥ puruṣo hyātmā kevalaṃ paramaṃ padam //
1.15.d:
कृटस्थो ह्यक्षरो व्यापी योगी नारायणः स्वयम् ।
तारकः पुरुषो ह्यात्मा केवलं परमं पदम् ॥
1.15.m: Indeed, unchanging, imperishable, and all-pervading, the yogin is Nārāyaṇa himself; / the deliverer, the Spirit, the self, the absolute supreme state.

1.15.s:
saiṣā māheśvarī gaurī mama śaktirnirañjanā /
sāntā satyā sadānandā paraṃ padamiti śrutiḥ //
1.15.d:
सैषा माहेश्वरी गौरी मम शक्तिर्निरञ्जना ।
सान्ता सत्या सदानन्दा परं पदमिति श्रुतिः ॥
1.15.m: This very Gaurī, the great sovereign goddess, is my taintless power; / she is peaceful, true, eternal bliss, the supreme state—thus says the Veda.

1.15.s:
asyāḥ sarvamidaṃ jātamatraiva layameṣyati /
eṣaiva sarvabhūtānāṃ gatīnāmuttamā gatiḥ //
1.15.d:
अस्याः सर्वमिदं जातमत्रैव लयमेष्यति ।
एषैव सर्वभूतानां गतीनामुत्तमा गतिः ॥
1.15.m: From her all this was born, and right here it will dissolve; / she alone is the supreme refuge among all paths for all beings.

1.15.s:
tayāhaṃ saṃgato devyā kevalo niṣkalaḥ paraḥ /
paśyāmyaśeṣamevedaṃ yastad veda sa mucyate //
1.15.d:
तयाहं संगतो देव्या केवलो निष्कलः परः ।
पश्याम्यशेषमेवेदं यस्तद् वेद स मुच्यते ॥
1.15.m: United with that Goddess, I, solitary, partless, and supreme, / behold this entire universe; he who knows this is liberated.

1.15.s:
tasmādanādimadvaitaṃ viṣṇumātmānamīśvaram /
ekameva vijānīdhvaṃ tato yāsyatha nirvṛtim //
1.15.d:
तस्मादनादिमद्वैतं विष्णुमात्मानमीश्वरम् ।
एकमेव विजानीध्वं ततो यास्यथ निर्वृतिम् ॥
1.15.m: Therefore know Viṣṇu, the self, the Lord, to be beginningless, / non-dual, and one alone; then you will attain liberation.

1.15.s:
manyante viṣṇumavyaktamātmānaṃ śraddhayānvitāḥ /
ye bhinnadṛṣṭyāpīśānaṃ pūjayanto na me priyāḥ //
1.15.d:
मन्यन्ते विष्णुमव्यक्तमात्मानं श्रद्धयान्विताः ।
ये भिन्नदृष्ट्यापीशानं पूजयन्तो न मे प्रियाः ॥
1.15.m: Those endowed with faith who consider Viṣṇu the unmanifest Self / but worship Īśāna with a vision of distinction are not dear to me.

1.15.s:
dviṣanti ye jagatsūtiṃ mohitā rauravādiṣu /
pacyamānā na mucyante kalpakoṭiśatairapi //
1.15.d:
द्विषन्ति ये जगत्सूतिं मोहिता रौरवादिषु ।
पच्यमाना न मुच्यन्ते कल्पकोटिशतैरपि ॥
1.15.m: Those who hate the origin of the world, deluded, / are cooked in the Raurava and other hells and are not freed even after hundreds of millions of cosmic ages.

1.15.s:
tasamādaśeṣabhūtānāṃ rakṣako viṣṇuravyayaḥ /
yathāvadiha vijñāya dhyeyaḥ sarvāpadi prabhuḥ //
1.15.d:
तसमादशेषभूतानां रक्षको विष्णुरव्ययः ।
यथावदिह विज्ञाय ध्येयः सर्वापदि प्रभुः ॥
1.15.m: Therefore, knowing properly that the imperishable Viṣṇu is the protector / of all beings, the Lord is to be meditated upon in every misfortune."

1.15.s:
śrutvā bhagavato vākyaṃ devyaḥ sarvagaṇeśvarāḥ /
nemurnārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ devīṃ ca himaśailajām //
1.15.d:
श्रुत्वा भगवतो वाक्यं देव्यः सर्वगणेश्वराः ।
नेमुर्नारायणं देवं देवीं च हिमशैलजाम् ॥
1.15.m: Hearing the word of the Lord, the goddesses and all the leaders of the Gaṇas / bowed to the divine Nārāyaṇa and to the goddess born of the snowy mountain.

1.15.s:
prārthayāmāsurīśāne bhaktiṃ bhaktajanapriye /
bhavānīpādayugale nārāyaṇapadāmbuje //
1.15.d:
प्रार्थयामासुरीशाने भक्तिं भक्तजनप्रिये ।
भवानीपादयुगले नारायणपदाम्बुजे ॥
1.15.m: They prayed for devotion to Īśāna, dear to devoted people, / at the pair of feet of Bhavānī and the lotus feet of Nārāyaṇa.

1.15.s:
tato nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ gaṇeśā mātaro 'pi ca /
na paśyanti jagatsūtiṃ tadbhutamivābhavat //
1.15.d:
ततो नारायणं देवं गणेशा मातरो ऽपि च ।
न पश्यन्ति जगत्सूतिं तद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥
1.15.m: Then the leaders of the Gaṇas and the mothers no longer saw / the divine Nārāyaṇa, the origin of the world; it was like a wonder.

1.15.s:
tadantare mahādaityo hyandhako manmathārditaḥ /
mohito girijāṃ devīmāhartuṃ girimāyayau //
1.15.d:
तदन्तरे महादैत्यो ह्यन्धको मन्मथार्दितः ।
मोहितो गिरिजां देवीमाहर्तुं गिरिमाययौ ॥
1.15.m: In the meantime, the great Daitya Andhaka, tormented by love / and deluded, came to the mountain to abduct the goddess Girijā.

1.15.s:
athānantavapuḥ śrīmān yogī nārāyaṇo 'malaḥ /
tatraivāvirabhūd daityairyuddhāya puruṣottamaḥ //
1.15.d:
अथानन्तवपुः श्रीमान् योगी नारायणो ऽमलः ।
तत्रैवाविरभूद् दैत्यैर्युद्धाय पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
1.15.m: Then the glorious, pure yogin Nārāyaṇa, of infinite forms, / the Supreme Spirit, appeared right there to fight the Daityas.

1.15.s:
kṛtvātha pārśve bhagavantamīśo
yuddhāya viṣṇuṃ gaṇadevamukhyaiḥ /
śilādaputreṇa ca mātṛkābhiḥ
sa kālarudro 'bhijagāma devaḥ //
1.15.d:
कृत्वाथ पार्श्वे भगवन्तमीशो
युद्धाय विष्णुं गणदेवमुख्यैः ।
शिलादपुत्रेण च मातृकाभिः
स कालरुद्रो ऽभिजगाम देवः ॥
1.15.m: Having then placed the divine Viṣṇu at his side, the Lord, / that divine Kalarudra, went forth to battle with the chiefs of the Gaṇas and gods, / with the son of Śilāda, and with the mothers.

1.15.s:
triśūlamādāya kṛśānukalpaṃ
sa devadevaḥ prayayau purastāt /
tamanvayuste gaṇarājavaryā
jagāma devo 'pi sahastrabāhuḥ //
1.15.d:
त्रिशूलमादाय कृशानुकल्पं
स देवदेवः प्रययौ पुरस्तात् ।
तमन्वयुस्ते गणराजवर्या
जगाम देवो ऽपि सहस्त्रबाहुः ॥
1.15.m: Taking a trident resembling fire, / that god of gods set forth in front; / those best of the lords of the Gaṇas followed him, / and the thousand-armed god also went forth.

1.15.s:
rarāja madhye bhagavān surāṇāṃ
vivāhano vāridavarṇavarṇaḥ /
tadā sumeroḥ śikharādhirūḍha-
strilokadṛṣṭirbhagavānivārkaḥ //
1.15.d:
रराज मध्ये भगवान् सुराणां
विवाहनो वारिदवर्णवर्णः ।
तदा सुमेरोः शिखराधिरूढ-
स्त्रिलोकदृष्टिर्भगवानिवार्कः ॥
1.15.m: The Lord shone in the midst of the gods, / having no vehicle, possessing the color of a cloud, / then like the divine sun mounted on the peak of Sumeru, / beholding the three worlds.

1.15.s:
jagatyanādirbhagavānameyo
haraḥ sahastrākṛtirāvirāsīt /
triśūlapāṇirgagane sughoṣaḥ
papāta devopari puṣpavṛṣṭiḥ //
1.15.d:
जगत्यनादिर्भगवानमेयो
हरः सहस्त्राकृतिराविरासीत् ।
त्रिशूलपाणिर्गगने सुघोषः
पपात देवोपरि पुष्पवृष्टिः ॥
1.15.m: In the world, the beginningless, immeasurable Lord / Hara appeared with a thousand forms; / with trident in hand, he roared loudly in the sky, / and a shower of flowers fell upon the god.

1.15.s:
samāgataṃ vīkṣya gaṇeśarājaṃ
samāvṛtaṃ devaripurgaṇeśaiḥ /
yuyodha śakreṇa samātṛkābhi-
r gaṇairaśeṣairamapapradhānaiḥ //
1.15.d:
समागतं वीक्ष्य गणेशराजं
समावृतं देवरिपुर्गणेशैः ।
युयोध शक्रेण समातृकाभि-
र् गणैरशेषैरमपप्रधानैः ॥
1.15.m: Seeing the king of the Gaṇa leaders arrived, / surrounded by the Gaṇa chiefs, the enemy of the gods / fought with Śakra, with the mothers, / and with all the Gaṇas having the immortals as their leaders.

1.15.s:
vijitya sarvānapi bāhuvīryāt
sa saṃyuge śaṃbhumanantadhāma /
samāyayau yatra sa kālarudro
vimānamāruhya vihīnasattvaḥ //
1.15.d:
विजित्य सर्वानपि बाहुवीर्यात्
स संयुगे शंभुमनन्तधाम ।
समाययौ यत्र स कालरुद्रो
विमानमारुह्य विहीनसत्त्वः ॥
1.15.m: Having conquered them all through the might of his arms / in battle, he, deprived of courage, / mounted a celestial vehicle and approached Śambhu of infinite splendor / where that Kalarudra stood.

1.15.s:
dṛṣṭvāndhakaṃ samayāntaṃ bhagavān garuḍadhvajaḥ /
vyājahāra mahādevaṃ bhairavaṃ bhūtibhūṣaṇam //
1.15.d:
दृष्ट्वान्धकं समयान्तं भगवान् गरुडध्वजः ।
व्याजहार महादेवं भैरवं भूतिभूषणम् ॥
1.15.m: Seeing Andhaka approaching, the Lord whose banner is Garuḍa / addressed Mahādeva, the Bhairava adorned with holy ash:

1.15.s:
hantumarhasi daityeśamandhakaṃ lokakaṇṭakam /
tvāmṛte bhagavān śakto hantā nānyo 'sya vidyate //
1.15.d:
हन्तुमर्हसि दैत्येशमन्धकं लोककण्टकम् ।
त्वामृते भगवान् शक्तो हन्ता नान्यो ऽस्य विद्यते ॥
1.15.m: "You ought to slay the lord of Daityas, Andhaka, the thorn of the world; / other than you, there is no other slayer capable of [killing] him, O Lord.

1.15.s:
tvaṃ hartā sarvalokānāṃ kālātmā hyaiśvarī tanuḥ /
stūyate vividhairmantrarvedavidbhirvicakṣaṇaiḥ //
1.15.d:
त्वं हर्ता सर्वलोकानां कालात्मा ह्यैश्वरी तनुः ।
स्तूयते विविधैर्मन्त्रर्वेदविद्भिर्विचक्षणैः ॥
1.15.m: You are the destroyer of all worlds, the soul of Time, the sovereign body / praised with various mantras by wise knowers of the Vedas."

1.15.s:
sa vāsudevasya vaco niśamya bhagavān haraḥ /
nirīkṣya viṣṇuṃ hanane daityandrasya matiṃ dadhau //
1.15.d:
स वासुदेवस्य वचो निशम्य भगवान् हरः ।
निरीक्ष्य विष्णुं हनने दैत्यन्द्रस्य मतिं दधौ ॥
1.15.m: Hearing the word of Vāsudeva and looking at Viṣṇu, / the divine Hara set his mind on slaying the lord of the Daityas.

1.15.s:
jagāma devatānīkaṃ gaṇānāṃ harṣamuttamam /
stuvanti bhairavaṃ devamantarikṣacarā janāḥ //
1.15.d:
जगाम देवतानीकं गणानां हर्षमुत्तमम् ।
स्तुवन्ति भैरवं देवमन्तरिक्षचरा जनाः ॥
1.15.m: The army of gods went forth, and supreme joy arose among the hosts; / beings roaming the atmosphere praised the terrifying god Bhairava:

1.15.s:
jayānanta mahādeva kālamūrte sanātana /
tvamagniḥ sarvabhūtānāmantaścarasi nityaśaḥ //
1.15.d:
जयानन्त महादेव कालमूर्ते सनातन ।
त्वमग्निः सर्वभूतानामन्तश्चरसि नित्यशः ॥
1.15.m: "Victory, O infinite one, O Mahādeva, whose form is time, O eternal one! / You, the fire within all living beings, move constantly.

1.15.s:
tvaṃ yatrajñastvaṃ vaṣaṭkārastvaṃ dhātā hariravyayaḥ /
tvaṃ brahmā tvaṃ mahādevastvaṃ dhāma paramaṃ padam //
1.15.d:
त्वं यत्रज्ञस्त्वं वषट्कारस्त्वं धाता हरिरव्ययः ।
त्वं ब्रह्मा त्वं महादेवस्त्वं धाम परमं पदम् ॥
1.15.m: You know the sacrifice; you are the vaṣaṭ-call; you are the creator, Hari the imperishable; / you are Brahmā; you are Mahādeva; you are the supreme abode, the highest state.

1.15.s:
oṅkāramūrtiryogātmā trayīnetrastrilocanaḥ /
mahāvibhūtirdeveśo jayāśeṣajagatpate //
1.15.d:
ओङ्कारमूर्तिर्योगात्मा त्रयीनेत्रस्त्रिलोचनः ।
महाविभूतिर्देवेशो जयाशेषजगत्पते ॥
1.15.m: Your form is the syllable Oṃ; your self is yoga; your eyes are the three Vedas; you are three-eyed; / of great majesty, lord of the gods: victory to you, O lord of the entire universe!"

1.15.s:
tataḥ kālāgnirudro 'sau gṛhītvāndhakamīśvaraḥ /
triśūlāgreṣu vinyasya prananarta satāṃ gatiḥ //
1.15.d:
ततः कालाग्निरुद्रो ऽसौ गृहीत्वान्धकमीश्वरः ।
त्रिशूलाग्रेषु विन्यस्य प्रननर्त सतां गतिः ॥
1.15.m: Then that lord, Kālāgnirudra, seized Andhaka, / fixed him upon the tips of his trident, and, the refuge of the virtuous, danced.

1.15.s:
dṛṣṭvāndhakaṃ devagaṇāḥ śūlaprotaṃ pitāmahaḥ /
praṇemurīśvaraṃ devaṃ bhairavaṃ bhavamocakam //
1.15.d:
दृष्ट्वान्धकं देवगणाः शूलप्रोतं पितामहः ।
प्रणेमुरीश्वरं देवं भैरवं भवमोचकम् ॥
1.15.m: Seeing Andhaka pierced upon the trident, the hosts of gods and the Grandfather / bowed to the divine lord, Bhairava, the releaser from worldly existence.

1.15.s:
astuvan munayaḥ siddhā jagurgandharvikiṃnarāḥ /
antarikṣe 'psaraḥ saṅghā nṛtyantisma manoramāḥ //
1.15.d:
अस्तुवन् मुनयः सिद्धा जगुर्गन्धर्विकिंनराः ।
अन्तरिक्षे ऽप्सरः सङ्घा नृत्यन्तिस्म मनोरमाः ॥
1.15.m: The sages and Siddhas praised him; Gandharvas and Kiṃnaras sang; / delightful throngs of Apsarases danced in the atmosphere.

1.15.s:
saṃsthāpito 'thaśūlāgre so 'ndhako dagdhakilbiṣaḥ /
utpannākhilavijñānastuṣṭāva parameśvaram //
1.15.d:
संस्थापितो ऽथशूलाग्रे सो ऽन्धको दग्धकिल्बिषः ।
उत्पन्नाखिलविज्ञानस्तुष्टाव परमेश्वरम् ॥
1.15.m: Placed thus upon the trident’s tip, his sins burnt away, / all knowledge arose within Andhaka, and he praised the Supreme Lord:

1.15.s:
andhaka uvāca
namāmi mūrdhnā bhagavantamekaṃ
samāhitā yaṃ vidurīśatattvam /
purātanaṃ puṇyamanantarūpaṃ
kālaṃ kaviṃ yogaviyogahetum //
1.15.d:
अन्धक उवाच
नमामि मूर्ध्ना भगवन्तमेकं
समाहिता यं विदुरीशतत्त्वम् ।
पुरातनं पुण्यमनन्तरूपं
कालं कविं योगवियोगहेतुम् ॥
1.15.m: Andhaka said: / "I bow my head to the one Lord / whom the concentrated know as the truth of the Sovereign, / the ancient, the holy, of infinite form, / Time, the sage, the cause of union and disunion;

1.15.s:
daṃṣṭrākarālaṃ divi nṛtyamānaṃ
hutāśavaktraṃ jvalanārkarūpam /
sahastrapādākṣiśirobhiyuktaṃ
bhavantamekaṃ praṇamāmi rudram //
1.15.d:
दंष्ट्राकरालं दिवि नृत्यमानं
हुताशवक्त्रं ज्वलनार्करूपम् ।
सहस्त्रपादाक्षिशिरोभियुक्तं
भवन्तमेकं प्रणमामि रुद्रम् ॥
1.15.m: fearsome with fangs, dancing in the sky, / whose face is fire, having the form of flame and sun, / endowed with a thousand feet, eyes, and heads: / to you alone, Rudra, I bow.

1.15.s:
jayādidevāmarapūjitāṅghre
vibhāgahīnāmalatattvarūpa /
tvamagnireko bahudhābhipūjyase
vāyvādibhedairakhilātmarūpa //
1.15.d:
जयादिदेवामरपूजिताङ्घ्रे
विभागहीनामलतत्त्वरूप ।
त्वमग्निरेको बहुधाभिपूज्यसे
वाय्वादिभेदैरखिलात्मरूप ॥
1.15.m: Victory, O primal god whose feet are worshipped by the immortals, / whose form is the pure truth without divisions! / You, the single fire, are worshipped in manifold ways / through the divisions of wind and the rest, whose form is the Self of all.

1.15.s:
tvāmekamāhuḥ puruṣaṃ purāṇam
ādityavarṇaṃ tamasaḥ parastāt /
tvaṃ paśyasīdaṃ paripāsyajastraṃ
tvamantako yogigaṇābhijuṣṭaḥ //
1.15.d:
त्वामेकमाहुः पुरुषं पुराणम्
आदित्यवर्णं तमसः परस्तात् ।
त्वं पश्यसीदं परिपास्यजस्त्रं
त्वमन्तको योगिगणाभिजुष्टः ॥
1.15.m: They declare you alone to be the ancient Spirit, / sun-colored, beyond darkness; / you behold this [universe] and protect it unceasingly; / you are the end-maker, frequented by hosts of yogins.

1.15.s:
eko 'ntarātmā bahudhā niviṣṭo
deheṣu dehādiviśeṣahīnaḥ /
tvamātmaśabdaṃ paramātmatattvaṃ
bhavantamāhuḥ śivameva kecit //
1.15.d:
एको ऽन्तरात्मा बहुधा निविष्टो
देहेषु देहादिविशेषहीनः ।
त्वमात्मशब्दं परमात्मतत्त्वं
भवन्तमाहुः शिवमेव केचित् ॥
1.15.m: The one inner Self, entered manifoldly / into bodies, devoid of the distinctions of body and the rest; / you are denoted by the word 'Self', the truth of the supreme Self— / some call you Śiva alone.

1.15.s:
tvamakṣaraṃ brahma paraṃ pavitra-
mānandarūpaṃ praṇavābhidhānam /
tvamīśvaro vedapadeṣu siddhaḥ
svayaṃ prabho 'śeṣaviśeṣahīnaḥ //
1.15.d:
त्वमक्षरं ब्रह्म परं पवित्र-
मानन्दरूपं प्रणवाभिधानम् ।
त्वमीश्वरो वेदपदेषु सिद्धः
स्वयं प्रभो ऽशेषविशेषहीनः ॥
1.15.m: You are the imperishable Brahman, supreme, pure, / whose form is bliss, whose name is the Praṇava; / you are the Lord established in the words of the Veda, / yourself, O sovereign, free from all distinctions.

1.15.s:
tvamindrarūpo varuṇāgnirūpo
haṃsaḥ prāṇo mṛtyurantāsi yajñaḥ /
prajāpatirbhagavānekarudro
nīlagrīvaḥ stūyase vedavidbhiḥ //
1.15.d:
त्वमिन्द्ररूपो वरुणाग्निरूपो
हंसः प्राणो मृत्युरन्तासि यज्ञः ।
प्रजापतिर्भगवानेकरुद्रो
नीलग्रीवः स्तूयसे वेदविद्भिः ॥
1.15.m: You have the form of Indra, the form of Varuṇa and Agni; / you are the Haṃsa, the life-breath, death, the end, and the sacrifice; / you are Prajāpati, the Lord, the one Rudra; / blue-throated, you are praised by the knowers of the Veda.

1.15.s:
nārāyaṇastvaṃ jagatāmathādiḥ
pitāmahastvaṃ prapitāmahaśca /
vedāntaguhyopaniṣatsu gītaḥ
sadāśivastvaṃ parameśvaro 'si //
1.15.d:
नारायणस्त्वं जगतामथादिः
पितामहस्त्वं प्रपितामहश्च ।
वेदान्तगुह्योपनिषत्सु गीतः
सदाशिवस्त्वं परमेश्वरो ऽसि ॥
1.15.m: You are Nārāyaṇa, and the origin of the worlds; / you are the Grandfather, and the Great-Grandfather; / you are sung in the secret Upaniṣads of the Vedānta; / you are Sadāśiva, the Supreme Lord.

1.15.s:
namaḥ parastāt tamasaḥ parasmai
parātmane pañcapadāntarāya /
triśaktyatītāya nirañjanāya
sahastraśaktyāsanasaṃsthitāya //
1.15.d:
नमः परस्तात् तमसः परस्मै
परात्मने पञ्चपदान्तराय ।
त्रिशक्त्यतीताय निरञ्जनाय
सहस्त्रशक्त्यासनसंस्थिताय ॥
1.15.m: Homage to the supreme beyond darkness, / the supreme Self within the five states, / transcendent over the three powers, taintless, / seated on the throne of a thousand powers!

1.15.s:
trimūrtaye 'nandapadātmamūrte
jagannivāsāya jaganmayāya /
namo lalāṭārpitalocanāya
namo janānāṃ hṛdi saṃsthitāya //
1.15.d:
त्रिमूर्तये ऽनन्दपदात्ममूर्ते
जगन्निवासाय जगन्मयाय ।
नमो ललाटार्पितलोचनाय
नमो जनानां हृदि संस्थिताय ॥
1.15.m: To the three-formed, whose form is the state of bliss, / the dwelling of the universe, consisting of the universe; / homage to him whose eye is placed upon his forehead; / homage to him who is seated in the heart of people!

1.15.s:
phaṇīndrahārāya namo 'stu tubhyaṃ
munīndrasiddhārcitapādayugma /
aiśvaryadharmāsanasaṃsthitāya
namaḥ parāntāya bhavodbhavāya //
1.15.d:
फणीन्द्रहाराय नमो ऽस्तु तुभ्यं
मुनीन्द्रसिद्धार्चितपादयुग्म ।
ऐश्वर्यधर्मासनसंस्थिताय
नमः परान्ताय भवोद्भवाय ॥
1.15.m: Homage to you whose necklace is the king of serpents, / whose pair of feet is worshipped by chiefs of sages and Siddhas, / who are seated on the throne of sovereignty and righteousness; / homage to the ultimate end, the source of existence!

1.15.s:
sahastracandrārkavilocanāya
namo 'stu te soma sumadhyamāya /
namo 'stu te deva hiraṇyabāho
namo 'mbikāyāḥ pataye mṛḍāya //
1.15.d:
सहस्त्रचन्द्रार्कविलोचनाय
नमो ऽस्तु ते सोम सुमध्यमाय ।
नमो ऽस्तु ते देव हिरण्यबाहो
नमो ऽम्बिकायाः पतये मृडाय ॥
1.15.m: Homage to you, Soma, whose eyes are a thousand moons and suns, / of slender waist; / homage to you, O god with golden arms; / homage to the husband of Ambikā, the merciful one!

1.15.s:
namo 'tiguhyāya guhāntarāya
vedāntavijñānasuniścitāya /
trikālahīnāmaladhāmadhāmne
namo maheśāya namaḥ śivāya //
1.15.d:
नमो ऽतिगुह्याय गुहान्तराय
वेदान्तविज्ञानसुनिश्चिताय ।
त्रिकालहीनामलधामधाम्ने
नमो महेशाय नमः शिवाय ॥
1.15.m: Homage to the deeply secret, within the cave [of the heart], / well-ascertained by the knowledge of Vedānta, / whose abode is the pure light free from the three times; / homage to Maheśa, homage to Śiva!"

1.15.s:
evaṃ stuvantaṃ bhagavān śūlāgrādavaropya tam /
tuṣṭaḥ provāca hastābhyāṃ spṛṣṭvātha parameśvaraḥ //
1.15.d:
एवं स्तुवन्तं भगवान् शूलाग्रादवरोप्य तम् ।
तुष्टः प्रोवाच हस्ताभ्यां स्पृष्ट्वाथ परमेश्वरः ॥
1.15.m: When he praised him thus, the Lord took him down from the trident's tip; / pleased, the Supreme Lord touched him with both hands and said:

1.15.s:
prīto 'haṃ sarvathā daitya stavenānena sāṃpratam /
saṃprāpya gāṇapatyaṃ me sannidhāne vasāmaraḥ //
1.15.d:
प्रीतो ऽहं सर्वथा दैत्य स्तवेनानेन सांप्रतम् ।
संप्राप्य गाणपत्यं मे सन्निधाने वसामरः ॥
1.15.m: "I am completely pleased now with this hymn, O Daitya; / having attained the status of a leader of my hosts, dwell near me as an immortal,

1.15.s:
arogaśchinnasaṃdeho devairapi supūjitaḥ /
nandīśvarasyānucaraḥ sarvaduḥ khavivarjitaḥ //
1.15.d:
अरोगश्छिन्नसंदेहो देवैरपि सुपूजितः ।
नन्दीश्वरस्यानुचरः सर्वदुः खविवर्जितः ॥
1.15.m: free from sickness, with doubts severed, well worshipped even by the gods, / an attendant of Nandīśvara, rid of all sorrow."

1.15.s:
evaṃ vyāhṛtamātre tu devadevena devatāḥ /
gaṇeśvarā mahādevamandhakaṃ devasannidhau //
1.15.d:
एवं व्याहृतमात्रे तु देवदेवेन देवताः ।
गणेश्वरा महादेवमन्धकं देवसन्निधौ ॥
1.15.m: No sooner had this been uttered by the god of gods, than the deities / and the lords of the hosts [looked upon] Mahādeva and Andhaka in the god's presence—

1.15.s:
sahastrasūryasaṃkāśaṃ trinetraṃ candracihnitam /
nīlakaṇṭhaṃ jaṭāmauliṃ śūlāsaktamahākaram //
1.15.d:
सहस्त्रसूर्यसंकाशं त्रिनेत्रं चन्द्रचिह्नितम् ।
नीलकण्ठं जटामौलिं शूलासक्तमहाकरम् ॥
1.15.m: resembling a thousand suns, three-eyed, marked by the moon, / blue-throated, with matted hair as a crown, his great hand holding a trident.

1.15.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ tuṣṭuvurdaityamāścaryaṃ paramaṃ gatāḥ /
uvāca bhagavān viṣṇurdevadevaṃ smayanniva //
1.15.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं तुष्टुवुर्दैत्यमाश्चर्यं परमं गताः ।
उवाच भगवान् विष्णुर्देवदेवं स्मयन्निव ॥
1.15.m: Seeing that Daitya, they praised him, filled with supreme wonder; / the lord Viṣṇu spoke to the god of gods, as if smiling:

1.15.s:
sthāne tava mahādeva prabhāvaḥ puruṣo mahān /
nekṣate 'jñānajān doṣān gṛhṇāti ca guṇānapi //
1.15.d:
स्थाने तव महादेव प्रभावः पुरुषो महान् ।
नेक्षते ऽज्ञानजान् दोषान् गृह्णाति च गुणानपि ॥
1.15.m: "Fitting is your majesty, O Mahādeva: the Great Spirit / looks not upon faults born of ignorance, but takes even good qualities."

1.15.s:
itīrito 'tha bhairavo gaṇeśadevapuṅgavaiḥ /
sakeśavaḥ sahāndhako jagāma śaṅkarāntikam //
1.15.d:
इतीरितो ऽथ भैरवो गणेशदेवपुङ्गवैः ।
सकेशवः सहान्धको जगाम शङ्करान्तिकम् ॥
1.15.m: Addressed thus by the lords of the hosts and the foremost gods, Bhairava, / accompanied by Keśava and by Andhaka, went into the presence of Śaṅkara.

1.15.s:
nirīkṣya devamāgataṃ saśaṅkaraḥ sahāndhakam /
samādhavaṃ samātṛkaṃ jagāma nirvṛtiṃ haraḥ //
1.15.d:
निरीक्ष्य देवमागतं सशङ्करः सहान्धकम् ।
समाधवं समातृकं जगाम निर्वृतिं हरः ॥
1.15.m: Beholding the god arrived, together with Śaṅkara and Andhaka, / with Mādhava and with the Mothers, Hara experienced delight.

1.15.s:
pragṛhya pāṇineśvaro hiraṇyalocanātmajam /
jagāma yatra śailajā vimānamīśavallabhā //
1.15.d:
प्रगृह्य पाणिनेश्वरो हिरण्यलोचनात्मजम् ।
जगाम यत्र शैलजा विमानमीशवल्लभा ॥
1.15.m: Taking the son of Hiraṇyākṣa by the hand, the Lord / went to the aerial chariot where the Daughter of the Mountain, beloved of the Lord, was.

1.15.s:
vilokya sā samāgataṃ bhavaṃ bhavārtihāriṇam /
avāpa sāndhakaṃ sukhaṃ prasādamandhakaṃ prati //
1.15.d:
विलोक्य सा समागतं भवं भवार्तिहारिणम् ।
अवाप सान्धकं सुखं प्रसादमन्धकं प्रति ॥
1.15.m: Seeing Bhava, who removes the distress of worldly existence, arrived with Andhaka, / she felt joy and favor toward Andhaka.

1.15.s:
athāndhako maheśvarīṃ dadarśa devapārśvagām /
papāta daṇḍavatkṣitau nanāma pādapadmayoḥ //
1.15.d:
अथान्धको महेश्वरीं ददर्श देवपार्श्वगाम् ।
पपात दण्डवत्क्षितौ ननाम पादपद्मयोः ॥
1.15.m: Then Andhaka beheld the Great Goddess standing at the god's side; / he fell to the ground like a staff and bowed to her lotus feet:

1.15.s:
namāmi devavallabhāmanādimadrijāmimām /
yataḥ pradhānapūruṣau nihanti yākhilaṃ jagat //
1.15.d:
नमामि देववल्लभामनादिमद्रिजामिमाम् ।
यतः प्रधानपूरुषौ निहन्ति याखिलं जगत् ॥
1.15.m: "I bow to this beloved of the god, the beginningless Daughter of the Mountain, / from whom are primordial matter and the Spirit, who destroys the entire universe;

1.15.s:
vibhāti yā śivāsane śivena sākamavyayā /
hiraṇmaye 'tinirmale namāmi tāmimāmajām //
1.15.d:
विभाति या शिवासने शिवेन साकमव्यया ।
हिरण्मये ऽतिनिर्मले नमामि तामिमामजाम् ॥
1.15.m: who shines on the seat of Śiva together with Śiva, the imperishable one, / upon the golden, exceedingly pure [throne]—to that unborn one I bow;

1.15.s:
yadantarākhilaṃ jagajjaganti yānti saṃkṣayam /
namāmi yatra tāmumāmaśeṣabedavarjitām //
1.15.d:
यदन्तराखिलं जगज्जगन्ति यान्ति संक्षयम् ।
नमामि यत्र तामुमामशेषबेदवर्जिताम् ॥
1.15.m: within whom is the entire universe, and in whom the worlds go to dissolution; / to that Umā, free of all divisions, I bow;

1.15.s:
na jāyate nahīyate na vardhate ca tāmumām /
namāmi yā guṇātigā girīśaputrikāmimām //
1.15.d:
न जायते नहीयते न वर्धते च तामुमाम् ।
नमामि या गुणातिगा गिरीशपुत्रिकामिमाम् ॥
1.15.m: who is not born, does not diminish, and does not increase—to that Umā / who transcends the qualities, the daughter of the Mountain-Lord, I bow.

1.15.s:
kṣamasva devi śailaje kṛtaṃ mayā vimāhataḥ /
surāsurairyadarcitaṃ namāmi te padāmbujam //
1.15.d:
क्षमस्व देवि शैलजे कृतं मया विमाहतः ।
सुरासुरैर्यदर्चितं नमामि ते पदाम्बुजम् ॥
1.15.m: Pardon, O goddess, Daughter of the Mountain, what was done by me in delusion; / I bow to your lotus foot, which is worshipped by gods and Asuras."

1.15.s:
itthaṃ bhagavatī gaurī bhaktinamreṇa pārvatī /
saṃstutā daityapatinā putratve jagṛhe 'ndhakam //
1.15.d:
इत्थं भगवती गौरी भक्तिनम्रेण पार्वती ।
संस्तुता दैत्यपतिना पुत्रत्वे जगृहे ऽन्धकम् ॥
1.15.m: Praised in this way by the lord of the Daityas bowed in devotion, / the divine Gaurī, Pārvatī, accepted Andhaka as a son.

1.15.s:
tataḥ sa mātṛbhiḥ sārdhaṃ bhairavo rudrasaṃbhavaḥ /
jagāmānujñayā śaṃbhoḥ pātālaṃ parameśvaraḥ //
1.15.d:
ततः स मातृभिः सार्धं भैरवो रुद्रसंभवः ।
जगामानुज्ञया शंभोः पातालं परमेश्वरः ॥
1.15.m: Then that Bhairava, born of Rudra, the supreme lord, / went together with the Mothers to the netherworld by the permission of Śambhu,

1.15.s:
yatra sā tāmasī viṣṇormūrtiḥ saṃhārakārikā /
samāste hariravyakto nṛsiṃhākṛtirīśvaraḥ //
1.15.d:
यत्र सा तामसी विष्णोर्मूर्तिः संहारकारिका ।
समास्ते हरिरव्यक्तो नृसिंहाकृतिरीश्वरः ॥
1.15.m: where that dark form of Viṣṇu that causes dissolution, / the unmanifest Hari, the Lord in the form of a man-lion, resides.

1.15.s:
tato 'nantākṛtiḥ śaṃbhuḥ śeṣeṇāpi supūjitaḥ /
kālāgnirudro bhagavān yuyojātmānamātmani //
1.15.d:
ततो ऽनन्ताकृतिः शंभुः शेषेणापि सुपूजितः ।
कालाग्निरुद्रो भगवान् युयोजात्मानमात्मनि ॥
1.15.m: Then Śambhu, of infinite form, well worshipped even by Śeṣa, / the divine Kālāgnirudra, united himself within the Self.

1.15.s:
yuñjatastasya devasya sarvā evātha mātaraḥ /
bubhukṣitā mahādevaṃ praṇamyāhustriśūlinam //
1.15.d:
युञ्जतस्तस्य देवस्य सर्वा एवाथ मातरः ।
बुभुक्षिता महादेवं प्रणम्याहुस्त्रिशूलिनम् ॥
1.15.m: As that god was uniting [himself], all the Mothers, / being hungry, bowed to Mahādeva, the trident-bearer, and said:

1.15.s:
mātara ūcuḥ
bubhukṣitā mahādeva anujñā dīyatāṃ tvayā /
trailokyaṃ bhakṣayiṣyāmo nānyathā tṛptirastinaḥ //
1.15.d:
मातर ऊचुः
बुभुक्षिता महादेव अनुज्ञा दीयतां त्वया ।
त्रैलोक्यं भक्षयिष्यामो नान्यथा तृप्तिरस्तिनः ॥
1.15.m: The Mothers said: / "We are hungry, O Mahādeva; let permission be given by you: / we will consume the three worlds; otherwise we have no satisfaction."

1.15.s:
etāvaduktvā vacanaṃ mātaro viṣṇusaṃbhavāḥ /
bhakṣayāñcakrire sarvaṃ trailokyaṃ sacarācaram //
1.15.d:
एतावदुक्त्वा वचनं मातरो विष्णुसंभवाः ।
भक्षयाञ्चक्रिरे सर्वं त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥
1.15.m:
Having spoken these words, the Mothers born from Viṣṇu
consumed the entire triple world, with its moving and unmoving beings.

1.15.s:
tataḥ sa bhairavo devo nṛsiṃhavapuṣaṃ harim /
dadhyau nārāyaṇaṃ devaṃ kṣaṇātprādurabhūddhariḥ //
1.15.d:
ततः स भैरवो देवो नृसिंहवपुषं हरिम् ।
दध्यौ नारायणं देवं क्षणात्प्रादुरभूद्धरिः ॥
1.15.m:
Then that god Bhairava meditated upon Hari in the form of a man-lion,
the god Nārāyaṇa; in an instant Hari appeared.

1.15.s:
vijñāpayāmāsa ca taṃ bhakṣayantīha mātaraḥ /
