nivārayāśu trailokyaṃ tvadīyā bhagavanniti //
1.15.d:
विज्ञापयामास च तं भक्षयन्तीह मातरः ।
निवारयाशु त्रैलोक्यं त्वदीया भगवन्निति ॥
1.15.m:
And he addressed him: 'Here the Mothers are devouring [everything];
swiftly restrain them from the triple world, O Lord, for they are yours!'

1.15.s:
saṃsmṛtā viṣṇunā devyo nṛsiṃhavapuṣā punaḥ /
upatasthurmahādevaṃ narasiṃhākṛtiṃ ca tam //
1.15.d:
संस्मृता विष्णुना देव्यो नृसिंहवपुषा पुनः ।
उपतस्थुर्महादेवं नरसिंहाकृतिं च तम् ॥
1.15.m:
Remembered by Viṣṇu in the form of a man-lion, the goddesses again
approached Mahādeva and him who had the form of a man-lion.

1.15.s:
saṃprāpya sannidhiṃ viṣṇoḥ sarvāḥ saṃhārakārikāḥ /
pradaduḥ śaṃbhave śaktiṃ bhairavāyātitejase //
1.15.d:
संप्राप्य सन्निधिं विष्णोः सर्वाः संहारकारिकाः ।
प्रददुः शंभवे शक्तिं भैरवायातितेजसे ॥
1.15.m:
Attaining the presence of Viṣṇu, all those who bring about dissolution
offered their power to Śambhu, the exceedingly radiant Bhairava.

1.15.s:
apaśyaṃstā jagatsūtiṃ nṛsiṃhamatha bhairavam /
kṣaṇādekatvamāpannaṃ śeṣāhiṃ cāpi mātaraḥ //
1.15.d:
अपश्यंस्ता जगत्सूतिं नृसिंहमथ भैरवम् ।
क्षणादेकत्वमापन्नं शेषाहिं चापि मातरः ॥
1.15.m:
Then the Mothers beheld the source of the world, the man-lion and Bhairava,
and the serpent Śeṣa as well, united in oneness in a single instant.

1.15.s:
vyājahāra hṛṣīkeśo ye bhaktāḥ śūlapāṇinaḥ /
ye ca māṃ saṃsmarantīha pālanīyāḥ prayatnataḥ //
1.15.d:
व्याजहार हृषीकेशो ये भक्ताः शूलपाणिनः ।
ये च मां संस्मरन्तीह पालनीयाः प्रयत्नतः ॥
1.15.m:
Hṛṣīkeśa declared: 'Those who are devotees of the trident-bearer,
and those who remember me here, are to be protected with every effort.

1.15.s:
mamaiva mūrtiratulā sarvasaṃhārakārikā /
maheśvarāṃśasaṃbhūtā bhuktimuktipradā tviyam //
1.15.d:
ममैव मूर्तिरतुला सर्वसंहारकारिका ।
महेश्वरांशसंभूता भुक्तिमुक्तिप्रदा त्वियम् ॥
1.15.m:
This matchless form of mine is the cause of universal destruction;
born of a portion of Maheśvara, it grants both enjoyment and liberation.

1.15.s:
ananto bhagavān kālo dvidhāvasthā mamaiva tu /
tāmasī rājasī mūrtirdevadevaścaturmukhaḥ //
1.15.d:
अनन्तो भगवान् कालो द्विधावस्था ममैव तु ।
तामसी राजसी मूर्तिर्देवदेवश्चतुर्मुखः ॥
1.15.m:
Endless Lord Time is an twofold state of mine:
the form endowed with darkness, and the form endowed with passion, the god of gods, the four-faced one.

1.15.s:
so 'yaṃ devo durādharṣaḥ kālo lokaprakālanaḥ /
bhakṣayiṣyati kalpānte rudrātmā nikhilaṃ jagat //
1.15.d:
सो ऽयं देवो दुराधर्षः कालो लोकप्रकालनः ।
भक्षयिष्यति कल्पान्ते रुद्रात्मा निखिलं जगत् ॥
1.15.m:
This invincible god, Time, the driver of the worlds,
whose self is Rudra, will consume the entire world at the end of the cosmic age.

1.15.s:
yā sā vimohikā mūrtirmama nārāyaṇāhvayā /
sattvodriktājagat kṛtsnaṃ saṃsthāpayati nityadā //
1.15.d:
या सा विमोहिका मूर्तिर्मम नारायणाह्वया ।
सत्त्वोद्रिक्ताजगत् कृत्स्नं संस्थापयति नित्यदा ॥
1.15.m:
That deluding form of mine named Nārāyaṇa,
abounding in goodness, perpetually establishes the whole world.

1.15.s:
sa hi viṣṇuḥ paraṃ brahma paramātmā parā gatiḥ /
mūlaprakṛtiravyaktā sadānandeti kathyate //
1.15.d:
स हि विष्णुः परं ब्रह्म परमात्मा परा गतिः ।
मूलप्रकृतिरव्यक्ता सदानन्देति कथ्यते ॥
1.15.m:
For he is Viṣṇu, the supreme Brahman, the Supreme Self, the ultimate goal;
he is called the unmanifest primordial matter, eternal bliss.'

1.15.s:
ityevaṃ bodhitā devyo viṣṇunā viśvamātaraḥ /
prapedire mahādevaṃ tameva śaraṇaṃ harim //
1.15.d:
इत्येवं बोधिता देव्यो विष्णुना विश्वमातरः ।
प्रपेदिरे महादेवं तमेव शरणं हरिम् ॥
1.15.m:
Instructed thus by Viṣṇu, the goddesses, Mothers of the universe,
took refuge in Mahādeva, and in that very Hari.

1.15.s:
etad vaḥ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ mayāndhakanibarhaṇam /
māhātmyaṃ devadevasya bhairavasyāmitaujasaḥ //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge pañcadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.15.d:
एतद् वः कथितं सर्वं मयान्धकनिबर्हणम् ।
माहात्म्यं देवदेवस्य भैरवस्यामितौजसः ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे पञ्चदशो ऽध्यायः
1.15.m:
All this has been related to you by me: the destruction of Andhaka
and the majesty of the god of gods, Bhairava of boundless radiance.

Thus ends the fifteenth chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand [verses] in the holy Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.16.s:
śrīkūrma uvāca
andake nigṛhīte vai prahlādasya mahātmanaḥ /
virocano nāma suto babhūva nṛpatiḥ purā //
1.16.d:
श्रीकूर्म उवाच
अन्दके निगृहीते वै प्रह्लादस्य महात्मनः ।
विरोचनो नाम सुतो बभूव नृपतिः पुरा ॥
1.16.m:
The holy Tortoise said:
When Andhaka was subdued, indeed, a son named Virocana
became king of the noble-souled Prahlāda of old.

1.16.s:
devāñjitvā sadevendrāna bahūn varṣān mahāsuraḥ /
pālayāmāsa dharmeṇa trailokyaṃ sacarācaram //
1.16.d:
देवाञ्जित्वा सदेवेन्द्रान बहून् वर्षान् महासुरः ।
पालयामास धर्मेण त्रैलोक्यं सचराचरम् ॥
1.16.m:
Having conquered the gods along with the lords of the gods, the great Asura
ruled the triple world, with its moving and unmoving beings, righteously for many years.

1.16.s:
tasyaivaṃ vartamānasya kadācid viṣṇucoditaḥ /
sanatkumāro bhagavān puraṃ prāpa mahāmuniḥ //
1.16.d:
तस्यैवं वर्तमानस्य कदाचिद् विष्णुचोदितः ।
सनत्कुमारो भगवान् पुरं प्राप महामुनिः ॥
1.16.m:
While he was living in this manner, once, impelled by Viṣṇu,
the venerable Sanatkumāra, the great sage, arrived at his city.

1.16.s:
dṛṣṭvā sihāsanagato brahmaputraṃ mahāsuraḥ /
nanāmotthāya śirasā prāñjalirvākyamabravīt //
1.16.d:
दृष्ट्वा सिहासनगतो ब्रह्मपुत्रं महासुरः ।
ननामोत्थाय शिरसा प्राञ्जलिर्वाक्यमब्रवीत् ॥
1.16.m:
Seeing the son of Brahmā while seated on his throne, the great Asura
rose, bowed with his head, and, with folded hands, spoke these words:

1.16.s:
dhanyo 'smyanugṛhīto 'smi saṃprāpto me purātanaḥ /
yogīśvaro 'dya bhagavān yato 'sau brahmavit svayam //
1.16.d:
धन्यो ऽस्म्यनुगृहीतो ऽस्मि संप्राप्तो मे पुरातनः ।
योगीश्वरो ऽद्य भगवान् यतो ऽसौ ब्रह्मवित् स्वयम् ॥
1.16.m:
'I am blessed, I am favored; the ancient master of yoga,
the venerable one, has arrived at my [city] today, since he himself knows Brahman.

1.16.s:
kimarthamāgato brahman svayaṃ devaḥ pitāmahaḥ /
brūhi me brahmaṇaḥ putra kiṃ kāryaṃ karavāṇyaham //
1.16.d:
किमर्थमागतो ब्रह्मन् स्वयं देवः पितामहः ।
ब्रूहि मे ब्रह्मणः पुत्र किं कार्यं करवाण्यहम् ॥
1.16.m:
For what reason have you come, O Brahman? Grandfather, the god himself!
Tell me, son of Brahmā, what service may I perform?'

1.16.s:
so 'bravīd bhagavān devo dharmayuktaṃ mahāsuram /
draṣṭumabhyāgato 'haṃ vai bhavantaṃ bhāgyavānasi //
1.16.d:
सो ऽब्रवीद् भगवान् देवो धर्मयुक्तं महासुरम् ।
द्रष्टुमभ्यागतो ऽहं वै भवन्तं भाग्यवानसि ॥
1.16.m:
The venerable god said to the righteous great Asura:
'I have indeed come to see you; you are fortunate.

1.16.s:
sudurlabhā nītireṣā daityānāṃ daityasattama /
triloke dhārmiko nūnaṃ tvādṛśo 'nyo na vidyate //
1.16.d:
सुदुर्लभा नीतिरेषा दैत्यानां दैत्यसत्तम ।
त्रिलोके धार्मिको नूनं त्वादृशो ऽन्यो न विद्यते ॥
1.16.m:
Such conduct among Daityas is exceedingly rare, O best of Daityas!
Surely no other righteous person like you exists in the three worlds.'

1.16.s:
ityukto 'surarājastaṃ punaḥ prāha mahāmunim /
dharmāṇāṃ paramaṃ dharmaṃ brūhi me brahmavittama //
1.16.d:
इत्युक्तो ऽसुरराजस्तं पुनः प्राह महामुनिम् ।
धर्माणां परमं धर्मं ब्रूहि मे ब्रह्मवित्तम ॥
1.16.m:
Addressed thus, the king of Asuras spoke again to that great sage:
'Tell me the supreme duty among duties, O best of knowers of Brahman!'

1.16.s:
so 'bravīd bhagavān yogī daityendrāya mahātmane /
sarvaguhyatamaṃ dharmamātmajñānamanuttamam //
1.16.d:
सो ऽब्रवीद् भगवान् योगी दैत्येन्द्राय महात्मने ।
सर्वगुह्यतमं धर्ममात्मज्ञानमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.16.m:
The venerable yogin declared to the noble-souled lord of Daityas
the most secret duty of all: unsurpassable knowledge of the Self.

1.16.s:
sa labdhvā paramaṃ jñānaṃ dattvā ca gurudakṣiṇām /
nidhāya putre tadrājyaṃ yogābhyāsarato 'bhavat //
1.16.d:
स लब्ध्वा परमं ज्ञानं दत्त्वा च गुरुदक्षिणाम् ।
निधाय पुत्रे तद्राज्यं योगाभ्यासरतो ऽभवत् ॥
1.16.m:
Having obtained supreme knowledge and given a fee to the guru,
he placed that kingdom upon his son and became devoted to the practice of yoga.

1.16.s:
sa tasya putro matimān balirnāma mahāsuraḥ /
brahmaṇyo dhārmiko 'tyarthaṃ vijigye 'tha purandaram //
1.16.d:
स तस्य पुत्रो मतिमान् बलिर्नाम महासुरः ।
ब्रह्मण्यो धार्मिको ऽत्यर्थं विजिग्ये ऽथ पुरन्दरम् ॥
1.16.m:
That son of his, the intelligent great Asura named Bali,
devoted to Brahmins and exceedingly righteous, then conquered Indra.

1.16.s:
kṛtvā tena mahad yuddhaṃ śakraḥ sarvāmarairvṛtaḥ /
jagāma nirjito viṣṇuṃ devaṃ śaraṇamacyutam //
1.16.d:
कृत्वा तेन महद् युद्धं शक्रः सर्वामरैर्वृतः ।
जगाम निर्जितो विष्णुं देवं शरणमच्युतम् ॥
1.16.m:
Having fought a great battle with him, Śakra, surrounded by all the immortals,
was defeated and went for refuge to the god Viṣṇu, Acyuta.

1.16.s:
tadantare 'ditirdevī devamātā suduḥ khitā /
daityendrāṇāṃ vadhārthāya putro me syāditi svayam //
1.16.d:
तदन्तरे ऽदितिर्देवी देवमाता सुदुः खिता ।
दैत्येन्द्राणां वधार्थाय पुत्रो मे स्यादिति स्वयम् ॥
1.16.m:
Meanwhile the goddess Aditi, mother of the gods, deeply grieved,
[wished] herself: 'May I have a son for the slaying of the Daitya lords.'

1.16.s:
tatāpa sumahad ghoraṃ taporāśistapaḥ param /
prapannā viṣṇumavyaktaṃ śaraṇyaṃ śaraṇaṃ harim //
1.16.d:
तताप सुमहद् घोरं तपोराशिस्तपः परम् ।
प्रपन्ना विष्णुमव्यक्तं शरण्यं शरणं हरिम् ॥
1.16.m:
A heap of ascetic power, she performed very great and dreadful, supreme austerity,
taking refuge in the unmanifest Viṣṇu, Hari, who offers shelter.

1.16.s:
kṛtvā hṛtpadmakiñjalke niṣkalaṃ paramaṃ padam /
vāsudevamanādyantamānandaṃ vyoma kevalam //
1.16.d:
कृत्वा हृत्पद्मकिञ्जल्के निष्कलं परमं पदम् ।
वासुदेवमनाद्यन्तमानन्दं व्योम केवलम् ॥
1.16.m:
Placing in the filaments of the heart-lotus the partless supreme abode,
Vāsudeva, without beginning or end, bliss, pure ether, [she meditated].

1.16.s:
prasanno bhagavān viṣṇuḥ śaṅkhacakragadādharaḥ /
āvirbabhūva yogātmā devamātuḥ puro hariḥ //
1.16.d:
प्रसन्नो भगवान् विष्णुः शङ्खचक्रगदाधरः ।
आविर्बभूव योगात्मा देवमातुः पुरो हरिः ॥
1.16.m:
Pleased, the venerable Viṣṇu, wielder of the conch, discus, and mace,
Hari, the self of yoga, appeared before the mother of the gods.

1.16.s:
dṛṣṭvā samāgataṃ viṣṇumaditirbhaktisaṃyutā /
mene kṛtārthamātmānaṃ toṣayāmāsa keśavam //
1.16.d:
दृष्ट्वा समागतं विष्णुमदितिर्भक्तिसंयुता ।
मेने कृतार्थमात्मानं तोषयामास केशवम् ॥
1.16.m:
Seeing that Viṣṇu had arrived, Aditi, full of devotion,
considered herself fulfilled and propitiated Keśava:

1.16.s:
aditiruvāca
jayāśeṣaduḥ khaughanāśaikaheto
jayānantamāhātmyayogābhiyukta /
jayānādimadhyāntavijñānamūrte
jayāśeṣakalpāmalānandarūpa //
1.16.d:
अदितिरुवाच
जयाशेषदुः खौघनाशैकहेतो
जयानन्तमाहात्म्ययोगाभियुक्त ।
जयानादिमध्यान्तविज्ञानमूर्ते
जयाशेषकल्पामलानन्दरूप ॥
1.16.m:
Aditi said:
'Victory to the sole cause of the destruction of the entire flood of sorrow!
Victory to the one intent on the yoga of endless majesty!
Victory to the form of consciousness without beginning, middle, or end!
Victory to the form of pure bliss through all cosmic ages!

1.16.s:
namo viṣṇave kālarūpāya tubhyaṃ
namo nārasiṃhāya śeṣāya tubhyam /
namaḥ kālarudrāya saṃhārakartre
namo vāsudevāya tubhyaṃ namaste //
1.16.d:
नमो विष्णवे कालरूपाय तुभ्यं
नमो नारसिंहाय शेषाय तुभ्यम् ।
नमः कालरुद्राय संहारकर्त्रे
नमो वासुदेवाय तुभ्यं नमस्ते ॥
1.16.m:
Homage to you, Viṣṇu, whose form is Time!
Homage to you, the Man-Lion, Śeṣa!
Homage to Kāla-Rudra, the maker of dissolution!
Homage to Vāsudeva! Homage, homage to you!

1.16.s:
namo viśvamāyāvidhānāya tubhyaṃ
namo yogagamyāya satyāya tubhyam /
namo dharmavijñānaniṣṭhāya tubhyaṃ
namaste varāhāya bhūyo namaste //
1.16.d:
नमो विश्वमायाविधानाय तुभ्यं
नमो योगगम्याय सत्याय तुभ्यम् ।
नमो धर्मविज्ञाननिष्ठाय तुभ्यं
नमस्ते वराहाय भूयो नमस्ते ॥
1.16.m:
Homage to you, the arranger of the world's illusory creative power!
Homage to you, reachable by yoga, who are truth!
Homage to you, intent on duty and wisdom!
Homage to you, the Boar! Repeated homage to you!

1.16.s:
namaste sahastrārkacandrābhamūrte
namo vedavijñānadharmābhigamya /
namo devadevādidevādideva
prabho viśvayone 'tha bhūyo namaste //
1.16.d:
नमस्ते सहस्त्रार्कचन्द्राभमूर्ते
नमो वेदविज्ञानधर्माभिगम्य ।
नमो देवदेवादिदेवादिदेव
प्रभो विश्वयोने ऽथ भूयो नमस्ते ॥
1.16.m:
Homage to you, whose form has the radiance of a thousand suns and moons!
Homage to the one reachable through Vedic wisdom and duty!
Homage to the god of gods, the primordial god, the first of all gods!
O Lord, source of the universe, repeated homage to you!

1.16.s:
namaḥ śaṃbhave satyaniṣṭhāya tubhyaṃ
namo hetave viśvarūpāya tubhyam /
namo yogapīṭhāntarasthāya tubhyaṃ
śivāyaikarūpāya bhūyo namaste //
1.16.d:
नमः शंभवे सत्यनिष्ठाय तुभ्यं
नमो हेतवे विश्वरूपाय तुभ्यम् ।
नमो योगपीठान्तरस्थाय तुभ्यं
शिवायैकरूपाय भूयो नमस्ते ॥
1.16.m:
Homage to you, Śambhu, grounded in truth!
Homage to you, the cause, whose form is the universe!
Homage to you, dwelling within the seat of yoga!
To Śiva of unitary form, repeated homage to you!'

1.16.s:
evaṃ sa bhagavān kṛṣṇo devamātrā jaganmayaḥ /
toṣitaśchandayāmāsa vareṇa prahasanniva //
1.16.d:
एवं स भगवान् कृष्णो देवमात्रा जगन्मयः ।
तोषितश्छन्दयामास वरेण प्रहसन्निव ॥
1.16.m:
Thus propitiated by the mother of the gods, the venerable Kṛṣṇa,
embodying the universe, invited her [to ask] for a boon, as if smiling:

1.16.s:
praṇamya śirasā bhūmau sā vabre varamuttamam /
tvāmeva putraṃ devānāṃ hitāya varaye varam //
1.16.d:
प्रणम्य शिरसा भूमौ सा वब्रे वरमुत्तमम् ।
त्वामेव पुत्रं देवानां हिताय वरये वरम् ॥
1.16.m:
Bowing with her head to the ground, she chose the supreme boon:
'I choose the boon of yourself as my son for the welfare of the gods.'

1.16.s:
tathāstvityāha bhagavān prapannajanavatsalaḥ /
dattvā varānaprameyastatraivāntaradhīyata //
1.16.d:
तथास्त्वित्याह भगवान् प्रपन्नजनवत्सलः ।
दत्त्वा वरानप्रमेयस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥
1.16.m:
'Let it be so,' said the venerable one, compassionate to those who seek refuge.
Having granted the boons, the immeasurable one vanished on that very spot.

1.16.s:
tato bahutithe kāle bhagavantaṃ janārdanam /
dadhāra garbhaṃ devānāṃ mātā nārāyaṇaṃ svayam //
1.16.d:
ततो बहुतिथे काले भगवन्तं जनार्दनम् ।
दधार गर्भं देवानां माता नारायणं स्वयम् ॥
1.16.m:
Then, after a long time, the mother of the gods
herself bore the embryo, the venerable Janārdana, Nārāyaṇa.

1.16.s:
samāviṣṭe hṛṣīkeśe devamāturathodaram /
utpātā jajñire ghorā balervairocaneḥ pure //
1.16.d:
समाविष्टे हृषीकेशे देवमातुरथोदरम् ।
उत्पाता जज्ञिरे घोरा बलेर्वैरोचनेः पुरे ॥
1.16.m:
When Hṛṣīkeśa had entered the womb of the mother of the gods,
dreadful omens arose in the city of Bali, son of Virocana.

1.16.s:
nirīkṣya sarvānutpātān daityendro bhayavihvalaḥ /
prahlādamasuraṃ vṛddhaṃ praṇamyāha pitāmaham //
1.16.d:
निरीक्ष्य सर्वानुत्पातान् दैत्येन्द्रो भयविह्वलः ।
प्रह्लादमसुरं वृद्धं प्रणम्याह पितामहम् ॥
1.16.m:
Observing all the portents, the lord of Daityas, agitated with fear,
bowed to the aged Asura Prahlāda, his grandfather, and said:

1.16.s:
baliruvāca
pitāmaha mahāprājña jāyante 'smatpure 'dhunā /
kimutpātā bhavet kāryamasmākaṃ kiṃnimittakāḥ //
1.16.d:
बलिरुवाच
पितामह महाप्राज्ञ जायन्ते ऽस्मत्पुरे ऽधुना ।
किमुत्पाता भवेत् कार्यमस्माकं किंनिमित्तकाः ॥
1.16.m:
Bali said:
'Grandfather, of great wisdom, why are portents arising
in our city now? What might be [their] effect for us, and what is their cause?'

1.16.s:
niśamya tasya vacanaṃ ciraṃ dhyātvā mahāsuraḥ /
namaskṛtya hṛṣīkeśamidaṃ vacanamabravīt //
1.16.d:
निशम्य तस्य वचनं चिरं ध्यात्वा महासुरः ।
नमस्कृत्य हृषीकेशमिदं वचनमब्रवीत् ॥
1.16.m:
Hearing his words, the great Asura meditated for a long time;
bowing to Hṛṣīkeśa, he spoke these words:

1.16.s:
prahlāda uvāca
yo yajñairijyate viṣṇuryasya sarvamidaṃ jagat /
dadhārāsuranāśārthaṃ mātā taṃ tridivaukasām //
1.16.d:
प्रह्लाद उवाच
यो यज्ञैरिज्यते विष्णुर्यस्य सर्वमिदं जगत् ।
दधारासुरनाशार्थं माता तं त्रिदिवौकसाम् ॥
1.16.m:
Prahlāda said:
Viṣṇu, who is worshipped with sacrifices, to whom belongs this entire universe—
for the destruction of the asuras, the mother of the dwellers of heaven bore him.

1.16.s:
yasmādabhinnaṃ sakalaṃ bhidyate yo 'khilādapi /
sa vāsudevo devānāṃ māturdehaṃ samāviśat //
1.16.d:
यस्मादभिन्नं सकलं भिद्यते यो ऽखिलादपि ।
स वासुदेवो देवानां मातुर्देहं समाविशत् ॥
1.16.m:
He from whom everything is not distinct, and who is distinct even from all,
that Vāsudeva entered the body of the mother of the gods.

1.16.s:
na yasya devā jānanti svarūpaṃ paramārthataḥ /
sa viṣṇuraditerdehaṃ svecchayādya samāviśat //
1.16.d:
न यस्य देवा जानन्ति स्वरूपं परमार्थतः ।
स विष्णुरदितेर्देहं स्वेच्छयाद्य समाविशत् ॥
1.16.m:
He whose essential nature the gods do not know in the highest truth,
that Viṣṇu has today entered the body of Aditi of his own will.

1.16.s:
yasmād bhavanti bhūtāni yatra saṃyānti saṃkṣayam /
so 'vatīrṇo mahāyogī purāṇapuruṣo hariḥ //
1.16.d:
यस्माद् भवन्ति भूतानि यत्र संयान्ति संक्षयम् ।
सो ऽवतीर्णो महायोगी पुराणपुरुषो हरिः ॥
1.16.m:
He from whom beings arise, and into whom they go to destruction,
that Hari, the great yogin, the ancient spirit, has descended.

1.16.s:
na yatra vidyate nāmajātyādiparikalpanā /
sattāmātrātmarūpo 'sau viṣṇuraṃśena jāyate //
1.16.d:
न यत्र विद्यते नामजात्यादिपरिकल्पना ।
सत्तामात्रात्मरूपो ऽसौ विष्णुरंशेन जायते ॥
1.16.m:
In whom there is no conception of name, genus, or the like,
he, whose nature is pure existence, Viṣṇu, is born through a portion [of himself].

1.16.s:
yasya sā jagatāṃ mātā śaktistaddharmadhāriṇī /
māyā bhagavatī lakṣmīḥ so 'vatīrṇo janārdanaḥ //
1.16.d:
यस्य सा जगतां माता शक्तिस्तद्धर्मधारिणी ।
माया भगवती लक्ष्मीः सो ऽवतीर्णो जनार्दनः ॥
1.16.m:
He whose power is that mother of the worlds, upholding his divine nature,
the illusory creative power, the blessed Lakṣmī—that Janārdana has descended.

1.16.s:
yasya sā tāmasī mūrtiḥ śaṅkaro rājasī tanuḥ /
brahmā saṃjāyate viṣṇuraṃśenaikena sattvabhṛt //
1.16.d:
यस्य सा तामसी मूर्तिः शङ्करो राजसी तनुः ।
ब्रह्मा संजायते विष्णुरंशेनैकेन सत्त्वभृत् ॥
1.16.m:
He whose form of darkness is Śaṅkara, whose form of passion is Brahmā,
Viṣṇu is born through one portion, bearing goodness.

1.16.s:
itthaṃ vicintya govindaṃ bhaktinamreṇa cetasā /
tameva gaccha śaraṇaṃ tato yāsyasi nirvṛtim //
1.16.d:
इत्थं विचिन्त्य गोविन्दं भक्तिनम्रेण चेतसा ।
तमेव गच्छ शरणं ततो यास्यसि निर्वृतिम् ॥
1.16.m:
Having thus reflected upon Govinda with a mind bowed in devotion,
go to him alone for refuge; then you shall attain supreme peace.

1.16.s:
tataḥ prahlādavacanād balirvairocanirharim /
jagāma śaraṇaṃ viśvaṃ pālayāmāsa dharmataḥ //
1.16.d:
ततः प्रह्लादवचनाद् बलिर्वैरोचनिर्हरिम् ।
जगाम शरणं विश्वं पालयामास धर्मतः ॥
1.16.m:
Then, at the word of Prahlāda, Bali, the son of Virocana, went to Hari for refuge,
and protected the universe in accordance with righteousness.

1.16.s:
kāle prāpte mahāviṣṇuṃ devānāṃ harṣavardhanam /
asūta kaśyapāccainaṃ devamātāditiḥ svayam //
1.16.d:
काले प्राप्ते महाविष्णुं देवानां हर्षवर्धनम् ।
असूत कश्यपाच्चैनं देवमातादितिः स्वयम् ॥
1.16.m:
When the time arrived, Aditi herself, mother of the gods, gave birth
to Mahāviṣṇu from Kaśyapa, increasing the joy of the gods.

1.16.s:
caturbhujaṃ viśālākṣaṃ śrīvatsāṅkitavakṣasam /
nīlameghapratīkāśaṃ bhrājamānaṃ śriyāvṛtam //
1.16.d:
चतुर्भुजं विशालाक्षं श्रीवत्साङ्कितवक्षसम् ।
नीलमेघप्रतीकाशं भ्राजमानं श्रियावृतम् ॥
1.16.m:
Four-armed, large-eyed, his chest marked with the Śrīvatsa,
resembling a dark-blue cloud, radiant, enveloped in splendor.

1.16.s:
upatasthuḥ surāḥ sarve siddhāḥ sādhyāśca cāraṇāḥ /
upendramindrapramukhā brahmā carṣigamairvṛtaḥ //
1.16.d:
उपतस्थुः सुराः सर्वे सिद्धाः साध्याश्च चारणाः ।
उपेन्द्रमिन्द्रप्रमुखा ब्रह्मा चर्षिगमैर्वृतः ॥
1.16.m:
All the gods, siddhas, sādhyas, and cāraṇas approached him,
Upendra, led by Indra, and Brahmā surrounded by hosts of sages.

1.16.s:
kṛtopanayano vedānadhyaiṣṭa bhagavān hariḥ /
samācāraṃ bharadvājāt trilokāya pradarśayan //
1.16.d:
कृतोपनयनो वेदानध्यैष्ट भगवान् हरिः ।
समाचारं भरद्वाजात् त्रिलोकाय प्रदर्शयन् ॥
1.16.m:
Having received the sacred thread ceremony, the blessed Lord Hari studied the Vedas,
learning proper conduct from Bharadvāja to display it to the three worlds.

1.16.s:
evaṃ hi laukikaṃ mārgaṃ pradarśayati sa prabhuḥ /
sa yat pramāṇaṃ kurute lokastadanuvartate //
1.16.d:
एवं हि लौकिकं मार्गं प्रदर्शयति स प्रभुः ।
स यत् प्रमाणं कुरुते लोकस्तदनुवर्तते ॥
1.16.m:
For in this way that Lord displays the worldly path;
whatever standard he sets, the world follows.

1.16.s:
tataḥ kālena matimān balirvairocaniḥ svayam /
yajñairyajñeśvaraṃ viṣṇumarcayāmāsa sarvagam //
1.16.d:
ततः कालेन मतिमान् बलिर्वैरोचनिः स्वयम् ।
यज्ञैर्यज्ञेश्वरं विष्णुमर्चयामास सर्वगम् ॥
1.16.m:
Then, in the course of time, the wise Bali, the son of Virocana, himself
worshipped Viṣṇu, the all-pervading lord of sacrifice, with sacrifices.

1.16.s:
brāhmaṇān pūjayāmāsa dattvā bahutaraṃ dhanam /
brahmarṣayaḥ samājagmuryajñavāṭaṃ mahātmanaḥ //
1.16.d:
ब्राह्मणान् पूजयामास दत्त्वा बहुतरं धनम् ।
ब्रह्मर्षयः समाजग्मुर्यज्ञवाटं महात्मनः ॥
1.16.m:
He honored the brahmins by giving abundant wealth;
and the brahmin seers came to the sacrificial enclosure of that great-souled one.

1.16.s:
vijñāya viṣṇurbhagavān bharadvājapracoditaḥ /
āsthāya vāmanaṃ rūpaṃ yajñadeśamathāgamat //
1.16.d:
विज्ञाय विष्णुर्भगवान् भरद्वाजप्रचोदितः ।
आस्थाय वामनं रूपं यज्ञदेशमथागमत् ॥
1.16.m:
Knowing [this], the blessed Lord Viṣṇu, urged by Bharadvāja,
assumed the form of a dwarf and went to the place of sacrifice.

1.16.s:
kṛṣṇājinopavītāṅga āṣāḍhena virājitaḥ /
brāhmaṇo jaṭilo vedānudgiran bhasmamaṇḍitaḥ //
1.16.d:
कृष्णाजिनोपवीताङ्ग आषाढेन विराजितः ।
ब्राह्मणो जटिलो वेदानुद्गिरन् भस्ममण्डितः ॥
1.16.m:
His body wearing a black buckskin and a sacred thread, shining with a staff of palāśa wood,
a brahmin with matted hair, uttering the Vedas, adorned with sacred ashes.

1.16.s:
saṃprāpyāsurarājasya samīpaṃ bhikṣuko hariḥ /
svapādairvimitaṃ deśamayācata baliṃ tribhiḥ //
1.16.d:
संप्राप्यासुरराजस्य समीपं भिक्षुको हरिः ।
स्वपादैर्विमितं देशमयाचत बलिं त्रिभिः ॥
1.16.m:
Having arrived near the king of the asuras, Hari as a beggar
begged Bali for ground measured by three of his own strides.

1.16.s:
prakṣālya caraṇau viṣṇorbalirbhāsamanvitaḥ /
ācāmayitvā bhṛṅgāramādāya svarṇanirmitam //
1.16.d:
प्रक्षाल्य चरणौ विष्णोर्बलिर्भासमन्वितः ।
आचामयित्वा भृङ्गारमादाय स्वर्णनिर्मितम् ॥
1.16.m:
Having washed the feet of Viṣṇu, Bali, full of splendor,
made [him] sip water, and taking a pitcher made of gold,

1.16.s:
dāsye tavedaṃ bhavate padatrayaṃ
prīṇātu devo hariravyayākṛtiḥ /
vicintya devasya karāgrapallave
nipātayāmāsa jalaṃ suśītalam //
1.16.d:
दास्ये तवेदं भवते पदत्रयं
प्रीणातु देवो हरिरव्ययाकृतिः ।
विचिन्त्य देवस्य कराग्रपल्लवे
निपातयामास जलं सुशीतलम् ॥
1.16.m:
“I will give to your honor these three strides of land;
may the god Hari, of imperishable form, be pleased.”
Having so resolved, onto the sprout-like fingertip of the god
he poured the cool water.

1.16.s:
vicakrame pṛthivīmeṣa etā-
mathāntarikṣaṃ divamādidevaḥ /
vyapetarāgaṃ ditijeśvaraṃ taṃ
prakartukāmaḥ śaraṇaṃ prapannam //
1.16.d:
विचक्रमे पृथिवीमेष एता-
मथान्तरिक्षं दिवमादिदेवः ।
व्यपेतरागं दितिजेश्वरं तं
प्रकर्तुकामः शरणं प्रपन्नम् ॥
1.16.m:
The primordial god strode over this earth,
and then the intermediate space and the sky,
desirous of purifying that lord of the sons of Diti
who had surrendered to him for refuge.

1.16.s:
ākramya lokatrayamīśapādaḥ
prājāpatyād brahmalokaṃ jagāma /
praṇemurādityasahastrakalpaṃ
ye tatra loke nivasanti siddhāḥ //
1.16.d:
आक्रम्य लोकत्रयमीशपादः
प्राजापत्याद् ब्रह्मलोकं जगाम ।
प्रणेमुरादित्यसहस्त्रकल्पं
ये तत्र लोके निवसन्ति सिद्धाः ॥
1.16.m:
Having traversed the three worlds, the foot of the Lord,
beyond the realm of Prajāpati, went to the world of Brahmā;
and those perfected ones residing in that world
bowed down to it, radiant like a thousand suns.

1.16.s:
athopatasthe bhagavānanādiḥ
pitāmahāstoṣayāmāsa viṣṇum /
bhittvā tadaṇḍasya kapālamūrdhvaṃ
jagāma divyāvaraṇāni bhūyaḥ //
1.16.d:
अथोपतस्थे भगवाननादिः
पितामहास्तोषयामास विष्णुम् ।
भित्त्वा तदण्डस्य कपालमूर्ध्वं
जगाम दिव्यावरणानि भूयः ॥
1.16.m:
Then the blessed beginningless Grandfather [Brahmā] approached
and satisfied Viṣṇu;
and piercing the upper shell of the cosmic egg,
[the foot] went further through the divine coverings.

1.16.s:
athāṇḍabhedānnipapāta śītalaṃ
mahājalaṃ tat puṇyakṛdbhiścajuṣṭam /
pravartate cāpi saridvarā tadā
gaṅgetyuktā brahmaṇā vyomasaṃsthā //
1.16.d:
अथाण्डभेदान्निपपात शीतलं
महाजलं तत् पुण्यकृद्भिश्चजुष्टम् ।
प्रवर्तते चापि सरिद्वरा तदा
गङ्गेत्युक्ता ब्रह्मणा व्योमसंस्था ॥
1.16.m:
Then from the cleavage of the egg fell cool,
great water, enjoyed by those who perform holy deeds;
and there flowed that excellent celestial river,
called the Gaṅgā by Brahmā, residing in the firmament.

1.16.s:
gatvā mahāntaṃ prakṛtiṃ pradhānaṃ
brahmāṇamekaṃ puruṣaṃ svabījam /
atiṣṭhadīśasya padaṃ tadavyayaṃ
dṛṣṭvā devāstatra tatra stuvanti //
1.16.d:
गत्वा महान्तं प्रकृतिं प्रधानं
ब्रह्माणमेकं पुरुषं स्वबीजम् ।
अतिष्ठदीशस्य पदं तदव्ययं
दृष्ट्वा देवास्तत्र तत्र स्तुवन्ति ॥
1.16.m:
Having reached the cosmic intellect, primordial matter, the unmanifest,
the one Brahmā, the Puruṣa, its own seed,
that imperishable foot of the Lord stood firm;
having seen it, the gods everywhere praised it.

1.16.s:
ālokya taṃ puruṣaṃ viśvakāyaṃ
mahān balirbhaktiyogena viṣṇum /
nanāma nārāyaṇamekamavyayaṃ
svacetasā yaṃ praṇamanti devāḥ //
1.16.d:
आलोक्य तं पुरुषं विश्वकायं
महान् बलिर्भक्तियोगेन विष्णुम् ।
ननाम नारायणमेकमव्ययं
स्वचेतसा यं प्रणमन्ति देवाः ॥
1.16.m:
Beholding that spirit whose body is the universe, Viṣṇu,
the great Bali, through the discipline of devotion,
bowed down to the one imperishable Nārāyaṇa,
whom the gods revere in their own hearts.

1.16.s:
tamabravīd bhagavānādikartā
bhūtvā punarvāmano vāsudevaḥ /
mamaiva daityādhipate 'dhunedaṃ
lokatrayaṃ bhavatā bhāvadattam //
1.16.d:
तमब्रवीद् भगवानादिकर्ता
भूत्वा पुनर्वामनो वासुदेवः ।
ममैव दैत्याधिपते ऽधुनेदं
लोकत्रयं भवता भावदत्तम् ॥
1.16.m:
The blessed creator of all, Vāsudeva,
having become the dwarf again, spoke to him:
“O sovereign of the daityas, now these three worlds are mine,
given by your honor with devotion.

1.16.s:
praṇamya mūrdhnā punareva daityo
nipātayāmāsa jalaṃ karāgre /
dāsye tavātmānamanantadhāmne
trivikramāyāmitavikramāya //
1.16.d:
प्रणम्य मूर्ध्ना पुनरेव दैत्यो
निपातयामास जलं कराग्रे ।
दास्ये तवात्मानमनन्तधाम्ने
त्रिविक्रमायामितविक्रमाय ॥
1.16.m:
Bowing his head, once again the daitya
poured water onto the tips of his fingers:
“I give my own self to you, whose abode is infinite,
to Trivikrama of boundless stride.”

1.16.s:
pragṛhya sūnorapi saṃpradattaṃ
prahlādasūnoratha śaṅkhapāṇiḥ /
jagāda daityaṃ jagadantarātmā
pātālamūlaṃ praviśeti bhūyaḥ //
1.16.d:
प्रगृह्य सूनोरपि संप्रदत्तं
प्रह्लादसूनोरथ शङ्खपाणिः ।
जगाद दैत्यं जगदन्तरात्मा
पातालमूलं प्रविशेति भूयः ॥
1.16.m:
Accepting what was offered even by the son of Prahlāda’s son,
the shell-handed inner self of the universe
spoke again to the daitya:
“Enter the root of the netherworld.

1.16.s:
samāsyatāṃ bhavatā tatra nityaṃ
bhuktvā bhogān devatānāmalabhyān /
dhyāyasva māṃ satataṃ bhaktiyogāt
pravekṣyase kalpadāhe punarmām //
1.16.d:
समास्यतां भवता तत्र नित्यं
भुक्त्वा भोगान् देवतानामलभ्यान् ।
ध्यायस्व मां सततं भक्तियोगात्
प्रवेक्ष्यसे कल्पदाहे पुनर्माम् ॥

1.16.s:
uktvaivaṃ daityasiṃhaṃ taṃ viṣṇuḥ satyaparākramaḥ /
purandarāya trailokyaṃ dadau viṣṇururukramaḥ //
1.16.d:
उक्त्वैवं दैत्यसिंहं तं विष्णुः सत्यपराक्रमः ।
पुरन्दराय त्रैलोक्यं ददौ विष्णुरुरुक्रमः ॥
1.16.m:
Having spoken thus to that lion among the daityas, Viṣṇu of true valor,
Viṣṇu of wide strides gave the three worlds to Indra.

1.16.s:
saṃstuvanti mahāyogaṃ siddhā devarṣikinnarāḥ /
brahmā śakro 'tha bhagavān rudrādityamarudgaṇāḥ //
1.16.d:
संस्तुवन्ति महायोगं सिद्धा देवर्षिकिन्नराः ।
ब्रह्मा शक्रो ऽथ भगवान् रुद्रादित्यमरुद्गणाः ॥
1.16.m:
The siddhas, divine seers, and kinnaras praised the great yogic power,
as did Brahmā, Indra, and the blessed Rudras, Ādityas, and Marut hosts.

1.16.s:
kṛtvaitadadbhutaṃ karma viṣṇurvāmanarūpadhṛk /
paśyatāmeva sarveṣāṃ tatraivāntaradhīyata //
1.16.d:
कृत्वैतदद्भुतं कर्म विष्णुर्वामनरूपधृक् ।
पश्यतामेव सर्वेषां तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥
1.16.m:
Having performed this miraculous deed, Viṣṇu, who assumed the dwarf form,
vanished right there while all were looking on.

1.16.s:
so 'pi daityavaraḥ śrīmān pātālaṃ prāpa coditaḥ /
prahlādenāsuravarairviṣṇunā viṣṇutatparaḥ //
1.16.d:
सो ऽपि दैत्यवरः श्रीमान् पातालं प्राप चोदितः ।
प्रह्लादेनासुरवरैर्विष्णुना विष्णुतत्परः ॥
1.16.m:
That illustrious best of daityas too, devoted to Viṣṇu, went to the netherworld,
impelled by Prahlāda, the best of the asuras, and by Viṣṇu.

1.16.s:
apṛcchad viṣṇumāhātmayaṃ bhaktiyogamanuttamam /
pūjāvidhānaṃ prahlādaṃ tadāhāsau cakāra saḥ //
1.16.d:
अपृच्छद् विष्णुमाहात्मयं भक्तियोगमनुत्तमम् ।
पूजाविधानं प्रह्लादं तदाहासौ चकार सः ॥
1.16.m:
He asked Prahlāda about the majesty of Viṣṇu,
the unsurpassed discipline of devotion, and the procedure of worship; and whatever he said, Bali performed.

1.16.s:
atha rathacaraṇāsiśaṅkhapāṇiṃ
sarasijolacanamīśamaprameyam /
śaraṇamupapayau sa bhāvayogāt
praṇatagatiṃ praṇidhāya karmayogam //
1.16.d:
अथ रथचरणासिशङ्खपाणिं
सरसिजोलचनमीशमप्रमेयम् ।
शरणमुपपयौ स भावयोगात्
प्रणतगतिं प्रणिधाय कर्मयोगम् ॥
1.16.m:
Then, dedicating his yoga of action to him who is the refuge of the bowed,
he approached for refuge with devotional concentration
that immeasurable Lord, who holds the discus, sword, and conch in his hands,
and whose eyes resemble lotuses.

1.16.s:
eṣa vaḥ kathito viprā vāmanasya parākramaḥ /
sa devakāryāṇi sadā karoti puruṣottamaḥ //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāya
1.16.d:
एष वः कथितो विप्रा वामनस्य पराक्रमः ।
स देवकार्याणि सदा करोति पुरुषोत्तमः ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे षोडशो ऽध्याय

1.17.s:
baleḥ putraśataṃ tvāsīnmahābalaparākramam /
teṣāṃ pradhāno dyutimān bāṇo nāma mahābalaḥ //
1.17.d:
बलेः पुत्रशतं त्वासीन्महाबलपराक्रमम् ।
तेषां प्रधानो द्युतिमान् बाणो नाम महाबलः ॥
1.17.m:
Bali indeed had a hundred sons of great strength and valor;
the foremost among them was the radiant one named Bāṇa, of great strength.

1.17.s:
so 'tīva śaṅkare bhakto rājā rājyamapālayat /
trailokyaṃ vaśamānīya bādhayāmāsa vāsavam //
1.17.d:
सो ऽतीव शङ्करे भक्तो राजा राज्यमपालयत् ।
त्रैलोक्यं वशमानीय बाधयामास वासवम् ॥
1.17.m:
Exceedingly devoted to Śaṅkara, he ruled the kingdom as king;
bringing the three worlds under his control, he harassed Indra.

1.17.s:
tataḥ śakrādayo devā gatvocuḥ kṛttivāsasam /
tvadīyo bādhate hyasmān bāṇo nāma mahāsuraḥ //
1.17.d:
ततः शक्रादयो देवा गत्वोचुः कृत्तिवाससम् ।
त्वदीयो बाधते ह्यस्मान् बाणो नाम महासुरः ॥
1.17.m:
Then the gods, led by Indra, went and said to the one clad in an animal skin [Śiva]:
“A great asura named Bāṇa, who is your own devotee, harasses us.”

1.17.s:
vyāhṛto daivadaiḥ sarvairdevadevo maheśvaraḥ /
dadāha bāṇasya puraṃ śareṇaikena līlayā //
1.17.d:
व्याहृतो दैवदैः सर्वैर्देवदेवो महेश्वरः ।
ददाह बाणस्य पुरं शरेणैकेन लीलया ॥
1.17.m:
Addressed by all the gods, the god of gods, Maheśvara,
burned the city of Bāṇa sportively with a single arrow.

1.17.s:
dahyamāne pure tasmin bāṇo rudraṃ triśūlinam /
yayau śaraṇamīśānaṃ gopatiṃ nīlalohitam //
1.17.d:
दह्यमाने पुरे तस्मिन् बाणो रुद्रं त्रिशूलिनम् ।
ययौ शरणमीशानं गोपतिं नीललोहितम् ॥
1.17.m:
While that city was burning, Bāṇa sought refuge
with Rudra who holds the trident, Īśāna, the lord of cattle, Nīlalohita.

1.17.s:
mūrdhanyādhāya talliṅgaṃ śāṃbhavaṃ bhītavarjitaḥ /
nirgatya tu purāt tasmāt tuṣṭāva parameśvaram //
1.17.d:
मूर्धन्याधाय तल्लिङ्गं शांभवं भीतवर्जितः ।
निर्गत्य तु पुरात् तस्मात् तुष्टाव परमेश्वरम् ॥
1.17.m: Placing that liṅga of Śambhu upon his head, freed from fear, / he came forth from that city and praised the Supreme Lord.

1.17.s:
saṃstuto bhagavānīśaḥ śaṅkaro nīlalohitaḥ /
gāṇapatyena bāṇaṃ taṃ yojayāmāsa bhāvataḥ //
1.17.d:
संस्तुतो भगवानीशः शङ्करो नीललोहितः ।
गाणपत्येन बाणं तं योजयामास भावतः ॥
1.17.m: Praised in this way, the blessed lord Śaṅkara, Nīlalohita, / lovingly appointed that Bāṇa to the leadership of his attendants.

1.17.s:
athābhavan danoḥ putrāstārādyā hyatibhīṣaṇāḥ /
tārastathā śambaraśca kapilaḥ śaṅkarastathā /
svarbhānurvṛṣaparvā ca prādhānyena prakīrtitāḥ //
1.17.d:
अथाभवन् दनोः पुत्रास्ताराद्या ह्यतिभीषणाः ।
तारस्तथा शम्बरश्च कपिलः शङ्करस्तथा ।
स्वर्भानुर्वृषपर्वा च प्राधान्येन प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
1.17.m: Now there were sons of Danu, beginning with Tāra, exceedingly terrifying: / Tāra, Śambara, Kapila, Śaṅkara, / Svarbhānu, and Vṛṣaparvan are recorded as the foremost.

1.17.s:
surasāyāḥ sahastraṃ tu sarpāṇāmabhavad dvijāḥ /
anekaśirasāṃ tadvat khecarāṇāṃ mahātmanām //
1.17.d:
सुरसायाः सहस्त्रं तु सर्पाणामभवद् द्विजाः ।
अनेकशिरसां तद्वत् खेचराणां महात्मनाम् ॥
1.17.m: From Surasā came a thousand snakes, O twice-born ones, / having many heads, moving through the sky, and great-souled.

1.17.s:
ariṣṭā janayāmāsa gandharvāṇāṃ sahastrakam /
anantādyā mahānāgāḥ kādraveyāḥ prakīrtitāḥ //
1.17.d:
अरिष्टा जनयामास गन्धर्वाणां सहस्त्रकम् ।
अनन्ताद्या महानागाः काद्रवेयाः प्रकीर्तिताः ॥
1.17.m: Ariṣṭā brought forth a thousand Gandharvas; / the great serpents, beginning with Ananta, are proclaimed as Kadrū's offspring.

1.17.s:
tāmrā ca janayāmāsa ṣaṭ kanyā dvijapuṅgavāḥ /
śukīṃ śyenīṃ ca bhāsīṃ ca sugrīvāṅgṛdhrikāṃ śucim //
1.17.d:
ताम्रा च जनयामास षट् कन्या द्विजपुङ्गवाः ।
शुकीं श्येनीं च भासीं च सुग्रीवाङ्गृध्रिकां शुचिम् ॥
1.17.m: And Tāmrā brought forth six daughters, O best of the twice-born: / Śukī, Śyenī, Bhāsī, Sugrīvā, Gṛdhrikā, and Śuci.

1.17.s:
gāstathā janayāmāsa surabhirmahiṣīstathā /
irā vṛkṣalatāvallīstṛṇajātīśca sarvaśaḥ //
1.17.d:
गास्तथा जनयामास सुरभिर्महिषीस्तथा ।
इरा वृक्षलतावल्लीस्तृणजातीश्च सर्वशः ॥
1.17.m: Surabhi brought forth cows and likewise buffaloes; / Irā [brought forth] trees, creepers, shrubs, and all kinds of grasses.

1.17.s:
khasā vai yakṣarakṣāṃsi munirapsarasastathā /
rakṣogaṇaṃ krodhavaśā janayāmāsa sattamāḥ //
1.17.d:
खसा वै यक्षरक्षांसि मुनिरप्सरसस्तथा ।
रक्षोगणं क्रोधवशा जनयामास सत्तमाः ॥
1.17.m: Khasā indeed [brought forth] Yakṣas and Rakṣases, Muni the Apsarases, / and Krodhavaśā brought forth the host of Rakṣases, O virtuous ones.

1.17.s:
vinatāyāśca putrau dvau prakhyātau garuḍāruṇau /
tayośca garuḍo dhīmān tapastaptvā suduścaram /
prasādācchūnilaḥ prāpto vāhanatvaṃ hareḥ svayam //
1.17.d:
विनतायाश्च पुत्रौ द्वौ प्रख्यातौ गरुडारुणौ ।
तयोश्च गरुडो धीमान् तपस्तप्त्वा सुदुश्चरम् ।
प्रसादाच्छूनिलः प्राप्तो वाहनत्वं हरेः स्वयम् ॥
1.17.m: And Vinatā had two sons, famous as Garuḍa and Aruṇa; / between them, wise Garuḍa, having performed severe austerities, / attained the role of being the mount of Hari himself by the grace of Śiva.

1.17.s:
ārādhya tapasā rudraṃ mahdevaṃ tathāruṇaḥ /
sārathye kalpitaḥ pūrvaṃ prītenārkasya śaṃbhunā //
1.17.d:
आराध्य तपसा रुद्रं मह्देवं तथारुणः ।
सारथ्ये कल्पितः पूर्वं प्रीतेनार्कस्य शंभुना ॥
1.17.m: Having worshipped Rudra, Mahādeva, through ascetic penance, Aruṇa / was previously appointed as the Sun's charioteer by pleased Śambhu.

1.17.s:
ete kaśyapadāyādāḥ kīrtitāḥ sthāṇujaṅgamāḥ /
vaivasvate 'nte hyasmiñchṛṇvatāṃ pāpanāśanāḥ //
1.17.d:
एते कश्यपदायादाः कीर्तिताः स्थाणुजङ्गमाः ।
वैवस्वते ऽन्ते ह्यस्मिञ्छृण्वतां पापनाशनाः ॥
1.17.m: These descendants of Kaśyapa, immovable and moving, / have been narrated in this Vaivasvata cosmic era; they destroy the sins of those who hear [them].

1.17.s:
saptaviṃśat sutāḥ proktāḥ somapatnyaśca suvratāḥ /
ariṣṭanemipatnīnāmapatyānīha ṣoḍaśa //
1.17.d:
सप्तविंशत् सुताः प्रोक्ताः सोमपत्न्यश्च सुव्रताः ।
अरिष्टनेमिपत्नीनामपत्यानीह षोडश ॥
1.17.m: Twenty-seven daughters are spoken of, the virtuous wives of Soma; / and sixteen offspring of the wives of Ariṣṭanemi here.

1.17.s:
bahuputrasya viduṣaścatastro vidyutaḥ smṛtāḥ /
tadvadaṅgirasaḥ putrā ṛṣayo brahmasatkṛtāḥ //
1.17.d:
बहुपुत्रस्य विदुषश्चतस्त्रो विद्युतः स्मृताः ।
तद्वदङ्गिरसः पुत्रा ऋषयो ब्रह्मसत्कृताः ॥
1.17.m: Four lightnings are recorded as [the daughters] of the wise Bahuputra; / likewise, the sons of Aṅgiras were sages honored by Brahmā.

1.17.s:
kuśāśvasya tu devarṣerdevapraharaṇāḥ sutāḥ /
ete yugasahastrānte jāyante punareva hi /
manvantareṣu niyataṃ tulyaiḥ kāryaiḥ svanāmabhiḥ //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.17.d:
कुशाश्वस्य तु देवर्षेर्देवप्रहरणाः सुताः ।
एते युगसहस्त्रान्ते जायन्ते पुनरेव हि ।
मन्वन्तरेषु नियतं तुल्यैः कार्यैः स्वनामभिः ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे सप्तदशो ऽध्यायः
1.17.m:
The divine sage Kuśāśva had divine weapons as his sons; / these indeed are born again at the end of a thousand yugas / in the cosmic eras of Manus with fixed tasks and matching names.

Thus ends the seventeenth chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.18.s:
sūta uvāca
etānutpādya putrāṃstu prajāsaṃtānakāraṇāt /
kaśyapo gotrakāmastu cacāra sumahat tapaḥ //
1.18.d:
सूत उवाच
एतानुत्पाद्य पुत्रांस्तु प्रजासंतानकारणात् ।
कश्यपो गोत्रकामस्तु चचार सुमहत् तपः ॥
1.18.m: Sūta said: / Having fathered these sons for the sake of continuing the progeny, / Kaśyapa, desiring a clan, performed great ascetic penance.

1.18.s:
tasya vai tapato 'tyarthaṃ prādurbhūtau sutāvimau /
vatsaraścāsitaścaiva tāvubhau brahmavādinau //
1.18.d:
तस्य वै तपतो ऽत्यर्थं प्रादुर्भूतौ सुताविमौ ।
वत्सरश्चासितश्चैव तावुभौ ब्रह्मवादिनौ ॥
1.18.m: As he was performing penance intensely, these two sons appeared: / Vatsara and Asita, both expositors of the Veda.

1.18.s:
vatsarānnaidhruvo jajñe raibhyaśca sumahāyaśāḥ /
raibhyasya jajñire raibhyāḥ putrā dyutimatāṃ varāḥ //
1.18.d:
वत्सरान्नैध्रुवो जज्ञे रैभ्यश्च सुमहायशाः ।
रैभ्यस्य जज्ञिरे रैभ्याः पुत्रा द्युतिमतां वराः ॥
1.18.m: From Vatsara was born Naidhruva, and the highly renowned Raibhya; / from Raibhya were born the Raibhyas, foremost among radiant men.

1.18.s:
cyavanasya sutā patnī naidhruvasya mahātmanaḥ /
sumedhā janayāmāsa putrān vai kuṇḍapāyinaḥ //
1.18.d:
च्यवनस्य सुता पत्नी नैध्रुवस्य महात्मनः ।
सुमेधा जनयामास पुत्रान् वै कुण्डपायिनः ॥
1.18.m: The wife of the great-souled Naidhruva was the daughter of Cyavana; / Sumedhā gave birth to sons, the Kuṇḍapāyins.

1.18.s:
asitasyaikaparṇāyāṃ brahmiṣṭhaḥ samapadyata /
nāmnā vai devalaḥ putro yogācāryo mahātapāḥ //
1.18.d:
असितस्यैकपर्णायां ब्रह्मिष्ठः समपद्यत ।
नाम्ना वै देवलः पुत्रो योगाचार्यो महातपाः ॥
1.18.m: By Ekaparṇā, Asita had a son deeply devoted to Brahman, / Devala by name, a master of yoga and a great ascetic.

1.18.s:
śāṇḍilyānāṃ paraḥ śrīmān sarvatattvārthavit sudhīḥ /
prasādāt pārvatīśasya yogamuttamamāptavān //
1.18.d:
शाण्डिल्यानां परः श्रीमान् सर्वतत्त्वार्थवित् सुधीः ।
प्रसादात् पार्वतीशस्य योगमुत्तममाप्तवान् ॥
1.18.m: He was supreme among the Śāṇḍilyas, glorious, knowledgeable in the truths of all principles, and wise; / by the grace of Pārvatī's lord, he attained supreme yoga.

1.18.s:
śāṇḍilyā naidhru vāraibhyāstrayaḥ pakṣāstu kāśyapāḥ /
naraprakṛtayo viprāḥ pulastyasya vadāmi vaḥ //
1.18.d:
शाण्डिल्या नैध्रु वारैभ्यास्त्रयः पक्षास्तु काश्यपाः ।
नरप्रकृतयो विप्राः पुलस्त्यस्य वदामि वः ॥
1.18.m: The Śāṇḍilyas, the Naidhruvas, and the Raibhyas are three divisions belonging to Kaśyapa, / being of human nature, O twice-born ones. I shall tell you of Pulastya's [lineage].

1.18.s:
tṛṇabindoḥ sutā viprā nāmnā tvilavilā smṛtā /
pulastyāya sa rājarṣistāṃ kanyāṃ pratyapādayat //
1.18.d:
तृणबिन्दोः सुता विप्रा नाम्ना त्विलविला स्मृता ।
पुलस्त्याय स राजर्षिस्तां कन्यां प्रत्यपादयत् ॥
1.18.m: The daughter of Tṛṇabindu, O twice-born ones, was known by name as Ilavilā; / that royal sage bestowed that maiden upon Pulastya.

1.18.s:
ṛṣistvailavilistasyāṃ viśravāḥ samapadyata /
tasya patnyaścatastrastu paulastyakulavardhikāḥ //
1.18.d:
ऋषिस्त्वैलविलिस्तस्यां विश्रवाः समपद्यत ।
तस्य पत्न्यश्चतस्त्रस्तु पौलस्त्यकुलवर्धिकाः ॥
1.18.m: In her was born the sage Viśravas, son of Ilavilā; / he had four wives who increased the family of Pulastya:

1.18.s:
puṣpotkaṭā ca rākā ca kaikasī devavarṇinī /
rūpalāvaṇyasaṃpannāstāsāṃ vai śṛṇuta prajāḥ //
1.18.d:
पुष्पोत्कटा च राका च कैकसी देववर्णिनी ।
रूपलावण्यसंपन्नास्तासां वै शृणुत प्रजाः ॥
1.18.m: Puṣpotkaṭā, Rākā, Kaikasī, and Devavarṇinī, / endowed with beauty and charm. Hear now of their offspring.

1.18.s:
jyeṣṭhaṃ vaiśravaṇaṃ tasya suṣuve devarūpiṇī /
kaikasī janayat putraṃ rāvaṇaṃ rākṣasādhipam //
1.18.d:
ज्येष्ठं वैश्रवणं तस्य सुषुवे देवरूपिणी ।
कैकसी जनयत् पुत्रं रावणं राक्षसाधिपम् ॥
1.18.m: To him, Devavarṇinī bore his eldest son, Vaiśravaṇa; / Kaikasī gave birth to a son, Rāvaṇa, the lord of the Rākṣasas,

1.18.s:
kumbhakarṇaṃ śūrpaṇakhāṃ tathaiva ca vibhīṣaṇam /
puṣpotkaṭā vyajanayat putrān viśravasaḥ śubhān //
1.18.d:
कुम्भकर्णं शूर्पणखां तथैव च विभीषणम् ।
पुष्पोत्कटा व्यजनयत् पुत्रान् विश्रवसः शुभान् ॥
1.18.m: and Kumbhakarṇa, Śūrpaṇakhā, and likewise Vibhīṣaṇa. / Puṣpotkaṭā brought forth splendid sons to Viśravas:

1.18.s:
mahodaraṃ prahastaṃ ca mahāpārśvaṃ kharaṃ tathā /
kumbhīnasīṃ tathā kanyāṃ rākāyāṃ śṛṇuta prajāḥ //
1.18.d:
महोदरं प्रहस्तं च महापार्श्वं खरं तथा ।
कुम्भीनसीं तथा कन्यां राकायां शृणुत प्रजाः ॥
1.18.m: Mahodara, Prahasta, Mahāpārśva, and Khara, / and a daughter, Kumbhīnasī. Hear now of the offspring born of Rākā:

1.18.s:
triśirā dūṣaṇaścaiva vidyujjihvo mahābalaḥ /
ityete krūrakarmāṇaḥ paulastyā rākṣasā daśa /
sarve tapobalotkṛṣṭā rudrabhaktāḥ subhīṣaṇāḥ //
1.18.d:
त्रिशिरा दूषणश्चैव विद्युज्जिह्वो महाबलः ।
इत्येते क्रूरकर्माणः पौलस्त्या राक्षसा दश ।
सर्वे तपोबलोत्कृष्टा रुद्रभक्ताः सुभीषणाः ॥
1.18.m: Triśiras, Dūṣaṇa, and Vidyujjihva of great strength; / these were the ten fierce Rākṣasas of Pulastya's lineage, / all distinguished by the power of penance, devotees of Rudra, and exceedingly terrifying.

1.18.s:
pulahasya mṛgāḥ putrāḥ sarve vyālāśca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ /
bhūtāḥ piśācāḥ sarpāśca śūkarā hastinastathā //
1.18.d:
पुलहस्य मृगाः पुत्राः सर्वे व्यालाश्च दंष्ट्रिणः ।
भूताः पिशाचाः सर्पाश्च शूकरा हस्तिनस्तथा ॥
1.18.m: The sons of Pulaha were wild animals, all fanged beasts of prey, / spirits, Piśācas, serpents, boars, and elephants.

1.18.s:
anapatyaḥ kratustasmin smṛto vaivasvate 'ntare /
marīceḥ kaśyapaḥ putraḥ svayameva prajāpatiḥ //
1.18.d:
अनपत्यः क्रतुस्तस्मिन् स्मृतो वैवस्वते ऽन्तरे ।
मरीचेः कश्यपः पुत्रः स्वयमेव प्रजापतिः ॥
1.18.m: Kratu is recorded as having been childless in that Vaivasvata cosmic era; / Marīci's son was Kaśyapa, the Prajāpati himself.

1.18.s:
bhṛgorapyabhavacchukro daityācāryo mahātapāḥ /
svādhyāyayoganirato harabhakto mahādyutiḥ //
1.18.d:
भृगोरप्यभवच्छुक्रो दैत्याचार्यो महातपाः ।
स्वाध्याययोगनिरतो हरभक्तो महाद्युतिः ॥
1.18.m: From Bhṛgu was born Śukra, the teacher of the Daityas, a great ascetic / devoted to the study of the Vedas and yoga, a devotee of Hara, and of great brilliance.

1.18.s:
atreḥ patnyo 'bhavan bahvyaḥ sodaryāstāḥ pativratāḥ /
kṛśāśvasya tu viprendrā ghṛtācyāmiti me śrutam //
1.18.d:
अत्रेः पत्न्यो ऽभवन् बह्व्यः सोदर्यास्ताः पतिव्रताः ।
कृशाश्वस्य तु विप्रेन्द्रा घृताच्यामिति मे श्रुतम् ॥
1.18.m: Atri had many wives who were devoted sisters, / the daughters of Kṛśāśva by Ghṛtācī, O foremost of twice-born ones, so have I heard.

1.18.s:
sa tāsu janayāmāsa svastyātreyān mahaujasaḥ /
vedavedāṅganiratāṃstapasā hatakilbiṣān //
1.18.d:
स तासु जनयामास स्वस्त्यात्रेयान् महौजसः ।
वेदवेदाङ्गनिरतांस्तपसा हतकिल्बिषान् ॥
1.18.m: In them he fathered the Svastyātreyas, of great power, / devoted to the Vedas and their auxiliary sciences, their sins destroyed by penance.

1.18.s:
nāradastu vasiṣṭhāya dadau devīmarundhatīm /
ūrdhvaretāstatra muniḥ śāpād dakṣasya nāradaḥ //
1.18.d:
नारदस्तु वसिष्ठाय ददौ देवीमरुन्धतीम् ।
ऊर्ध्वरेतास्तत्र मुनिः शापाद् दक्षस्य नारदः ॥
1.18.m: Nārada gave the noble Arundhatī to Vasiṣṭha; / the sage Nārada lived there as a celibate due to a curse from Dakṣa.

1.18.s:
haryaśveṣu tu naṣṭeṣu māyayā nāradasya tu /
śaśāpa nāradaṃ dakṣaḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ //
1.18.d:
हर्यश्वेषु तु नष्टेषु मायया नारदस्य तु ।
शशाप नारदं दक्षः क्रोधसंरक्तलोचनः ॥
1.18.m: When the Haryaśvas had perished through the illusory art of Nārada, / Dakṣa, his eyes blood-red with anger, cursed Nārada:

1.18.s:
yasmānmama sutāḥ sarve bhavato māyayā dvija /
kṣayaṃ nītāstvaśeṣeṇa nirapatyo bhaviṣyati //
1.18.d:
यस्मान्मम सुताः सर्वे भवतो मायया द्विज ।
क्षयं नीतास्त्वशेषेण निरपत्यो भविष्यति ॥
1.18.m: ‘Since all my sons have been brought entirely to destruction / through your illusory art, O twice-born, you shall be without offspring.’

1.18.s:
arundhatyāṃ vasiṣṭhastu śaktimutpādayat sutam /
śakteḥ parāśaraḥ śrīmān sarvajñastapatāṃ varaḥ //
1.18.d:
अरुन्धत्यां वसिष्ठस्तु शक्तिमुत्पादयत् सुतम् ।
शक्तेः पराशरः श्रीमान् सर्वज्ञस्तपतां वरः ॥
1.18.m: In Arundhatī, Vasiṣṭha fathered a son, Śakti; / from Śakti came the glorious Parāśara, omniscient, best among ascetics.

1.18.s:
ārādhya devadeveśamīśānaṃ tripurāntakam /
lebhe tvapratimaṃ putraṃ kṛṣṇādvaipāyanaṃ prabhum //
1.18.d:
आराध्य देवदेवेशमीशानं त्रिपुरान्तकम् ।
लेभे त्वप्रतिमं पुत्रं कृष्णाद्वैपायनं प्रभुम् ॥
1.18.m: Having worshipped the lord of gods, Īśāna, the destroyer of the three cities, / he obtained an incomparable son, the lord Kṛṣṇa Dvaipāyana.

1.18.s:
dvaipāyanācchrako jajñe bhagavāneva śaṅkaraḥ /
aṃśāṃśenāvatīryorvyāṃ svaṃ prāpa paramaṃ padam //
1.18.d:
द्वैपायनाच्छ्रको जज्ञे भगवानेव शङ्करः ।
अंशांशेनावतीर्योर्व्यां स्वं प्राप परमं पदम् ॥
1.18.m: From Dvaipāyana was born Śuka, none other than the blessed lord Śaṅkara, / who, having descended to earth with a portion of his portion, attained his own supreme abode.

1.18.s:
śukasyāpyabhavan putrāḥ pañcātyantatapasvinaḥ /
bhūriśravāḥ prabhuḥ śaṃbhuḥ kṛṣṇo gauraśca pañcamaḥ /
kanyā kīrtimatī caiva yogamātā dhṛtavratā //
1.18.d:
शुकस्याप्यभवन् पुत्राः पञ्चात्यन्ततपस्विनः ।
भूरिश्रवाः प्रभुः शंभुः कृष्णो गौरश्च पञ्चमः ।
कन्या कीर्तिमती चैव योगमाता धृतव्रता ॥
1.18.m: Śuka also had five sons of great penance: / Bhūriśravas, Prabhu, Śambhu, Kṛṣṇa, and Gaura as the fifth, / and a daughter, Kīrtimatī, mother of yoga and keeper of vows.

1.18.s:
ete 'tra vaṃśyāḥ kathitā brāhmaṇā brahmavādinām /
ata ūrdhvaṃ nibodhadhvaṃ kaśyapādrājasaṃtatim //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge aṣṭādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.18.d:
एते ऽत्र वंश्याः कथिता ब्राह्मणा ब्रह्मवादिनाम् ।
अत ऊर्ध्वं निबोधध्वं कश्यपाद्राजसंततिम् ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे अष्टादशो ऽध्यायः
1.18.m:
These descendants of the expositors of the Veda, all Brāhmaṇas, have been recounted here; / henceforth, learn of the royal lineage sprung from Kaśyapa.

Thus ends the eighteenth chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.19.s:
sūta uvāca
aditiḥ suṣuve putramādityaṃ kaśyapāt prabhum /
tasyādityasya caivasīd bhāryāṇāṃ tu catuṣṭayam /
saṃjñā rājñī prabhā chāyā putrāṃstāsāṃ nibodhata //
1.19.d:
सूत उवाच
अदितिः सुषुवे पुत्रमादित्यं कश्यपात् प्रभुम् ।
तस्यादित्यस्य चैवसीद् भार्याणां तु चतुष्टयम् ।
संज्ञा राज्ञी प्रभा छाया पुत्रांस्तासां निबोधत ॥
1.19.m: Sūta said: / Aditi bore to Kaśyapa a powerful son, the Sun; / and that Sun had four wives: / Saṃjñā, Rājñī, Prabhā, and Chāyā. Learn of their sons.

1.19.s:
saṃjñā tvāṣṭrī ca suṣuve sūryānmanumanuttamam /
yamaṃ ca yamunāṃ caiva rājñī raivatameva ca //
1.19.d:
संज्ञा त्वाष्ट्री च सुषुवे सूर्यान्मनुमनुत्तमम् ।
यमं च यमुनां चैव राज्ञी रैवतमेव च ॥
1.19.m: And Saṃjñā, daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, bore to the sun the peerless Manu, / and Yama, and Yamunā; and Rājñī bore Raivata;

1.19.s:
prabhā prabhātamādityācchāyā sāvarṇamātmajam /
śaniṃ ca tapatīṃ caiva viṣṭiṃ caiva yathākramam //
1.19.d:
प्रभा प्रभातमादित्याच्छाया सावर्णमात्मजम् ।
शनिं च तपतीं चैव विष्टिं चैव यथाक्रमम् ॥
1.19.m: Prabhā [bore] Prabhāta to the sun; Chāyā bore her son Sāvarṇa, / and Śani, and Tapatī, and Viṣṭi in due order.

1.19.s:
manostu prathamasyāsan nava putrāstu saṃyamāḥ /
ikṣvākurnabhagaścaiva dhṛṣṭaḥ śaryātireva ca //
1.19.d:
मनोस्तु प्रथमस्यासन् नव पुत्रास्तु संयमाः ।
इक्ष्वाकुर्नभगश्चैव धृष्टः शर्यातिरेव च ॥
1.19.m: To the first Manu there were nine self-controlled sons: / Ikṣvāku and Nabhaga, Dhṛṣṭa and Śaryāti,

1.19.s:
nariṣyantaśca nābhāgo hyariṣṭaḥ kāruṣakastathā /
pṛṣadhraśca mahātejā navaite śakrasannibhāḥ //
1.19.d:
नरिष्यन्तश्च नाभागो ह्यरिष्टः कारुषकस्तथा ।
पृषध्रश्च महातेजा नवैते शक्रसन्निभाः ॥
1.19.m: and Nariṣyanta, and Nābhāga, and Ariṣṭa, and Kāruṣaka, / and Pṛṣadhra of great splendour; these nine were like Indra.

1.19.s:
ilā jyeṣṭhā variṣṭhā ca somavaṃśavivṛddhaye /
budhasya gatvā bhavanaṃ somaputreṇa saṃgatā //
1.19.d:
इला ज्येष्ठा वरिष्ठा च सोमवंशविवृद्धये ।
बुधस्य गत्वा भवनं सोमपुत्रेण संगता ॥
1.19.m: Ilā was the eldest and most excellent. For the increase of the Lunar dynasty, / she went to the abode of Budha and united with the son of Soma.

1.19.s:
asūta saumyajaṃ devī purūravasamuttamam /
pitṝṇāṃ tṛptikartāraṃ budhāditi hi naḥ śrutam //
1.19.d:
असूत सौम्यजं देवी पुरूरवसमुत्तमम् ।
पितॄणां तृप्तिकर्तारं बुधादिति हि नः श्रुतम् ॥
1.19.m: The goddess bore to Budha the excellent Purūravas, born of the son of Soma, / who brought gratification to the ancestors; so indeed have we heard.

1.19.s:
saṃprāpya puṃstvamamalaṃ sudyumna iti viśrutaḥ /
ilā putratrayaṃ lebhe punaḥ strītvamavindata //
1.19.d:
संप्राप्य पुंस्त्वममलं सुद्युम्न इति विश्रुतः ।
इला पुत्रत्रयं लेभे पुनः स्त्रीत्वमविन्दत ॥
1.19.m: Having attained pure manhood, renowned as Sudyumna, / [and having] fathered three sons, Ilā obtained womanhood once again:

1.19.s:
utkalaśca gayaścaiva vinatāśvastathaiva ca /
sarve te 'pratimaprakhyāḥ prapannāḥ kamalodbhavam //
1.19.d:
उत्कलश्च गयश्चैव विनताश्वस्तथैव च ।
सर्वे ते ऽप्रतिमप्रख्याः प्रपन्नाः कमलोद्भवम् ॥
1.19.m: Utkala, Gaya, and Vinatāśva; / all of them, renowned as matchless, took refuge in the lotus-born [Brahmā].

1.19.s:
ikṣvākoścābhavad vīro vikukṣirnāma pārthivaḥ /
jyeṣṭhaḥ putraśatasyāpi daśa pañca ca tatsutāḥ //
1.19.d:
इक्ष्वाकोश्चाभवद् वीरो विकुक्षिर्नाम पार्थिवः ।
ज्येष्ठः पुत्रशतस्यापि दश पञ्च च तत्सुताः ॥
1.19.m: And to Ikṣvāku was born a heroic king named Vikukṣi, / the eldest even of a hundred sons; and his sons were fifteen.

1.19.s:
teṣāñjyeṣṭhaḥ kakutstho 'bhūt kākutstho hi suyodhanaḥ /
suyodhanāt pṛthuḥ śrīmān viśvakaśca pṛthoḥ sutaḥ //
1.19.d:
तेषाञ्ज्येष्ठः ककुत्स्थो ऽभूत् काकुत्स्थो हि सुयोधनः ।
सुयोधनात् पृथुः श्रीमान् विश्वकश्च पृथोः सुतः ॥
1.19.m: The eldest among them was Kakutstha; the descendant of Kakutstha was Suyodhana; / from Suyodhana came glorious Pṛthu, and Viśvaka was the son of Pṛthu;

1.19.s:
viśvakādārdrako dhīmān yuvanāśvastu tatsutaḥ /
sa gokarṇamanuprāpya yuvanāśvaḥ pratāpavān //
1.19.d:
विश्वकादार्द्रको धीमान् युवनाश्वस्तु तत्सुतः ।
स गोकर्णमनुप्राप्य युवनाश्वः प्रतापवान् ॥
1.19.m: from Viśvaka came wise Ārdraka, and Yuvanāśva was his son. / That majestic Yuvanāśva, having reached Gokarṇa,

1.19.s:
dṛṣṭvā tu gautamaṃ vipraṃ tapantamanalaprabham /
praṇamya daṇḍavad bhūmau putrakāmo mahīpatiḥ /
apṛcchat karmaṇā kena dhārmikaṃ prāpnuyāt sutam //
1.19.d:
दृष्ट्वा तु गौतमं विप्रं तपन्तमनलप्रभम् ।
प्रणम्य दण्डवद् भूमौ पुत्रकामो महीपतिः ।
अपृच्छत् कर्मणा केन धार्मिकं प्राप्नुयात् सुतम् ॥
1.19.m: and having seen the brāhmaṇa Gautama blazing with the lustre of fire, / bowed down like a staff upon the ground, desirous of a son, the lord of the earth, / and asked by what action he might obtain a righteous son.

1.19.s:
gautama uvāca
ārādhya pūrvapuruṣaṃ nārāyaṇamanāmayam /
anādinidhanaṃ devaṃ dhārmikaṃ prāpnuyāt sutam //
1.19.d:
गौतम उवाच
आराध्य पूर्वपुरुषं नारायणमनामयम् ।
अनादिनिधनं देवं धार्मिकं प्राप्नुयात् सुतम् ॥
1.19.m: Gautama said: / By worshipping the Primal Spirit, Nārāyaṇa free from affliction, / the god without beginning or end, one may obtain a righteous son.

1.19.s:
yasya putraḥ svayaṃ brahmā pautraḥ syānnīlalohitaḥ /
tamādikṛṣṇamīśānamārādhyāpnoti satsutam //
1.19.d:
यस्य पुत्रः स्वयं ब्रह्मा पौत्रः स्यान्नीललोहितः ।
तमादिकृष्णमीशानमाराध्याप्नोति सत्सुतम् ॥
1.19.m: He whose son is Brahmā himself, and whose grandson is Nīlalohita— / by worshipping him, the primal Kṛṣṇa, the Lord, one obtains a good son.

1.19.s:
na yasya bhagavān brahmā prabhāvaṃ vetti tattvataḥ /
tamārādhya hṛṣīkeśaṃ prāpnuyāddhārmikaṃ sutam //
1.19.d:
न यस्य भगवान् ब्रह्मा प्रभावं वेत्ति तत्त्वतः ।
तमाराध्य हृषीकेशं प्राप्नुयाद्धार्मिकं सुतम् ॥
1.19.m: He whose majesty the blessed Brahmā does not know in its true nature— / by worshipping that Hṛṣīkeśa, one may obtain a righteous son.

1.19.s:
sa gautamavacaḥ śrutvā yuvanāśvo mahīpatiḥ /
ārādhayanmahāyogaṃ vāsudevaṃ sanātanam //
1.19.d:
स गौतमवचः श्रुत्वा युवनाश्वो महीपतिः ।
आराधयन्महायोगं वासुदेवं सनातनम् ॥
1.19.m: Hearing that speech of Gautama, King Yuvanāśva / worshipped Vāsudeva, the eternal master of great yoga.

1.19.s:
tasya putro 'bhavad vīraḥ śrāvastiriti viśrutaḥ /
nirmitā yena śrāvastirgauḍadeśe mahāpurī //
1.19.d:
तस्य पुत्रो ऽभवद् वीरः श्रावस्तिरिति विश्रुतः ।
निर्मिता येन श्रावस्तिर्गौडदेशे महापुरी ॥
1.19.m: His son was the hero renowned as Śrāvasti, / by whom the great city Śrāvastī was built in the Gauḍa country.

1.19.s:
tasmācca bṛhadaśvo 'bhūt tasmāt kuvalayāśvakaḥ /
dhundhumāratvamagamad dhundhuṃ hatvā mahāsuram //
1.19.d:
तस्माच्च बृहदश्वो ऽभूत् तस्मात् कुवलयाश्वकः ।
धुन्धुमारत्वमगमद् धुन्धुं हत्वा महासुरम् ॥
1.19.m: And from him came Bṛhadaśva; from him came Kuvalayāśva; / he attained the status of Dhundhumāra after slaying the great asura Dhundhu.

1.19.s:
dhundhumārasya tanayāstrayaḥ proktā dvijottamāḥ /
dṛḍhāśvaścaiva daṇḍāśvaḥ kapilāśvastathaiva ca //
1.19.d:
धुन्धुमारस्य तनयास्त्रयः प्रोक्ता द्विजोत्तमाः ।
दृढाश्वश्चैव दण्डाश्वः कपिलाश्वस्तथैव च ॥
1.19.m: Three sons of Dhundhumāra are proclaimed, O best of the twice-born: / Dṛḍhāśva, Daṇḍāśva, and Kapilāśva.

1.19.s:
dṛḍhāśvasya pramodastu haryaśvastasya cātmajaḥ /
haryaśvasya nikumbhastu nikumbhāt saṃhatāśvakaḥ //
1.19.d:
दृढाश्वस्य प्रमोदस्तु हर्यश्वस्तस्य चात्मजः ।
हर्यश्वस्य निकुम्भस्तु निकुम्भात् संहताश्वकः ॥
1.19.m: The son of Dṛḍhāśva was Pramoda, and Haryaśva was his son; / the son of Haryaśva was Nikumbha, and from Nikumbha came Saṃhatāśva;

1.19.s:
kṛśāśvaśca raṇāśvaśca saṃhatāśvasya vai sutau /
yuvanāśvo raṇāśvasya śakratulyabalo yudhi //
1.19.d:
कृशाश्वश्च रणाश्वश्च संहताश्वस्य वै सुतौ ।
युवनाश्वो रणाश्वस्य शक्रतुल्यबलो युधि ॥
1.19.m: Kṛśāśva and Raṇāśva were indeed the two sons of Saṃhatāśva; / the son of Raṇāśva was Yuvanāśva, equal in strength to Indra in battle.

1.19.s:
kṛtvā tu vāruṇīmiṣṭimṛṣīṇāṃ vai prasādataḥ /
lebhe tvapratimaṃ putraṃ viṣṇubhaktamanuttamam /
māndhātāraṃ mahāprājñaṃ sarvaśastrabhṛtāṃ varam //
1.19.d:
कृत्वा तु वारुणीमिष्टिमृषीणां वै प्रसादतः ।
लेभे त्वप्रतिमं पुत्रं विष्णुभक्तमनुत्तमम् ।
मान्धातारं महाप्राज्ञं सर्वशस्त्रभृतां वरम् ॥
1.19.m: Having performed a sacrifice to Varuṇa, through the grace of the sages, / he obtained a matchless son, an unsurpassed devotee of Viṣṇu, / Māndhātṛ, of great wisdom, the foremost of all bearers of weapons.

1.19.s:
māndhātuḥ purukutso 'bhūdambarīṣaśca vīryavān /
mucukundaśca puṇyātmā sarve śakrasamā yudhi //
1.19.d:
मान्धातुः पुरुकुत्सो ऽभूदम्बरीषश्च वीर्यवान् ।
मुचुकुन्दश्च पुण्यात्मा सर्वे शक्रसमा युधि ॥
1.19.m: To Māndhātṛ were born Purukutsa, and powerful Ambarīṣa, / and the virtuous-souled Mucukunda; all were equal to Indra in battle.

1.19.s:
ambarīṣasya dāyādo yuvanāśvo 'paraḥ smṛtaḥ /
harito yuvanāśvasya hāritastatsuto 'bhavat //
1.19.d:
अम्बरीषस्य दायादो युवनाश्वो ऽपरः स्मृतः ।
हरितो युवनाश्वस्य हारितस्तत्सुतो ऽभवत् ॥
1.19.m: The heir of Ambarīṣa is remembered as another Yuvanāśva; / the son of Yuvanāśva was Harita, and his son was Hārita.

1.19.s:
purukutsasya dāyādastrasadasyurmahāyaśāḥ /
narmadāyāṃ samutpannaḥ saṃbhūtistatsuto 'bhavat //
1.19.d:
पुरुकुत्सस्य दायादस्त्रसदस्युर्महायशाः ।
नर्मदायां समुत्पन्नः संभूतिस्तत्सुतो ऽभवत् ॥
1.19.m: The heir of Purukutsa was the illustrious Trasadasyu, / born of Narmadā; Saṃbhūti was his son;

1.19.s:
viṣṇuvṛddhaḥ sutastasya tvanaraṇyo 'bhavat paraḥ /
bṛhadaśavo 'naraṇyasya haryaśvastatsuto 'bhavat //
1.19.d:
विष्णुवृद्धः सुतस्तस्य त्वनरण्यो ऽभवत् परः ।
बृहदशवो ऽनरण्यस्य हर्यश्वस्तत्सुतो ऽभवत् ॥
1.19.m: Viṣṇuvṛddha was his son, and another was Anaraṇya; / the son of Anaraṇya was Bṛhadaśva, and Haryaśva was his son.

1.19.s:
so 'tīva dhārmiko rājā kardamasya prajāpateḥ /
prasādāddhārmikaṃ putraṃ lebhe sūryaparāyaṇam //
1.19.d:
सो ऽतीव धार्मिको राजा कर्दमस्य प्रजापतेः ।
प्रसादाद्धार्मिकं पुत्रं लेभे सूर्यपरायणम् ॥
1.19.m: That exceedingly righteous king, through the grace / of the Prajāpati Kardama, obtained a righteous son devoted to the sun.

1.19.s:
sa tu sūryaṃ samabhyarcya rājā vasumanāḥ śubham /
lebhe tvapratimaṃ putraṃ tridhanvānamarindamam //
1.19.d:
स तु सूर्यं समभ्यर्च्य राजा वसुमनाः शुभम् ।
लेभे त्वप्रतिमं पुत्रं त्रिधन्वानमरिन्दमम् ॥
1.19.m: Having worshipped the auspicious sun, King Vasumanas / obtained an incomparable son, Tridhanvan, subduer of enemies.

1.19.s:
ayajaccāśvamedhena śatrūn jitvā dvijottamāḥ /
svādhyāyavān dānaśīlastitikṣurdharmatatparaḥ //
1.19.d:
अयजच्चाश्वमेधेन शत्रून् जित्वा द्विजोत्तमाः ।
स्वाध्यायवान् दानशीलस्तितिक्षुर्धर्मतत्परः ॥
1.19.m: He sacrificed with the horse sacrifice, having conquered his enemies, O best of the twice-born; / he was devoted to Vedic study, generous, forbearing, and intent upon righteousness.

1.19.s:
ṛṣayastu samājagmuryajñavāṭaṃ mahātmanaḥ /
vasiṣṭhakaśyapamukhā devāścendrapurogamāḥ //
1.19.d:
ऋषयस्तु समाजग्मुर्यज्ञवाटं महात्मनः ।
वसिष्ठकश्यपमुखा देवाश्चेन्द्रपुरोगमाः ॥
1.19.m: The sages assembled at the sacrificial enclosure of that great-souled one, / headed by Vasiṣṭha and Kaśyapa, and the gods headed by Indra.

1.19.s:
tān praṇamya mahārājaḥ papraccha vinayānvitaḥ /
samāpya vidhivad yajñaṃ vasiṣṭhādīn dvijottamān //
1.19.d:
तान् प्रणम्य महाराजः पप्रच्छ विनयान्वितः ।
समाप्य विधिवद् यज्ञं वसिष्ठादीन् द्विजोत्तमान् ॥
1.19.m: Having bowed to them, the great king, filled with humility, / having duly concluded the sacrifice, questioned Vasiṣṭha and the other best of the twice-born:

1.19.s:
vasumanā uvāca
kiṃsviccheyaskarataraṃ loke 'smin brāhmaṇarṣabhāḥ /
yajñastapo vā saṃnyāso brūta me sarvavedinaḥ //
1.19.d:
वसुमना उवाच
किंस्विच्छेयस्करतरं लोके ऽस्मिन् ब्राह्मणर्षभाः ।
यज्ञस्तपो वा संन्यासो ब्रूत मे सर्ववेदिनः ॥
1.19.m: Vasumanas said: / What is more conducive to the highest good in this world, O bulls among brāhmaṇas— / sacrifice, austerity, or renunciation? Tell me, you who know all.

1.19.s:
vasiṣṭha uvāca
adhītya vedān vidhivat putrānutpādya dharmataḥ /
iṣṭvā yajñeśvaraṃ yajñair gaccheda vanamathātmavān //
1.19.d:
वसिष्ठ उवाच
अधीत्य वेदान् विधिवत् पुत्रानुत्पाद्य धर्मतः ।
इष्ट्वा यज्ञेश्वरं यज्ञैर् गच्छेद वनमथात्मवान् ॥
1.19.m: Vasiṣṭha said: / Having studied the Vedas according to rule, having produced sons according to righteousness, / having worshipped the Lord of sacrifice with sacrifices, the self-controlled man may then go to the forest.

1.19.s:
pulastya uvāca
ārādhya tapasā devaṃ yoginaṃ parameṣṭhinam /
pravrajed vidhivad yajñairiṣṭvā pūrvaṃ surottamān //
1.19.d:
पुलस्त्य उवाच
आराध्य तपसा देवं योगिनं परमेष्ठिनम् ।
प्रव्रजेद् विधिवद् यज्ञैरिष्ट्वा पूर्वं सुरोत्तमान् ॥
1.19.m: Pulastya said: / Having worshipped through austerity the divine yogin, the Supreme Being, / one should go forth into homelessness according to rule, having first worshipped the foremost gods with sacrifices.

1.19.s:
pulaha uvāca
yamāhurekaṃ puruṣaṃ purāṇaṃ parameśvaram /
tamārādhya sahastrāṃśuṃ tapasā mokṣamāpnuyāt //
1.19.d:
पुलह उवाच
यमाहुरेकं पुरुषं पुराणं परमेश्वरम् ।
तमाराध्य सहस्त्रांशुं तपसा मोक्षमाप्नुयात् ॥
1.19.m: Pulaha said: / He whom they call the one ancient Spirit, the Supreme Lord— / by worshipping that thousand-rayed one through austerity, one may attain liberation.

1.19.s:
jamadagniruvāca
ajasya nābhāvadhyekamīśvareṇa samarpitam /
bījaṃ bhagavatā yena sa devastapasejyate //
1.19.d:
जमदग्निरुवाच
अजस्य नाभावध्येकमीश्वरेण समर्पितम् ।
बीजं भगवता येन स देवस्तपसेज्यते ॥
1.19.m: Jamadagni said: / In the navel of the Unborn, a single seed was deposited by the Lord, / by which blessed one [it was placed]—that god is worshipped through austerity.

1.19.s:
viśvāmitra uvāca
yo 'gniḥ sarvātmako 'nantaḥ svayaṃbhūrviśvatomukhaḥ /
sa rudrastapasogreṇa pūjyate netarairmakhaiḥ //
1.19.d:
विश्वामित्र उवाच
यो ऽग्निः सर्वात्मको ऽनन्तः स्वयंभूर्विश्वतोमुखः ।
स रुद्रस्तपसोग्रेण पूज्यते नेतरैर्मखैः ॥
1.19.m: Viśvāmitra said: / The fire which consists of all, infinite, self-existent, facing in all directions— / that Rudra is worshipped through fierce austerity, not by other sacrifices.

1.19.s:
bharadvāja uvāca
yo yajñairijyate devo jātavedāḥ sanātanaḥ /
sa sarvadaivatatanuḥ pūjyate tapaseśvaraḥ //
1.19.d:
भरद्वाज उवाच
यो यज्ञैरिज्यते देवो जातवेदाः सनातनः ।
स सर्वदैवततनुः पूज्यते तपसेश्वरः ॥
1.19.m: Bharadvāja said: / The god who is worshipped through sacrifices, the eternal knower of all beings, / he whose body is all the deities, the Lord, is worshipped through austerity.

1.19.s:
atriruvāca
yataḥ sarvamidaṃ jātaṃ yasyāpatyaṃ prajāpatiḥ /
tapaḥ sumahadāsthāya pūjyate sa maheśvaraḥ //
1.19.d:
अत्रिरुवाच
यतः सर्वमिदं जातं यस्यापत्यं प्रजापतिः ।
तपः सुमहदास्थाय पूज्यते स महेश्वरः ॥
1.19.m: Atri said: / From whom all this arose, whose offspring is Prajāpati— / undertaking immense austerity, that Maheśvara is worshipped.

1.19.s:
gautama uvāca
yataḥ pradhānapuruṣau yasya śaktimayaṃ jagat /
sa devadevastapasā pūjanīyaḥ sanātanaḥ //
1.19.d:
गौतम उवाच
यतः प्रधानपुरुषौ यस्य शक्तिमयं जगत् ।
स देवदेवस्तपसा पूजनीयः सनातनः ॥
1.19.m: Gautama said: / From whom primary matter and spirit arise, of whose power the universe consists— / that eternal God of gods is to be worshipped through austerity.

1.19.s:
kaśyapa uvāca
sahastranayano devaḥ sākṣī sa tu prajāpatiḥ /
prasīdati mahāyogī pūjitastapasā paraḥ //
1.19.d:
कश्यप उवाच
सहस्त्रनयनो देवः साक्षी स तु प्रजापतिः ।
प्रसीदति महायोगी पूजितस्तपसा परः ॥
1.19.m: Kaśyapa said: / The thousand-eyed god, the witness, he who is Prajāpati, / the supreme great yogin, when worshipped through austerity, becomes pleased.

1.19.s:
kraturuvāca
prāptādhyayanayajñas labdhaputrasya caiva hi /
nāntareṇa tapaḥ kaściddharmaḥ śāstreṣu dṛśyate //
1.19.d:
क्रतुरुवाच
प्राप्ताध्ययनयज्ञस् लब्धपुत्रस्य चैव हि ।
नान्तरेण तपः कश्चिद्धर्मः शास्त्रेषु दृश्यते ॥
1.19.m: Kratu said: / For one who has accomplished study and sacrifice and has obtained a son, / no duty is seen in the scriptures apart from austerity.

1.19.s:
ityākarṇya sa rājarṣistān praṇamyātihṛṣṭadhīḥ /
visarjayitvā saṃpūjya tridhanvānamathābravīt //
1.19.d:
इत्याकर्ण्य स राजर्षिस्तान् प्रणम्यातिहृष्टधीः ।
विसर्जयित्वा संपूज्य त्रिधन्वानमथाब्रवीत् ॥
1.19.m: Hearing this, that royal sage bowed to them with an exceedingly joyful mind; / having worshipped and dismissed them, he then spoke to Tridhanvan:

1.19.s:
ārādhayiṣye tapasā devamekākṣarāhvayam /
prāṇaṃ bṛhantaṃ puruṣamādityāntarasaṃsthitam //
1.19.d:
आराधयिष्ये तपसा देवमेकाक्षराह्वयम् ।
प्राणं बृहन्तं पुरुषमादित्यान्तरसंस्थितम् ॥
1.19.m: I shall worship through austerity the god whose name is the single syllable, / the breath of life, the immense Spirit situated within the sun.

1.19.s:
tvaṃ tu dharmarato nityaṃ pālayaitadatandritaḥ /
cāturvarṇyasamāyuktamaśeṣaṃ kṣitimaṇḍalam //
1.19.d:
त्वं तु धर्मरतो नित्यं पालयैतदतन्द्रितः ।
चातुर्वर्ण्यसमायुक्तमशेषं क्षितिमण्डलम् ॥
1.19.m: "You, however, always devoted to righteousness, unflaggingly protect / this entire circle of the earth comprising the four classes."

1.19.s:
evamuktvā sa tadrājyaṃ nidhāyātmabhave nṛpaḥ /
jagāmāraṇyamanaghastapaścartumanuttamam //
1.19.d:
एवमुक्त्वा स तद्राज्यं निधायात्मभवे नृपः ।
जगामारण्यमनघस्तपश्चर्तुमनुत्तमम् ॥
1.19.m: Having spoken thus and placed that kingdom upon his own son, the faultless king / went to the forest to perform unsurpassed asceticism.

1.19.s:
himavacchikhare ramye devadāruvane śubhe /
kandamūlaphalāhāro munyannairayajat surān //
1.19.d:
हिमवच्छिखरे रम्ये देवदारुवने शुभे ।
कन्दमूलफलाहारो मुन्यन्नैरयजत् सुरान् ॥
1.19.m: On a delightful peak of the Himālaya, in an auspicious cedar forest, / subsisting on roots, tubers, and fruits, he worshipped the gods with the food of sages.

1.19.s:
saṃvatsaraśataṃ sāgraṃ taponirdhūtakalmaṣaḥ /
jajāpa manasā devīṃ sāvitrariṃ vedamātaram //
1.19.d:
संवत्सरशतं साग्रं तपोनिर्धूतकल्मषः ।
जजाप मनसा देवीं सावित्ररिं वेदमातरम् ॥
1.19.m: For over a full hundred years, his sins shaken off by asceticism, / he mentally recited the goddess Sāvitrī, the mother of the Vedas.

1.19.s:
tasyaivaṃ japato devaḥ svayaṃbhūḥ parameśvaraḥ /
hiraṇyagarbho viśvātmā taṃ deśamagamat svayam //
1.19.d:
तस्यैवं जपतो देवः स्वयंभूः परमेश्वरः ।
हिरण्यगर्भो विश्वात्मा तं देशमगमत् स्वयम् ॥
1.19.m: While he was thus reciting, the self-existent god, the supreme lord, / Hiraṇyagarbha, the soul of all, went to that region in person.

1.19.s:
dṛṣṭvā devaṃ samāyāntaṃ brahmāṇaṃ viśvatomukham /
nanāma śirasā tasya pādayornāma kīrtayan //
1.19.d:
दृष्ट्वा देवं समायान्तं ब्रह्माणं विश्वतोमुखम् ।
ननाम शिरसा तस्य पादयोर्नाम कीर्तयन् ॥
1.19.m: Seeing the god Brahmā, whose faces are everywhere, approaching, / he bowed his head at his feet, praising his name:

1.19.s:
namo devādhidevāya brahmaṇe paramātmane /
hirṇyamūrtaye tubhyaṃ sahastrākṣāya vedhase //
1.19.d:
नमो देवाधिदेवाय ब्रह्मणे परमात्मने ।
हिर्ण्यमूर्तये तुभ्यं सहस्त्राक्षाय वेधसे ॥
1.19.m: "Salutations to the supreme God of gods, to Brahman, the supreme soul, / to you whose form is golden, who are thousand-eyed, the creator!

1.19.s:
namo dhātre vidhātre ca namo vedātmamūrtaye /
sāṃkhyayogādhigamyāya namaste jñānamūrtaye //
1.19.d:
नमो धात्रे विधात्रे च नमो वेदात्ममूर्तये ।
सांख्ययोगाधिगम्याय नमस्ते ज्ञानमूर्तये ॥
1.19.m: "Salutations to the supporter and the ordainer, salutations to the embodiment of the Vedas, / attainable through Sāṅkhya and Yoga, salutations to you whose form is knowledge!

1.19.s:
namastrimūrtaye tubhyaṃ straṣṭre sarvārthavedine /
puruṣāya purāṇāya yogināṃ gurave namaḥ //
1.19.d:
नमस्त्रिमूर्तये तुभ्यं स्त्रष्ट्रे सर्वार्थवेदिने ।
पुरुषाय पुराणाय योगिनां गुरवे नमः ॥
1.19.m: "Salutations to you of threefold form, the creator, knower of all aims, / to the ancient Puruṣa, salutations to the preceptor of yogins!"

1.19.s:
tataḥ prasanno bhagavān viriñco viśvabhāvanaḥ /
varaṃ varaya bhadraṃ te varado 'smītyabhāṣata //
1.19.d:
ततः प्रसन्नो भगवान् विरिञ्चो विश्वभावनः ।
वरं वरय भद्रं ते वरदो ऽस्मीत्यभाषत ॥
1.19.m: Then, pleased, the blessed Viriñca, creator of the universe, / said: "Choose a boon, blessings to you, I am a grantor of boons."

1.19.s:
rājovāca
japeyaṃ devadeveśa gāyatrīṃ vedamātaram /
bhūyo varṣaśataṃ sāgraṃ tāvadāyurbhavenmama //
1.19.d:
राजोवाच
जपेयं देवदेवेश गायत्रीं वेदमातरम् ।
भूयो वर्षशतं साग्रं तावदायुर्भवेन्मम ॥
1.19.m:
The king said:
"O Lord of the gods of gods, may I recite the Gāyatrī, the mother of the Vedas, / for over another hundred years; may my lifespan be that long."

1.19.s:
bāḍhamityāha viśvātmā samālokya narādhipam /
spṛṣṭvā karābhyāṃ suprītastatraivāntaradhīyata //
1.19.d:
बाढमित्याह विश्वात्मा समालोक्य नराधिपम् ।
स्पृष्ट्वा कराभ्यां सुप्रीतस्तत्रैवान्तरधीयत ॥
1.19.m: "So be it," said the soul of all, looking upon the ruler of men; / well pleased, having touched him with both hands, he vanished right there.

1.19.s:
so 'pi labdhavaraḥ śrīmān jajāpātiprasannadhīḥ /
śāntastriṣavaṇasnāyī kandamūlaphalāśanaḥ //
1.19.d:
सो ऽपि लब्धवरः श्रीमान् जजापातिप्रसन्नधीः ।
शान्तस्त्रिषवणस्नायी कन्दमूलफलाशनः ॥
1.19.m: Having obtained the boon, the glorious [king], his mind exceedingly clear, / tranquil, bathing at the three junctures of the day, eating roots, tubers, and fruits, recited.

1.19.s:
tasya pūrṇe varṣaśate bhagavānugradīdhitiḥ /
prādurāsīnmahāyogī bhānormaṇḍalamadhyataḥ //
1.19.d:
तस्य पूर्णे वर्षशते भगवानुग्रदीधितिः ।
प्रादुरासीन्महायोगी भानोर्मण्डलमध्यतः ॥
1.19.m: When his hundred years were complete, the blessed one of fierce rays, / the great yogin, became manifest from the center of the sun's orb.

1.19.s:
taṃ dṛṣṭvā vedaviduṣaṃ maṇḍalasthaṃ sanātanam /
svayaṃbhuvamanādyantaṃ brahmāṇaṃ vismayaṃ gataḥ //
1.19.d:
तं दृष्ट्वा वेदविदुषं मण्डलस्थं सनातनम् ।
स्वयंभुवमनाद्यन्तं ब्रह्माणं विस्मयं गतः ॥
1.19.m: Seeing that eternal one, who knows the Vedas, situated in the orb, / the self-existent, beginningless and endless Brahmā, he was filled with amazement.

1.19.s:
tuṣṭāva vaidikairmantraiḥ sāvitryā ca viśeṣataḥ /
kṣaṇādapaśyat puruṣaṃ tameva parameśvaram //
1.19.d:
तुष्टाव वैदिकैर्मन्त्रैः सावित्र्या च विशेषतः ।
क्षणादपश्यत् पुरुषं तमेव परमेश्वरम् ॥
1.19.m: He praised [him] with Vedic mantras and especially with the Sāvitrī; / in a moment he saw that very supreme lord as a Puruṣa,

1.19.s:
caturmukhaṃ jaṭāmaulimaṣṭahastaṃ trilocanam /
candrāvayavalakṣamāṇaṃ naranārītanuṃ haram //
1.19.d:
चतुर्मुखं जटामौलिमष्टहस्तं त्रिलोचनम् ।
चन्द्रावयवलक्षमाणं नरनारीतनुं हरम् ॥
1.19.m: four-faced, with a crown of matted locks, eight-armed, three-eyed, / bearing the crescent moon, Hara whose body is man and woman,

1.19.s:
bhāsayantaṃ jagat kṛtsnaṃ nīlakaṇṭhaṃ svaraśmibhiḥ /
raktāmbaradharaṃ raktaṃ raktamālyānulepanam //
1.19.d:
भासयन्तं जगत् कृत्स्नं नीलकण्ठं स्वरश्मिभिः ।
रक्ताम्बरधरं रक्तं रक्तमाल्यानुलेपनम् ॥
1.19.m: illuminating the entire universe with his rays, the blue-throated one, / wearing red garments, red, with red garlands and ointments.

1.19.s:
tadbhāvabhāvito dṛṣṭvā sadbhāvena pareṇa hi /
nanāma śirasā rudraṃ sāvitryānena caiva hi //
1.19.d:
तद्भावभावितो दृष्ट्वा सद्भावेन परेण हि ।
ननाम शिरसा रुद्रं सावित्र्यानेन चैव हि ॥
1.19.m: Pervaded by devotion to him upon seeing him with supreme genuine faith, / he bowed his head to Rudra and recited this Sāvitrī:

1.19.s:
namaste nīlakaṇṭhāya bhāsvate parameṣṭhine /
trayīmayāya rudrāya kālarūpāya hetave //
1.19.d:
नमस्ते नीलकण्ठाय भास्वते परमेष्ठिने ।
त्रयीमयाय रुद्राय कालरूपाय हेतवे ॥
1.19.m: "Salutations to you, the blue-throated one, the radiant Parameṣṭhin, / Rudra composed of the three Vedas, the cause whose form is Time."

1.19.s:
tadā prāha mahādevo rājānaṃ prītamānasaḥ /
imāni me rahasyāni nāmāni śṛṇu cānagha //
1.19.d:
तदा प्राह महादेवो राजानं प्रीतमानसः ।
इमानि मे रहस्यानि नामानि शृणु चानघ ॥
1.19.m: Then Mahādeva, his mind pleased, said to the king: / "Hear these secret names of mine, O sinless one,

1.19.s:
sarvavedeṣu gītāni saṃsāraśamanāni tu /
namaskuruṣva nṛpate ebhirmāṃ satataṃ śuciḥ //
1.19.d:
सर्ववेदेषु गीतानि संसारशमनानि तु ।
नमस्कुरुष्व नृपते एभिर्मां सततं शुचिः ॥
1.19.m: "praised in all the Vedas and bringing an end to worldly existence; / bow down to me constantly with these, O ruler of men, being pure.

1.19.s:
adhyāyaṃ śatarudrīyaṃ yajuṣāṃ sāramuddhṛtam /
japasvānanyacetasko mayyāsaktamanā nṛpa //
1.19.d:
अध्यायं शतरुद्रीयं यजुषां सारमुद्धृतम् ।
जपस्वानन्यचेतस्को मय्यासक्तमना नृप ॥
1.19.m: "The Śatarudrīya hymn, extracted as the essence of the Yajus formulas, / recite with a single-pointed mind, your heart attached to me, O king.

1.19.s:
brahmacārī mitāhāro bhasmaniṣṭhaḥ samāhitaḥ /
japedāmaraṇād rudraṃ sa yāti paramaṃ padam //
1.19.d:
ब्रह्मचारी मिताहारो भस्मनिष्ठः समाहितः ।
जपेदामरणाद् रुद्रं स याति परमं पदम् ॥
1.19.m: "Chaste, eating moderately, dedicated to [wearing] sacred ashes, concentrated, / whoever recites the Rudra [hymn] until death goes to the supreme state."

1.19.s:
ityuktvā bhagavān rudro bhaktānugrahakāmyayā /
punaḥ saṃvatsaraśataṃ rājñe hyāyurakalpayat //
1.19.d:
इत्युक्त्वा भगवान् रुद्रो भक्तानुग्रहकाम्यया ।
पुनः संवत्सरशतं राज्ञे ह्यायुरकल्पयत् ॥
1.19.m: Having spoken thus, the blessed Rudra, wishing to show grace to his devotee, / granted the king a lifespan of another hundred years.

1.19.s:
dattvāsmai tat paraṃ jñānaṃ vairāgyaṃ parameśvaraḥ /
kṣaṇādantardadhe rudrastadadbhutamivābhavat //
1.19.d:
दत्त्वास्मै तत् परं ज्ञानं वैराग्यं परमेश्वरः ।
क्षणादन्तर्दधे रुद्रस्तदद्भुतमिवाभवत् ॥
1.19.m: Having bestowed that supreme knowledge and detachment upon him, the supreme lord / Rudra vanished in an instant; that was indeed wondrous.

1.19.s:
rājāpi tapasā rudraṃ jajāpānanyamānasaḥ /
bhasmacchannastriṣavaṇaṃ snātvā śāntaḥ samāhitaḥ //
1.19.d:
राजापि तपसा रुद्रं जजापानन्यमानसः ।
भस्मच्छन्नस्त्रिषवणं स्नात्वा शान्तः समाहितः ॥
1.19.m: The king too recited the Rudra [hymn] with asceticism, his mind on no other, / covered in ashes, having bathed at the three junctures of the day, tranquil, concentrated.

1.19.s:
japatastasya nṛpateḥ pūrṇe varṣaśate punaḥ /
yogapravṛttirabhavat kālāt kālātmakaṃ param //
1.19.d:
जपतस्तस्य नृपतेः पूर्णे वर्षशते पुनः ।
योगप्रवृत्तिरभवत् कालात् कालात्मकं परम् ॥
1.19.m: As that king was reciting, when another hundred years had passed, / an engagement in yoga arose from [his master of] time, the supreme one whose nature is Time.

1.19.s:
viveśa tad vedasāraṃ sthānaṃ vai parameṣṭhinaḥ /
bhānoḥ sa maṇḍalaṃ śubhraṃ tato yāto maheśvaram //
1.19.d:
विवेश तद् वेदसारं स्थानं वै परमेष्ठिनः ।
भानोः स मण्डलं शुभ्रं ततो यातो महेश्वरम् ॥
1.19.m: He entered that abode of Parameṣṭhin, the essence of the Vedas, / the bright orb of the sun, and from there he went to Maheśvara.

1.19.s:
yaḥ paṭhecchṛṇuyād vāpi rājñaścaritamuttamam /
sarvapāpavinirmukto brahmaloke mahīyate //
iti śrīkūrmapurāṇe ṣaṭsāhastryāṃ saṃhitāyāṃ pūrvavibhāge ekonaviśo 'dhyāyaḥ
1.19.d:
यः पठेच्छृणुयाद् वापि राज्ञश्चरितमुत्तमम् ।
सर्वपापविनिर्मुक्तो ब्रह्मलोके महीयते ॥
इति श्रीकूर्मपुराणे षट्साहस्त्र्यां संहितायां पूर्वविभागे एकोनविशो ऽध्यायः
1.19.m:
Whoever reads or hears the excellent conduct of this king, / freed from all sins, is honored in the world of Brahmā.

Thus ends the nineteenth chapter in the former section of the compilation of six thousand verses in the glorious Kūrma Purāṇa.

1.20.s:
sūta uvāca
tridhanvā rājaputrastu dharmeṇāpālayanmahīm /
tasya putro 'bhavad vidvāṃstrayyāruṇa iti smṛtaḥ //
1.20.d:
सूत उवाच
त्रिधन्वा राजपुत्रस्तु धर्मेणापालयन्महीम् ।
तस्य पुत्रो ऽभवद् विद्वांस्त्रय्यारुण इति स्मृतः ॥
1.20.m:
Sūta said:
And the prince Tridhanvan ruled the earth with righteousness; / his son was the learned one known as Trayyāruṇa.

1.20.s:
tasya satyavrato nāma kumāro 'bhūnmahābalaḥ /
bhāryā satyadhanā nāma hariścandramajījanat //
1.20.d:
तस्य सत्यव्रतो नाम कुमारो ऽभून्महाबलः ।
भार्या सत्यधना नाम हरिश्चन्द्रमजीजनत् ॥
1.20.m: His son was Satyavrata, exceedingly strong; / his wife, named Satyadhanā, gave birth to Hariścandra.

1.20.s:
hariścandrasya putro 'bhūd rohito nāma vīryavān /
harito rohitasyātha dhundhustasya suto 'bhavat //
1.20.d:
हरिश्चन्द्रस्य पुत्रो ऽभूद् रोहितो नाम वीर्यवान् ।
हरितो रोहितस्याथ धुन्धुस्तस्य सुतो ऽभवत् ॥
1.20.m: The son of Hariścandra was the valiant Rohita; / Rohita's son was Harita, and Dhundhu was his son.

1.20.s:
vijayaśca sudevaśca dhundhuputrau babhūvatuḥ /
vijayasyābhavat putraḥ kāruko nāma vīryavān //
1.20.d:
विजयश्च सुदेवश्च धुन्धुपुत्रौ बभूवतुः ।
विजयस्याभवत् पुत्रः कारुको नाम वीर्यवान् ॥
1.20.m: Vijaya and Sudeva were the two sons of Dhundhu; / Vijaya's son was the valiant Kāruka.

1.20.s:
kārukasya vṛkaḥ putrastasmād bāhurajāyata /
sagarastasya putrau'bhūd rājā paramadhārmikaḥ //
1.20.d:
कारुकस्य वृकः पुत्रस्तस्माद् बाहुरजायत ।
सगरस्तस्य पुत्रौऽभूद् राजा परमधार्मिकः ॥
1.20.m: The son of Kāruka was Vṛka; from him Bāhu was born; / Sagara was his son, a most righteous king.

1.20.s:
dve bhārye sagarasyāpi prabhā bhānumatī tathā /
tābhyāmārādhitaḥ prādādaurvāgnirvaramuttamam //
1.20.d:
द्वे भार्ये सगरस्यापि प्रभा भानुमती तथा ।
ताभ्यामाराधितः प्रादादौर्वाग्निर्वरमुत्तमम् ॥
1.20.m: Sagara had two wives: Prabhā and Bhānumatī; / worshipped by both of them, the Aurva fire granted an excellent boon.

1.20.s:
ekaṃ bhānumatī putramagṛhṇādasamañjasam /
prabhā ṣaṣṭisahastraṃ tu putrāṇāṃ jagṛhe śubhā //
1.20.d:
एकं भानुमती पुत्रमगृह्णादसमञ्जसम् ।
प्रभा षष्टिसहस्त्रं तु पुत्राणां जगृहे शुभा ॥
1.20.m: Bhānumatī chose a single son, Asamañjas; / the auspicious Prabhā chose sixty thousand sons.

1.20.s:
asamañsasya tanayo hyaṃśumān nāma pārthivaḥ /
tasya putro dilīpastu dilīpāt tu bhagīrathaḥ //
1.20.d:
असमञ्सस्य तनयो ह्यंशुमान् नाम पार्थिवः ।
तस्य पुत्रो दिलीपस्तु दिलीपात् तु भगीरथः ॥
1.20.m: The son of Asamañjas was the king named Aṃśumat; / his son was Dilīpa, and from Dilīpa [came] Bhagīratha,

1.20.s:
yena bhāgīrathī gaṅgā tapaḥ kṛtvāvatāritā /
prasādād devadevasya mahādevasya dhīmataḥ //
1.20.d:
येन भागीरथी गङ्गा तपः कृत्वावतारिता ।
प्रसादाद् देवदेवस्य महादेवस्य धीमतः ॥
1.20.m: by whom, having performed asceticism, the river Bhāgīrathī Gaṅgā was brought down / through the grace of the wise Mahādeva, the God of gods.

1.20.s:
bhagīrathasya tapasā devaḥ prītamanā haraḥ /
babhāra śirasā gaṅgāṃ somānte somabhūṣaṇaḥ //
1.20.d:
भगीरथस्य तपसा देवः प्रीतमना हरः ।
बभार शिरसा गङ्गां सोमान्ते सोमभूषणः ॥
1.20.m: Pleased in mind by Bhagīratha's asceticism, the god Hara, / adorned with the moon, bore Gaṅgā on his head at the edge of the moon.

1.20.s:
bhagīrathasutaścāpi śruto nāma babhūva ha /
nābhāgastasya dāyādaḥ sindhudvīpastato 'bhavat //
1.20.d:
भगीरथसुतश्चापि श्रुतो नाम बभूव ह ।
नाभागस्तस्य दायादः सिन्धुद्वीपस्ततो ऽभवत् ॥
1.20.m: And the son of Bhagīratha was named Śruta; / his heir was Nābhāga, and from him came Sindhudvīpa.

1.20.s:
ayutāyuḥ sutastasya ṛtuparṇastu tatsutaḥ /
ṛtuparṇasya putro 'bhūt sudāso nāma dhārmikāḥ /
saudāsastasya tanayaḥ khyātaḥ kalmāṣapādakaḥ //
1.20.d:
अयुतायुः सुतस्तस्य ऋतुपर्णस्तु तत्सुतः ।
ऋतुपर्णस्य पुत्रो ऽभूत् सुदासो नाम धार्मिकाः ।
सौदासस्तस्य तनयः ख्यातः कल्माषपादकः ॥
1.20.m: Ayutāyus was his son, and Ṛtuparṇa was his son; / Ṛtuparṇa's son was the righteous Sudāsa; / Saudāsa was his son, famous as Kalmāṣapāda.

1.20.s:
vasiṣṭhastu mahātejāḥ kṣetre kalmāṣapādake /
aśmakaṃ janayāmasā tamikṣvākukuladhvajam //
1.20.d:
वसिष्ठस्तु महातेजाः क्षेत्रे कल्माषपादके ।
अश्मकं जनयामसा तमिक्ष्वाकुकुलध्वजम् ॥
1.20.m: And the exceedingly splendid Vasiṣṭha, in the field of Kalmāṣapāda, / begat Aśmaka, the banner of the Ikṣvāku lineage.

1.20.s:
aśmakasyotkalāyāṃ tu nakulo nāma pārthivaḥ /
sa hi rāmabhayād rājā vanaṃ prāpa suduḥ khitaḥ //
1.20.d:
अश्मकस्योत्कलायां तु नकुलो नाम पार्थिवः ।
स हि रामभयाद् राजा वनं प्राप सुदुः खितः ॥
1.20.m: To Aśmaka, in Utkalā, was born the king named Nakula; / he, in terror of Rāma, went to the forest, deeply sorrowful.

1.20.s:
vibhrat sa nārīkavacaṃ tasmācchataratho 'bhavat /
tasmād bilibiliḥ śrīmānvṛddhaśarmācatatsutaḥ //
1.20.d:
विभ्रत् स नारीकवचं तस्माच्छतरथो ऽभवत् ।
तस्माद् बिलिबिलिः श्रीमान्वृद्धशर्माचतत्सुतः ॥
1.20.m: Wearing a woman's armor, from him was born Śataratha; / from him came the glorious Bilibili, and his son was Vṛddhaśarman.

1.20.s:
tasmād viśvasahastasmāt khaṭvāṅga iti viśrutaḥ /
dīrghabāhuḥ sutastasya raghustasmādajāyata //
1.20.d:
तस्माद् विश्वसहस्तस्मात् खट्वाङ्ग इति विश्रुतः ।
दीर्घबाहुः सुतस्तस्य रघुस्तस्मादजायत ॥
1.20.m: From him came Viśvasaha; from him came the celebrated Khaṭvāṅga; / Dīrghabāhu was his son, and from him Raghu was born.

1.20.s:
raghorajaḥ samutpanno rājā daśarathastataḥ /
rāmo dāśarathirvoro dharmajño lokaviśrutaḥ //
1.20.d:
रघोरजः समुत्पन्नो राजा दशरथस्ततः ।
रामो दाशरथिर्वोरो धर्मज्ञो लोकविश्रुतः ॥
1.20.m: From Raghu, Aja was born, and from him King Daśaratha; / [from him was born] Rāma, the valiant son of Daśaratha, knower of righteousness, renowned throughout the worlds.

1.20.s:
bharato lakṣmaṇaścaiva śatrughnaśca mahābalaḥ /
sarve śakrasamā yuddhe viṣṇuśaktisamanvitāḥ /
jajñe rāvaṇanāśārthaṃ viṣṇuraṃśena viśvakṛt //
1.20.d:
भरतो लक्ष्मणश्चैव शत्रुघ्नश्च महाबलः ।
सर्वे शक्रसमा युद्धे विष्णुशक्तिसमन्विताः ।
जज्ञे रावणनाशार्थं विष्णुरंशेन विश्वकृत् ॥
1.20.m: And Bharata, Lakṣmaṇa, and the mighty Śatrughna— / all were equal to Indra in battle, endowed with the power of Viṣṇu. / Viṣṇu, the creator of all, took birth in a portion [of himself] to destroy Rāvaṇa.

1.20.s:
rāmasya subhagā bhāryā janakasyātmajā śubhā /
sītā trilokavikhyātā śīlaudāryaguṇānvitā //
1.20.d:
रामस्य सुभगा भार्या जनकस्यात्मजा शुभा ।
सीता त्रिलोकविख्याता शीलौदार्यगुणान्विता ॥
1.20.m: Rāma's fortunate and auspicious wife was the daughter of Janaka, / renowned across the three worlds, endowed with good character and nobility.

1.20.s:
tapasā toṣitā devī janakena girīndrajā /
prāyacchajjānakīṃ sītāṃ rāmamevāśritā patim //
1.20.d:
तपसा तोषिता देवी जनकेन गिरीन्द्रजा ।
प्रायच्छज्जानकीं सीतां राममेवाश्रिता पतिम् ॥
1.20.m: Pleased by Janaka's ascetic penance, the goddess, the daughter of the king of mountains, / gave him Jānakī Sītā, who had taken refuge in Rāma alone as her husband.

1.20.s:
